docs.title: Enterprise Scale Azure Factory (ESAF)
docs.text:
Go from an empty Azure subscription to a governed AI Factory, then build agents and ML models in it.

An AI Factory is a production line for AI projects. The platform team builds the line once. Each project team then gets the same secure project: private networking, identities, Microsoft Foundry, Azure AI Search and Azure Machine Learning.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text: Part What it gives you Common part of the Factory One network, the private DNS zones, a data lake, a Key Vault and monitoring, shared by all projects of a scale set. Projects One resource group for each team and environment, with the Azure services that team switches on. Tools The app, the azurefactory CLI, the Python SDK and REST. All four call the same Factory API, so the result is the same. Pipelines Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions run the Bicep templates. You choose one of them when you create the Factory. Code templates Agents, RAG, voice, MCP, machine learning and data examples that run inside a project. See the library. Operations Dashboards, usage and cost reports, and the status of every run. See Monitor and operate.

docs.title: One project, the services you choose
docs.text:
Every project starts from the same template. Each Azure service has its own enable... setting in variables.json, and you switch on what the team needs. The Azure resource library lists them by category, and Every variable in variables.json explains each setting.

Area Services you can switch on AI and agents Microsoft Foundry with its agent service, model deployments, Azure AI Search, Speech, Bot Service Machine learning Azure Machine Learning, Databricks, AKS for online endpoints Full stack Web Apps, Functions, Container Apps, AKS, SQL, PostgreSQL, Cosmos DB, Redis, API Management Data and integration Data Factory, Event Hubs, Logic Apps, the common data lake Private access Private endpoints, private DNS, and a hub with VPN and Bastion. See Hub and network modes.

docs.title: What happens when you switch a service off
docs.text:
Setting a service to "false" stops the pipeline from deploying it. What happens to a resource that already exists depends on one more setting, enableDeleteForDisabledResources.

enableDeleteForDisabledResources A service that is switched off but exists in Azure "false" (the default) Stays as it is. The pipeline leaves every existing resource alone. "true" The next run of the project pipeline deletes it, before it deploys the rest.

With "true" the pipeline deletes only resources in the project resource group that have the AI Factory name of a service you switched off. It keeps Key Vault, storage accounts, Application Insights, dashboards and managed identities, and it never touches the common resource group. Databases are deleted with their data. Deleted Foundry, AI Services, Azure OpenAI and Azure Machine Learning resources are also purged, so you can't restore them. Read the list of switched-off services before you set it to "true".

To delete a whole project, a scale set or a Factory, use Clean up instead.

docs.title: Safe changes
docs.text:
• Name the Factory, the scale set, the project and the environment in every call.
  • Follow the run that a call returns until it ends. If you are unsure whether a deployment or a deletion worked, read its status before you start it again.
  • Deleting a project never removes the common part that other projects use.

A scale set in ESAF is a group of projects that share one network in one environment and subscription. It has nothing to do with Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets. See Core concepts.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
This site describes the main branch, where development happens. A release branch, such as release/v1.25, is a stable version that you choose when you create a Factory. News and releases lists what changed.

ESAF follows the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for AI and the Well-Architected guidance for AI workloads.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
An AI Factory has a common part and one resource group for each project. Every project starts from the same template, and the team switches on the Azure services it needs. You choose one of three hub modes when you create the Factory.

Each image shows the Factory with one hub mode, and how it connects to Microsoft 365, Microsoft Power Platform, SharePoint, Microsoft Fabric and the AI gateway. A numbered blue circle is a code template for that part: select the circle, or find the number in the table below.

External hubOwn hubStandalone

The Factory connects to a hub that you already own, with VNet peering. Your hub gives the VPN or ExpressRoute connection, the firewall and the private DNS zones. Choose it when you have a landing zone, or when several Factories share one hub.

Open the image at full size | PNG

The Factory creates its own hub in its Dev network, with a VPN gateway, a DNS Private Resolver and Bastion. Choose it when you need private access and have no central hub.

Open the image at full size | PNG

The Factory has no hub. It keeps its network and its private DNS zones in the common resource group, and people reach the services over the internet from the IP addresses you allow. Choose it to evaluate ESAF or to run a workshop. Networking is hybrid or public.

Open the image at full size | PNG

docs.title: How each connection works
docs.text:
Connection How it works Settings and templates Microsoft 365: Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot You publish an agent of the Foundry project. Azure Bot Service passes each message from Teams or Copilot to that agent. enableBotService, botFoundryAgentName, botFoundryProjectResourceId. Template 1. Microsoft Power Platform: Copilot Studio and Power Automate The common virtual network has a subnet that is delegated to Power Platform (common_pbi_subnet_name). You connect your Power Platform environment to that subnet. Agents and flows then call the Factory over the private network. common_pbi_subnet_name, common_pbi_subnet_cidr. No code template yet. SharePoint SharePoint is a knowledge source outside the Factory. Foundry IQ connects to it, and your agents answer from it. Template 5 keeps each reader's permissions and has an optional SharePoint sync. AI gateway: API Management, or Kong One endpoint in front of a pool of model deployments, with retries when a backend is throttled. Kong is the alternative when your organization runs Kong. The gateway has its own pipeline. ENABLE_APIM or ENABLE_KONG, and the apimGateway... and kongGateway... settings. Template 7. See AI gateways. Microsoft Fabric A Fabric data agent answers questions about your Fabric data. A Foundry agent calls it as a tool. Templates 3, 4 and 18. Azure Machine Learning A Foundry agent trains, retrains and scores models in the workspace of the project. enableAzureMachineLearning. Templates 8 and 14.

Every setting is explained in Every variable in variables.json, and the Azure resource library lists the services by category.

docs.title: Monitor and operate
docs.text:
Choose the question you want to answer.

Your question Use Good to know Is the Factory API running? azurefactory health It checks the API process. For the health of Azure resources, use the health model below. What exists in my Factory? The catalog: factories, scale sets and projects It shows what the API has saved and deployed. Did this deployment finish? The status and the logs of the job that the call returned A job ends as succeeded or failed. Follow it until then. How much did we use, and what did it cost? The usage workbooks and the cost reports Azure reports cost with a delay, so today's cost is incomplete. Are the services of a project healthy together? The optional Azure Monitor health model It is a preview service that you set up for each project.

Remove and recover has the commands for job status, logs, watching a GitHub workflow, saved reports and the cost of a resource group. Project teams start at Project dashboards.

docs.title: Metrics, reports and dashboards
docs.text:
• Sample reports show demonstration data, so that you can see a report before you have usage of your own.
  • Saved reports show results that were collected earlier.
  • Live reads ask Azure now. Your identity needs read access to the subscription or the resource group.
  • Dashboards have their own refresh operation, apart from reading a report.

Treat missing or old data as unknown, never as zero cost or good health. To report business results, add your own measures to the application.

docs.title: Optional health models
docs.text:
The healthmodel package deploys an Azure Monitor health model for a project: a tree of the services, the signals of each one and the alerts. It has its own Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions pipelines and uses the preview API Microsoft.CloudHealth. Check that your region supports it.

Health model guide

docs.title: Agent Chat and MCP
docs.text:
Component What it is for ESAF Agent Chat Ask questions about your Factory and its documentation, in a chat that answers from the sources. See Enable ESAF Agent Chat. Agent Chat live voice Talk to the same agent. A voice orb shows when it listens, thinks and speaks. It needs Agent Chat, an Entra ID app registration and private access to Foundry. Factory MCP server Gives MCP clients, such as an agent, the read-only tools of the Factory. Private Azure MCP template Gives the agents of your workload read-only tools for Azure resources. MCP on the AI gateway Publishes the Factory MCP server through API Management. It is an optional step of the project 001 Dev pipeline.

Each of these acts with the permissions of the person or the identity that calls it.

More info

Dashboards | Agent Chat template | Factory MCP | Private Azure MCP template | MCP on the AI gateway | Agent Chat and live voice

Model calls, monitoring queries and deployments each need their own permissions, and each has its own cost.

docs.title: v1.25
docs.text:
The v1.25 release notes describe the release/v1.25 branch as of 23 September 2026: the Factory API with its CLI and SDK, the Agent Factory, the ML Model Factory, versioned data, monitoring and the gateway policies.

The roadmap lists what is planned after that.

docs.title: Not available yet
docs.text: Capability Status Promotion from Dev to Stage to Prod as one workflow Not available. You deploy each environment with its own settings. Keeping selected resources when a whole resource group is deleted Not available. A whole-group delete removes everything in the group. A health model command in the CLI and the app Not available. Deploy the health model with its own pipeline. Sending reports by email Not available.

docs.title: Before you run a template
docs.text:
1. Ask your platform team for a project: see Usage docs and the prerequisites.
  2. Check that the project has the services on the card. The Azure resource library names the setting that switches each one on.
  3. Open the template and follow its guide. New to the Agent Factory or the Model Factory? Start with Run your first agent or Train your first model.

docs.title: Where the templates live
docs.text: Folder in usecase_code What it holds 40-agent-factory The Agent Factory: prompt agents, hosted agents, RAG, voice, MCP and the agents that work with Fabric and Azure Machine Learning. 50-ml-model-factory The Model Factory: batch, online and streaming examples for each task and technology. The library lists the examples that are tested in Azure. The use-case tree has all of them. 10-azure-function Azure Functions, including the one that runs the six ESAF scenarios. 20-agent-foundry Two starter scripts for Foundry agents, each in one file.

docs.title: AI Factory concepts
docs.text: An AI Factory keeps the shared platform services apart from the projects that use them. The platform team owns the Factory and its scale sets. Each project team owns its project.

docs.title: Factory, scale set and project
docs.text:
Term Meaning Factory One governed AI platform: its name, its region and its settings. Scale set A group of projects that share one network, in one environment and subscription. It has nothing to do with Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets. Project One team's workload, with a three-digit number such as 001, its own resource group and its own settings. Environment Dev, Stage or Prod. A project is deployed to each environment that you ask for. Common services The network, data lake, Key Vault and monitoring that the projects of a scale set share.

You name a Factory, a scale set and a project by their key or number in every call, for example esaf.upsert_project("002", "dev", scale_set="001"). See scale and environment choices and the six scenarios.

docs.title: Watch the concepts
docs.text:
These animations are the lessons under View > Concept animations in the configuration wizard. They show an example setup. If your device asks for reduced motion, you get a still image. Use the links below each animation to open it at full size.

The animations carry their own font: Open Sans font notices and license.

docs.title: Factories, scale sets and projects
docs.text: Animated SVG | GIF | Still image

docs.title: Configuration map
docs.text:
Follow ingestion, DataOps, training, inference and an agent in a small example. The region labels are examples.

Animated SVG | GIF | Still image

docs.title: Choose the layer you need
docs.text: Goal Guidance Configure or operate the factory Factory tools Understand planning and dependency checks Platform automation Build infrastructure IaC templates Prepare and move data DataOps Train and evaluate models MLOps Build agents and RAG applications GenAIOps Follow usage, cost and health Monitor and operate

docs.title: Three rules to keep in mind
docs.text:
1. A call does the whole scenario. esaf.init_factory() or esaf.upsert_project(...) saves the settings and runs the pipeline that deploys them. Follow the run it returns until it ends.
  2. Switching a service off deletes it only when you ask for that. A switched-off service that already exists stays in Azure unless enableDeleteForDisabledResources is "true". See what happens when you switch a service off.
  3. Azure is the truth. A template or a diagram shows what a deployment creates. The run status and the Azure portal show what exists.

You choose GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps as the pipeline provider when you create the Factory. Both run the same Bicep templates. See GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps.

docs.title: Where your Factory is stored
docs.text: The Factory API keeps your factories in a folder named azurefactory, with register.json as its index and one variables.json for each project. See Folder structure. Change the settings with a tool rather than by editing the files, so that the API checks them.

docs.title: Enterprise design and scale
docs.text: An AI Factory lets many teams reuse one common infrastructure, while every project keeps its own resources in each environment.

docs.title: Scale by projects and scale sets
docs.text:
A scale set groups projects that share one network, in one environment and subscription. It has nothing to do with Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets. A project names the scale set it runs in.

How many projects fit in a scale set depends on its address range, the subnets that already exist and your service quotas. When a scale set is full, add a scale set.

docs.title: Environments and subscriptions
docs.text:
Choice Meaning Shared subscriptions Environments can share subscriptions while retaining explicit identity and network targets. Own subscriptions Use the selected subscriptions for the intended isolated targets. Existing enterprise network Reuse approved hub, DNS and subnet arrangements through supported inputs.

Add only the environments you need. Dev is created first. Stage and Prod are created when you ask for them, in subscriptions that already exist.

docs.title: Watch Dev, Stage and Prod
docs.text:
Follow a versioned candidate through development, evaluation, release approval and monitoring. The animation shows the recommended process. Promote code and models between environments. Keep production data and secrets where they are.

Animated SVG | GIF | Still image

docs.title: Review each design concern
docs.text:
Concern What to check Security Identity, least privilege, data access, private connectivity and supported encryption options. Reliability Dependencies, backup/recovery, regional service support and failure handling. Cost Selected services, environment SKUs, model capacity and usage/cost reporting. Operations Reviewed changes, exact run tracking, diagnostic settings and ownership. Performance Workload needs, compute/service sizing, scaling limits and available capacity.

These are the pillars of the Well-Architected guidance for AI workloads.

docs.title: Plan network space before deployment
docs.text:
Give each environment its own range, and keep the ranges apart from your existing networks and from the VPN client pool. ESAF plans subnets inside the range you give. It doesn't resize a VNet that already exists.

The Parameters checklist and the platform automation guide list the settings. With private networking, the pipeline runner and your users also need a route and DNS to reach the private endpoints. See Hub and network modes.

More info

With shared subscriptions, a scale set uses a /18 range and the third octet starts at 0 for Dev, 64 for Stage and 128 for Prod. With own subscriptions it uses a /20 range, with 0, 16 and 32.

Which services and models you can use depends on the Azure region and cloud. Check the region of your Factory before you switch on a service.

Registered operations | Shared template parameters

docs.title: Platform automation
docs.text: ESAF turns the settings you choose into a repeatable deployment. This page lists what it works out for you and what you still decide.

docs.title: What the automation does
docs.text: Area What ESAF does What you decide Address planning Calculates the subnets of each project from the range of the scale set and the subnets that already exist. Give a range that is large enough and doesn't overlap your other networks. Service dependencies Checks that the services you switched on have the services they need. Private Foundry agents, for example, need AI Search, Cosmos DB and Storage. Choose the services. Resolve what the check reports. Identity and access Creates the managed identities and assigns the roles for the project team and the services. Name the people or the Entra ID groups of the team. Settings in three formats Maps each setting to its name in variables.json, in the Azure DevOps variables and in the GitHub variables. Change a setting in one place, with a tool. Naming Builds every resource name from the Factory prefix, the project number, the region and the environment. Choose the prefix and the suffix once, when you create the Factory. Updates Runs the same pipeline again to add a service or change a setting. Read the plan of a change before you run it.

docs.title: Groups and personas
docs.text: A project has a team. You name its members as users or as Entra ID groups (use_ad_groups). The pipeline gives the team the roles it needs on the project's services. Persona names such as team lead or data scientist label the groups. See Parameters for the settings.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Start with Parameters, then use Add and update to make the change.

More info

Address ranges. With shared subscriptions, a scale set uses a /18 range and the third octet starts at 0 for Dev, 64 for Stage and 128 for Prod. With own subscriptions it uses a /20 range, with 0, 16 and 32. Private DNS, routing, the VPN client pool and the access of the pipeline runner are part of the same plan.

Names. Use the resource IDs that a run returns in later calls, rather than building a name from the prefix yourself.

Stopped runs. When a run stops, read its status before you start it again. See Remove and recover.

docs.title: DataOps templates
docs.text: DataOps prepares data for your models and agents. Choose a data source, storage target, transformation and versioning approach before running a workload.

docs.title: Watch the data flow
docs.text:
These lessons from the configuration wizard show the data path for each kind of workload. Choose a tab. If your device asks for reduced motion, you get a still image.

DataOpsDataOps + MLOpsDataOps + RAGDataOps + fine-tuning

Follow original inputs through Bronze, Silver and Gold, with explicit versioning and producer/consumer ownership.

Animated SVG | GIF | Still image

Prepare reproducible training and inference data, keeping held-out evaluation data separate from training.

Animated SVG | GIF | Still image

Prepare approved documents and the copies that retrieval reads. The source owner's data stays unchanged.

Animated SVG | GIF | Still image

Prepare an approved, versioned training dataset, with separate data for evaluation.

Animated SVG | GIF | Still image

docs.title: A reusable data path
docs.text:
Stage Purpose Landing / original inputs Keep the source version and its origin clear. Bronze Preserve the supported original input representation. Silver Clean and transform data using the selected engine and format. Gold Create the model/application-ready view and reproducible splits. Inference and feedback Track scoring inputs, outputs, checkpoints and feedback separately.

The Model Factory examples read and write a versioned data lake, with Delta tables where the scenario uses them. Each scenario names its input folders.

docs.title: Choose the tools for the workload
docs.text: Data Factory orchestrates ingestion, Databricks transforms the data, and Event Hubs carries event streams. Switch on the ones your workload needs. To read from Fabric or OneLake, add a connection and give the project access to the workspace. The code templates library has templates that use Fabric.

docs.title: Common or project storage
docs.text:
use_common_datalake_storage chooses where a workload example keeps its data: the common data lake of the scale set, or the storage account of the project. New examples use project storage.

Changing the setting doesn't move your data

When you change it, copy the data yourself and deploy the workload again, so that it reads from the new place.

A project writes only to its own data. To share Silver data with another project, give that project read access or an approved copy.

docs.title: Continue
docs.text:
• ML Model Factory configuration and data
  • Agent Factory storage and ingestion
  • MLOps and GenAIOps
More info

Keep your configuration and your copies of the examples apart from the shared engines and from generated output. Each scenario lists what it needs: the storage format, a hierarchical namespace, checkpoints and the licence of its sample data.

After you assign access to a folder, test it as the person who will use it.

docs.title: Agent Factory and GenAIOps
docs.text: The Agent Factory is a set of code templates for prompt agents, hosted agents, multi-agent teams, data ingestion and RAG. Find them all, with filters, in the code templates library.

docs.title: Watch RAG step by step
docs.text:
Follow approved documents through chunking and indexing, then a question through retrieval to a grounded answer. RAG gives the model your documents as context when a question is asked. The model itself isn't trained on them.

Animated SVG | GIF | Still image

See also DataOps + RAG and fine-tuning.

docs.title: Choose a starting point
docs.text:
Example area Use 41-single-agent Foundry prompt-agent and supported hosted-framework examples. 42-multi-agent A hosted team calling separately persisted knowledge/reviewer agents. 43-data Ingestion and retrieval preparation for the selected target. 44-azure-mcp A narrow, private read-only Azure tool example. 45-rag-agent Explicit source-bound RAG with separate Search and Foundry IQ paths.

Open the Agent Factory quickstart, or follow Run your first agent.

docs.title: The project gives you the services, the template gives you the agent
docs.text:
The project pipeline deploys Foundry, Storage, Key Vault, AI Search, Cosmos DB, monitoring and the hosting services you switched on. Private Foundry agents need AI Search, Cosmos DB and Storage together. You then run a template to ingest your data and deploy an agent.

The model names, versions, SKUs and capacity of a project are settings. See Every variable in variables.json.

docs.title: RAG and shared data
docs.text:
Choose the source, its version and who may read the answers. Then run the ingestion and connect the index or the Foundry IQ knowledge base to the agent. To keep the access rights of each document, start from the template with access control lists in the library.

When you change use_common_datalake_storage, copy the data yourself and deploy the agent again.

docs.title: Gateways
docs.text:
Gateway What it does API Management as the AI gateway Puts one endpoint in front of several model deployments, with load balancing, retries and token limits. Kong The alternative AI gateway, when your organization runs Kong. Application Gateway Brings web traffic from your network to an application in a project.

See the gateway settings and the architecture.

Agent Chat and the Factory MCP server are for operating the Factory itself. The agents you build for your workload are separate, and each runs with its own identity and permissions.

More info

Private RAG example | Private Azure MCP | Monitor and operate

The private Azure MCP template gives an agent read-only tools for Azure resources. It can't change them. Model calls and ingestion cost money, so check the quota and the budget of the project before a large run.

docs.title: Infrastructure templates
docs.text: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) describes Azure resources as versioned files. ESAF uses Bicep modules, and its pipelines run them in the right order.

docs.title: Common and project infrastructure
docs.text:
Source area Role esml-common The common part: network, data lake, Key Vault and monitoring esml-genai-1 The project, in phases modules One reusable module for each Azure service and for access copy_to_local_settings The Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions pipelines

The folder names keep their history. There is one project template today, and the project pipeline deploys it in phases: foundation, core infrastructure, AI services, databases, compute, the AI and ML platform, access, Foundry, dashboards and integration.

docs.title: Use settings before customizing shared code
docs.text:
To change what is deployed, change a setting: start with Parameters and Add and update. Keep your settings outside the copied templates, because an update replaces those copies.

The debug switches skip pipeline steps while you investigate a problem. Run the full pipeline again afterwards.

docs.title: Reuse what you already have
docs.text:
You can point ESAF at a VNet and subnets, a common resource group, a data lake or a Key Vault that already exist. Decide which tool owns each resource, so that two tools don't change the same one.

Bicep details | Bring your own infrastructure

More info

Current Bicep source | GHA project phases | ADO project jobs

Deleting works in a set order, which differs from the order of deployment. Use Clean up to delete a project, a scale set or a Factory.

docs.title: ML Model Factory and MLOps
docs.text: The Model Factory is a set of code templates and shared engines to prepare data, train and compare models, and deploy the one you choose. Find them in the code templates library.

docs.title: Watch the model lifecycle
docs.text:
Follow versioned data through training, evaluation on held-out data, comparison, registration, the approval to deploy, and monitoring.

Animated SVG | GIF | Still image

For the upstream data path, see DataOps + MLOps.

docs.title: Choose your use case
docs.text:
Pattern Typical use Batch Score a dataset on demand or on a schedule. Online Answer individual inference requests. Streaming Process continuous or micro-batch events with checkpoints.

The current Model Factory organizes examples by pattern, task and technology: classification, regression, forecasting and supported vision routes using custom Python, AutoML, Azure ML pipelines and Databricks.

Start at the use-case tree, or follow Train your first model. Each example lists what it needs.

docs.title: Where to make your changes
docs.text: Folder in 50-ml-model-factory Ownership user-config Your scenario, model policy, storage and Databricks choices. Project copies of usecase-type examples Thin examples you can adapt for the workload. accelerator Shared maintainer-owned engines; avoid copying their internals. data/out and ml-environment Generated datasets, models, reports and run artifacts.

docs.title: Train, compare and deploy separately
docs.text:
1. Validate the chosen scenario, input data, budget and compute references.
  2. Render or inspect the job before submitting cloud work.
  3. Evaluate candidates against compatible held-out data and the configured policy.
  4. Review registration and deployment as separate actions.
  5. Monitor inputs, performance and freshness after deployment.

The best model of a comparison still needs your approval before it goes to production. When labels or observations are missing, the monitoring shows the result as unknown.

docs.title: Version and engine limits
docs.text:
azure-esml-sdk (azure_esml) is a new API. Code written for the ESML v1 SDK needs changes to use it. AutoML forecasting isn't available for streaming, because that forecast needs the observed history with every request. The Model Factory guide names the alternative.

The compute sizes and versions of a project are settings, and what you can choose depends on the region. See the Parameters reference.

More info

Model Factory quickstart and limitations | Shared pipeline templates | DataOps

Each example lists what it needs: the licence of its sample data, the vision packages, a compute cluster that exists, and a sign-in to Azure.

docs.title: Bicep infrastructure
docs.text: Bicep describes the Azure resources that the pipelines deploy. You change settings. ESAF runs the Bicep modules for you.

docs.title: How a change reaches Azure
docs.text:
1. Choose the Factory, the scale set and the project.
  2. Change the settings, for example switch on a service.
  3. Run the change with the app, the CLI, the Python SDK or REST.
  4. Follow the run until it ends, then look at the resources in Azure.

Add and update walks through it for each tool. You only edit Bicep when you add a service that ESAF doesn't have yet.

docs.title: Source organization
docs.text:
Location under environment_setup\aifactory\bicep Purpose esml-common The common part of a scale set esml-genai-1 The project, deployed in phases modules One reusable module for each Azure service and for access copy_to_local_settings The Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions pipelines that are copied to your repository scripts Checks, settings conversion and helper steps of the pipelines

The folder names keep their history. There is one project template today.

The variables.json of a project has two sections: dev, and stage_prod for Stage and Prod. See Every variable in variables.json.

docs.title: Updating what exists
docs.text:
Running the pipeline again updates the resources that exist and adds the services you switched on. Azure can't change some properties in place. Such a change fails, and the log of the run gives the reason.

Switching a service off

A switched-off service that exists stays in Azure while enableDeleteForDisabledResources is "false", the default. With "true", the next project pipeline run deletes it. See what happens when you switch a service off.

docs.title: Encryption and private networking
docs.text:
Each service has its own settings for customer-managed keys, private endpoints, DNS and roles. Give the key and the permissions that each switched-on service needs. See the Parameters reference.

More info

The modules include aiSearch.bicep, keyVault.bicep, storageAccount.bicep and aksCluster.bicep. See the module folder for all of them.

When you attach an AKS cluster to Azure Machine Learning, the template passes the load-balancer subnet of that cluster.

After a run succeeds, test that your users and the pipeline runner reach the services over the private network.

docs.title: Bring your own infrastructure
docs.text:
Do you already manage shared Azure resources with Terraform? Point ESAF at those resources with the settings below. Decide which tool owns each resource, so that Terraform and ESAF never change the same one.

ESAF deploys with Bicep

ESAF has no Terraform templates of its own. You keep Terraform for the resources it already manages, and ESAF deploys the rest with Bicep.

docs.title: A practical split
docs.text:
Your platform team provides subscriptions, the hub network, DNS, storage or other common services. ESAF then uses them through these settings.

Input What it identifies vnetNameFull_param, vnetResourceGroup_param Existing VNet and its resource group commonResourceGroup_param Common resource-group reference datalakeName_param Existing data-lake account kvNameFromCOMMON_param Existing common Key Vault BYO_subnets and the subnet names Use subnets that already exist centralDnsZoneByPolicyInHub and privDns* settings Central private-DNS design and location

See all parameters for the exact names and conditions. Give the deployment identity access to each resource you name.

docs.title: Before you integrate
docs.text:
1. Agree which tool owns each resource and its state.
  2. Collect the IDs, subscriptions, address ranges, DNS zones and routes.
  3. Give the deployment identity only the permissions it needs.
  4. Read what a Factory or project deletion removes, so that it stays away from the resources Terraform owns. See Clean up.
More info

Bicep | Add and update

ESAF doesn't read Terraform state. You name each existing resource in the settings.

docs.title: Azure DevOps
docs.text: Choose Azure DevOps when your team keeps its repositories, pipelines and service connections there. The Factory, its settings and the Bicep templates are the same as with GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Start with a Factory
docs.text: Create the Factory with the ado orchestrator: follow Create your AI Factory, or Add and update when you want to review each step yourself.

docs.title: What to have ready
docs.text: Input What it is Azure tenant and subscription The environment you deploy to, and an identity that may deploy there. Azure DevOps organization, project and repository Where the code and the pipelines live. Azure DevOps tenant azureDevOpsTenantId. It can differ from the Azure tenantId. Keep both as they are. Service connections One for each environment you deploy, by its exact name. Agent pool A Linux pool. With private networking, its agents need a route to the private endpoints. Version The ESAF version to deploy, such as main or a release.

docs.title: Service-connection parameters
docs.text:
JSON/YAML key Purpose dev_service_connection Dev deployment dev_seeding_kv_service_connection Dev seeding-vault access test_service_connection / test_seeding_kv_service_connection Stage, when selected prod_service_connection / prod_seeding_kv_service_connection Prod, when selected

One service principal can serve several of these connections. Each connection you name must be authorized for its pipeline. The settings that end in a secret name hold the name of a Key Vault secret, never the secret itself.

docs.title: Follow the run
docs.text:
Keep the job ID that a call returns, and follow that job until it ends. Then open the pipeline run in Azure DevOps for the details of each step. The CLI commands workflow status and workflow watch follow GitHub runs only.

Parameters | Add and update | Remove and recover

Earlier way: the launcher scripts

A repository that was set up with v1.24 has these scripts in its root:

  • ADO-create-new-aifactory-scaleset.sh creates a Factory with its identities, repository and pipelines.
  • ADO-update-aifactory-and-run-project.sh updates the templates and runs the project pipeline.
  • --project-only runs the project pipeline without updating the templates.
  • --aifactory-env dev|stage|prod selects the environment.

Create uses version 124 unless you give another, and update keeps the version that was saved. Name main to use the current development version. --prepare-only prepares Azure and the settings without completing the deployment, so it does change things. All inputs are in the launcher reference.

The variables live in aifactory\esml-infra\azure-devops\bicep\yaml\variables\variables.yaml. Azure DevOps uses the YAML names, and GitHub uses its own uppercase names.

Current ADO templates | Setup overview

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text: Choose GitHub Actions when your team keeps its repositories, environments and workflows on GitHub. The Factory, its settings and the Bicep templates are the same as with Azure DevOps.

docs.title: Start with a Factory
docs.text: Create the Factory with the gha orchestrator: follow Create your AI Factory, or Add and update when you want to review each step yourself.

docs.title: Repository, identity and environments
docs.text:
Area What to have ready Repository Its owner and name, and whether it is private or public. Azure identity A federated identity (OIDC) for the workflows, or a service principal. GitHub environment Its exact name (upper and lower case matter), with its variables, secrets and protection rules. Runner A self-hosted runner that reaches the private endpoints, when the Factory is private. Azure target The tenant, the subscription, the region and the environment.

Full bootstrap creates the GitHub environments Dev, Stage and Prod, and stores which GitHub environment belongs to which Factory environment in the repository variable AIFACTORY_GITHUB_ENVIRONMENTS. Creating a GitHub environment deploys nothing to Azure. Keep the names of existing environments, because the federated identity is bound to them.

When you enroll an existing repository, the federated identity is bound to environment:<auth_namespace>. If that name isn't dev, stage or prod and the variable doesn't exist yet, enrollment creates AIFACTORY_GITHUB_ENVIRONMENTS with that name. An existing variable is never overwritten. The plan warns when it names a different environment.

The Add-Factory-Agent and project dashboard workflows read the operating system of the self-hosted runner from selfHostedRunnerOS in variables.json. Without that setting they use the runner in azurefactory/register.json (Linux), and otherwise Windows.

docs.title: Settings and private access
docs.text:
GitHub variables have uppercase names, and variables.json has its own names. The Parameters reference lists both for every setting. A change in a local .env file reaches the workflows after the variables are published to GitHub.

With private networking, use a self-hosted runner inside the network. A GitHub-hosted runner can't reach private endpoints.

docs.title: Follow the run
docs.text:
Follow the job that a call returns, or the GitHub run itself. workflow status and workflow watch only read: starting the watch again never starts the workflow again. When a watch times out, the run in Azure continues.

Status and recovery examples

More info

Subnets. In a shared VNet, each new project gets its subnets from the free ranges. Existing subnets keep their names and ranges. Add one project at a time to a shared network.

Simple mode. Simple mode and Full bootstrap take different inputs for addresses and services. Simple mode can create a new Application Gateway. To use a gateway you already have, leave that option off. See the simple mode reference.

MCP and AI gateway. The Factory MCP server and the AI gateway are optional steps of the project 001 Dev pipeline. See the settings.

Earlier way: the launcher scripts

A repository that was set up with v1.24 has these scripts in its root:

  • GHA-create-new-aifactory-scaleset.sh creates a Factory with its identities, repository and workflows.
  • GH-update-aifactory-and-run-project.sh updates the templates and runs the project workflow. GHA-update-aifactory-and-run-project.sh calls the same script.
  • --project-only runs the project workflow without updating the templates.
  • --aifactory-env dev|stage|prod selects the environment.

Create uses version 124 unless you give another, and update keeps the version that was saved. Pass --aifactory-version main to use the current development version.

A launcher run commits and pushes, sets up identities, creates Azure resources that cost money and starts workflows. --prepare-only does all of that except the deployment. With --no-wait the script returns before the workflows end, so follow them on GitHub.

Complete launcher inputs | Current GHA templates | Setup guide

docs.title: Parameters: configure your factory
docs.text:
Parameters are the settings of a Factory and its projects. They are the variables in variables.json, and they have matching names in the Azure DevOps variables.yaml and in the GitHub .env file. Use this section to find the name of a setting, its values and what it depends on.

What you need Open Start configuring a Factory CLI, Python SDK or REST tutorial Choose the Azure services of a project Azure resource library See every variable in variables.json, with its default and what it does Every variable in variables.json Know which inputs to collect Required inputs Look up an exact key, default or format mapping All parameters Change settings and deploy them Add and update Delete a project, a scale set or a Factory Clean up, Remove and recover

Switching a service off

A service set to "false" is no longer deployed. A resource that already exists stays in Azure while enableDeleteForDisabledResources is "false", the default. With "true", the next run of the project pipeline deletes the switched-off services that exist in the project resource group, and it purges Foundry, AI Services, Azure OpenAI and Azure Machine Learning resources. It keeps Key Vault, storage, Application Insights and managed identities. See what happens when you switch a service off.

docs.title: Change settings with a tool
docs.text:
Read the settings of the Factory, the project and the environment you mean before you change them. The quickest way is one call, such as esaf.upsert_project(..., settings=...): see the six scenarios. To review each change before it is saved, use these commands.

Task CLI Python SDK REST Read editable settings catalog settings catalog_settings(...) GET /api/v1/factory-catalog/settings Prepare setting replacements catalog configure-settings catalog_settings_prepare(...) POST /api/v1/factory-catalog/prepare, action configure-settings Save reviewed replacements catalog confirm catalog_confirm(...) POST /api/v1/factory-catalog/confirm Read deployed-template parameter choices parameters get catalog_parameters(...) GET /api/v1/factory-catalog/parameters Prepare typed parameter changes parameters prepare parameter_prepare(...) POST /api/v1/factory-catalog/parameters/prepare Save reviewed parameter changes parameters confirm parameter_confirm(...) POST /api/v1/factory-catalog/parameters/confirm

The table gives the names only. Add and update has a full example for each one.

The Factory API writes register.json and the variables.json of each project. Change them with a tool, so that the API checks every value. A project keeps its own saved settings: changing a default of the Factory changes new projects only.

docs.title: Dev, Stage and Prod
docs.text:
The variables.json of a project has two sections: dev, and stage_prod for Stage and Prod. Stage and Prod have their own subscriptions and share the settings of stage_prod, so a change there reaches both.

The template of variables.json in the repository has a dev section only. It holds the Dev and the Stage/Prod value of each SKU side by side.

docs.title: Settings that belong together
docs.text: Area Settings Private Foundry agents enableAIFoundry and enableAFoundryCaphost need AI Search, Cosmos DB and Storage. Switch them on together. Network and DNS The address range, and where the private DNS zones live: in the Factory or in your hub. See Hub and network modes. Models and compute The model version, the SKU and the capacity. What you can choose depends on the region and on your quota. MCP and gateways The Factory MCP server, the AI gateway on API Management or Kong, and Application Gateway each have their own settings. See MCP and AI gateway. Access Entra ID object IDs of users or groups, and the names of Key Vault secrets. A setting holds the name of a secret, never the secret itself. Deletion enableDeleteForDisabledResources for switched-off services. Clean up for a whole project, scale set or Factory.

docs.title: Optional project ownership labels
docs.text:
org-department-name and org-department-id say who owns a project. Both are empty by default. Use the same values in every environment of the project. They are labels only: they change no access and no Azure tags.

More info

The name supports plain Unicode text up to 200 characters; the ID is a string up to 128 characters, not necessarily a GUID. Control characters are rejected. JSON/YAML use the hyphenated names; .env uses ORG_DEPARTMENT_NAME and ORG_DEPARTMENT_ID. Read/edit them at project scope, not as an inherited factory label.

The generated reference is built from the templates in the repository. It lists the default of every setting and its name in each format. An older Factory API can lack a setting that is new in the templates. /api/v1/schema lists the settings your API knows, /openapi.json lists its HTTP requests, and parameters get lists the settings of the deployed templates.

Earlier way: edit the files of a v1.24 repository (Legacy)

In a repository that was set up with v1.24, you edit the file that its pipeline reads. Keep the other keys, the value types and the environments as they are. Change a setting in one format only, because the .env file, the YAML and the JSON are separate inputs. GitHub variables are published by their own step.

The commands config review and config save, and the routes /api/v1/projects/load, /api/v1/import, /api/v1/validation, /api/v1/export and /api/v1/projects/save, work on such a JSON file. Export writes a file on the machine that runs the API. It doesn't deploy.

The pipeline reads the dev section first, then stage_prod, then a test or prod section when one exists. See file first or wrapper first.

The Factory API is an administration service that listens on the local machine. Keep its key on a server you trust, never in browser JavaScript.

docs.title: Parameters - complete reference
docs.text:
Start with the required inputs. This reference lists every setting you can change, with its default and its name in each format. For one explained list, see Every variable in variables.json.

The page is built from the templates on the main branch. To change a setting, use a tool rather than editing the files.

Jump to current feature choices, all JSON/YAML parameters, or GitHub environment parameters.

docs.title: MCP and AI Gateway parameters
docs.text:
These settings switch on optional steps of the project001 Dev pipeline, in Azure DevOps and in GitHub Actions.

JSON/YAML GitHub name Effect / requirements enableAIFactoryMCP ENABLE_AI_FACTORY_MCP Host read-only Factory MCP; needs Foundry, Container Apps, approved image digests and the Entra app. enableAIGatewaySKU ENABLE_AI_GATEWAY_SKU Create or adopt the dedicated AI Gateway with the selected Foundry account. addAIFactoryMCP2AIGatewaySKU ADD_AI_FACTORY_MCP_2_AI_GATEWAY_SKU Register the MCP tool server; both components and suitable private outbound networking are required.

All three default to false. False skips the step; it does not delete resources. To delete a switched-off service that exists, see enableDeleteForDisabledResources in the variables list. aifactoryMcpImage, aifactoryMcpApiImage and aifactoryMcpEntraAppId are required for MCP hosting. aiGatewaySkuResourceId selects an existing gateway to adopt; aiGatewaySkuOutboundSubnetId provides the new gateway's outbound subnet when registration needs it. aifactoryMcpClassicApimResourceIds (optional, requires enableAIFactoryMCP) lists classic APIM gateways whose system-assigned identities may call the MCP; the APIMs are only read and an administrator assigns AiFactory.Mcp.Read to each identity. The exact environment names and defaults are in the generated tables below.

The AI gateway for model calls has its own pipeline and settings: API Management with a pool of model backends (ENABLE_APIM), or Kong as the alternative (ENABLE_KONG). Application Gateway is for web traffic and has its own settings. See component prerequisites.

docs.title: Safe editing
docs.text:
Change settings with a tool. Read the default of a setting and what it depends on, and change only the values you mean to. Removing a value you set returns the setting to its default; it deletes nothing in Azure. A setting that ends in a secret name holds the name of a Key Vault secret, never the secret itself.

More info Alternative and Legacy ways

docs.title: Scope and authoritative sources
docs.text:
The generated tables include every unique key in these shared templates:

  • environment_setup/aifactory/bicep/copy_to_local_settings/github-actions/.env.template
  • environment_setup/aifactory/bicep/copy_to_local_settings/azure-devops/esml-yaml-pipelines/variables/variables.yaml
  • environment_setup/aifactory/variables.json — every section and key, including all Dev and Stage/Prod SKU fields.

They also cover external create-bootstrap environment inputs and the configuration helper's CLI options, from bootstrap/lib/create-new-aifactory-scaleset.sh, bootstrap/lib/release_version.sh, the GH/ADO update launchers, and bootstrap/lib/aifactory_scaleset_config.py. Public Bash command switches are documented below. Internal resume flags, generated state, shell implementation locals, external service API schemas, and module-internal ARM inputs are excluded. The launcher scripts read their inputs from environment variables and then write the files of the chosen orchestrator. Those inputs are a different list from the GitHub .env file that the scripts write.

Two distinct JSON contracts

The raw checked-in consumer template environment_setup/aifactory/variables.json currently has a dev section only. Stage/Prod SKU pairs such as dev.skuAISearchStageProd are present inside it; there is no checked-in top-level stage_prod section. The legacy bootstrap helper's update_json() updates dev. The generated inventory below reports that shared template exactly; it is not the Azure Factory v2 output schema.

Each backend-generated Azure Factory v2 project has one variables.json with direct top-level dev and stage_prod sections, stored at factories/<key>/scalesets/<immutable storage_suffix>/projects/projectNNN/variables.json. Both sections retain the full configuration, with separate subscription and SKU values. They are not nested inside a wrapper or split across per-environment files. Review the selected project's two sections before CLI/API dispatch.

docs.title: Reading defaults and requirements
docs.text:
• M — mandatory in the source template's deployment context. A supplied default can satisfy the input, so you only edit the M rows whose default doesn't fit.
  • C — conditionally required. Applies only to the selected environment, identity route, service or networking mode. For example, Stage service connections are not prerequisites for a Dev-only run.
  • O — optional override or feature switch. A switch can still need other services: read its description. A switch stays O when a preset turns it on. The services that private Foundry agents need together are marked C.
  • Values are actual assignments, not the sometimes stale <default> text in comments. Empty strings and <todo> / <optional> placeholders are shown literally and are not usable credentials or resource IDs.
  • YAML and GHA marker annotations occasionally differ. Each GHA row retains its own annotation; a JSON key inherits the YAML annotation where available. Untagged settings default to O, with route/service conditions described in text.
  • Binding names come from shared workflow expressions, preflight getval mappings, bootstrap writers and explicitly reviewed template correspondences. No automatic case conversion is used. A binding may be a workflow fallback rather than an equivalent standalone input.

docs.title: Networking and DNS
docs.text:
The shared template default is shared-subscriptions with common_vnet_cidr=172.16.XX.0/18 and network-aligned Dev/Stage/Prod selectors 0 / 64 / 128. Own-subscription /20 planning uses 0 / 16 / 32. XX replaces the third octet in the VNet and subnet templates. Environments, VPN client pools and existing networks must not overlap. ESAF plans inside the range you give. It doesn't resize a network that already exists.

centralDnsZoneByPolicyInHub enableAIFactoryHub Meaning false false Standalone DNS/network intent false true Own AI Factory hub intent true Either External central-DNS hub takes precedence; supply its subscription/resource group

JSON stores these flags as booleans, while the YAML and GitHub templates use strings. The three public-access flags control access to the Azure services. Monitoring has its own switch: set enableAMPLS to true for private-only ingestion to Application Insights and Log Analytics.

docs.title: Models, SKUs and aliases
docs.text:
modelGPTXSku / MODEL_GPTX_SKU and default_model_sku / DEFAULT_MODEL_SKU default to DataZoneStandard. Check that the region of your Factory offers the model and version, and that your subscription has the quota for the capacity you ask for. Dev and Stage/Prod service SKUs remain separate fields.

AI Search has a particularly important fallback: skuAISearchDev reads SKU_AISEARCH_DEV, then ADMIN_AISEARCH_TIER; skuAISearchStageProd reads SKU_AISEARCH_STAGEPROD, then ADMIN_AISEARCH_TIER. The shared ADMIN_AISEARCH_TIER=basic can therefore override the workflow's final Stage/Prod standard fallback. ADMIN_AI_SEARCH_TIER is another spelling consumed by preflight, not a safe rename of every workflow input. Likewise, semantic tier and Azure ML principal-ID compatibility spellings coexist in the template.

docs.title: Capacity-only service fallbacks
docs.text:
Both ADO and GitHub Actions isolate AI Search, PostgreSQL Flexible Server and Container Apps from their cognitive/database/compute batches. Each has three separately visible attempt steps immediately after its batch. Only recognized regional/SKU capacity failures schedule another attempt; unrelated errors fail immediately, and exhausted candidates fail the pipeline before downstream deployments. Attempts 2 and 3 wait 240 seconds at their start when scheduled. With a nonempty AI Search region array, all region/SKU combinations instead run inside the separate regional-fallback task, without arming the three legacy SKU steps. Local normalization selects the current environment's route; [] or blank skips that regional task entirely, retaining ordinary Search/networking and SKU-only retries. Successful attempts export the effective SKU (and PostgreSQL tier) for later steps. The existing JSON-array names skuAISearchDevArray and skuAISearchStageProdArray remain supported alongside the comma-separated skuArrayAISearchDev / skuArrayAISearchStageProd names. A customized spelling takes precedence over the unchanged default. When both spellings have different custom values, validation fails and names them. Container Apps detected before the run retain their existing application images and configuration. Retry reconciliation uses the original existence flags, so only resources absent at the start are reapplied unless explicitly opted in.

The selected Dev or Stage/Prod SKU is tried first, followed by the remaining configured candidates in array order. Defaults are:

Service Selected defaults (Dev / Stage/Prod) Candidate arrays (both environments) Retry switch AI Search basic / standard basic,standard,standard2 aisearchRetryCapcityArray PostgreSQL Standard_B1ms / Standard_B1ms Standard_B1ms,Standard_B2s,Standard_B2ms postgreSQLRetryCapacityArray Container Apps Consumption / Consumption Consumption,D4,D8 containerAppsRetryCapacityArray

Configure skuArray<Service>Dev / skuArray<Service>StageProd alongside sku<Service>Dev / sku<Service>StageProd. All retry switches default to true; false attempts only the selected SKU (for AI Search, in each configured region). Keep the existing Capcity spelling in the AI Search switch. The generated inventory below lists the corresponding GitHub uppercase variable names.

Both aiSearchFallbackLocationArrayDev and aiSearchFallbackLocationArrayStageProd default in new JSON, ADO and GHA templates to ["francecentral","denmarkeast","italynorth","norwayeast","germanywestcentral"], in that order, Germany last. Test/Stage and Prod share the latter setting. The primary remains aiSearchLocation, otherwise project location; it is tried first with selected-first SKUs, then each fallback in list order. Up to five fallbacks plus the primary and three SKUs allow 18 creation attempts, with the unchanged 240-second delay before each retry. Explicit [] or blank disables regional fallback; missing runtime fields and undefined GHA variables retain [] for historical inputs. Denmark East is in the list because the portal allows it, although it is missing from Microsoft's AI Search region list. Germany is last because of its known capacity shortage.

This is provisioning-only recovery, not runtime failover, replication or index migration. Existing Search keeps its actual region and requested SKU changes; only recognized Search capacity errors permit retries. Only Search placement changes: the private endpoint remains in the original VNet region and outbound shared-link targets are unchanged. Effective region/SKU are published only after Search and required network deployment succeed. Review residency, latency, egress and cost before provisioning with these defaults.

Attempts honor the infra phase, deletion and service/debug switches, retaining the cognitive/database capability-host debug override used by ADO. AI Search also runs when private Foundry requires it (enableAIFoundry=true and enablePublicGenAIAccess!=true), even if enableAISearch=false. The preflight step checks your quota. A region can still be out of capacity when the deployment runs, which is what the retries are for. Container Apps fallback from Consumption to D4 or D8 changes to dedicated workload-profile pricing; review costs before enabling these candidates.

ADO has separate Dev/Stage/Prod seeding-vault coordinates and service connections. GHA commonly uses one seeding-vault variable name with environment-specific overrides. Review the collision table rather than copying one value into all environments. Some source defaults genuinely differ, including resource naming, Hybrid Benefit, user RBAC restrictions, placeholders and tag macros.

docs.title: Identity, secrets and lifecycle
docs.text:
Secret-name inputs identify entries in the seeding Key Vault; they are not secret values. Federated managed-identity/OIDC bootstrap can leave legacy service-principal secret-name fields empty. A seeding-vault shell may still be required. Existing-SP and PAT routes require secrets only when selected; keep them out of committed files, logs and command history.

The delete and debug switches are listed with the other settings. Leave them false for normal runs. Before you set a delete switch to true, read which project and environment the run targets and back up what you need.

docs.title: Bash create and update contract
docs.text:
Run these entrypoints from the generated consumer checkout, using Bash/Git Bash. They use the existing deployment engine and route configuration.

Entrypoint Public switch Meaning GHA-create-new-aifactory-scaleset.sh, ADO-create-new-aifactory-scaleset.sh --repo-root PATH Explicit legacy consumer root Create --aifactory-version VERSION Explicit source version, e.g. main, 124, 125, 1.100, 10.2 Create --dry-run Collect/validate without mutation; not an offline preview or supported simple-mode launch Create --prepare-only Prepare Azure, identity, configuration and automation without completing deployment Create --no-wait Dispatch without waiting; incompatible with the simple-mode dependent chain Create --non-interactive Read answers from process environment Create --yes Accept the execution summary Create/update --help, -h Show entrypoint help ALL-create-new-aifactory-scaleset.sh --orchestrator ado\|gha Select one route, then forward create options GH-update-aifactory-and-run-project.sh, GHA-update-aifactory-and-run-project.sh, ADO-update-aifactory-and-run-project.sh --project-only Dispatch project only; skip factory/template updates Update --aifactory-env dev\|stage\|prod Dispatch only the selected environment; conflicts with a different AIFACTORY_TARGET_ENVIRONMENT. Update --aifactory-version VERSION Choose update source version explicitly

Legacy create defaults to 124. Update inherits the saved version unless an explicit version selector is provided. Choose main explicitly for development; --project-only keeps the templates as they are. Current create validation accepts AIF_NETWORK_MODE=priv (default), h (hybrid) or pub (public). Private networking needs a hub (external, or the own hub with AIF_SETUP_HUB_ACCESS=true) unless AIFACTORY_PRIVATE_NETWORK_REQUIRES_HUB=false; a Standalone AI Factory without a hub uses h or pub. Its general region prompt defaults to swedencentral, whereas the shared configuration templates default to eastus2. The first run of a launcher deploys Dev only and copies the Dev subscription to the Stage and Prod settings. Change those before you deploy Stage or Prod.

The launcher scripts don't read or write azurefactory/register.json. For a Factory that the Factory API manages, use the CLI, the SDK or REST. The create script rejects AIF_CREATE_PROJECTS and AIF_PROJECT_MODE.

docs.title: Simple-mode technical contract
docs.text:
AIF_SIMPLE_MODE=true opts the GHA create entrypoint into contract v2, private-ai-foundation-v2. Use --non-interactive --yes --repo-root PATH and wait for the full common → access hub → project chain, followed by the private HTTPS gateway only when its deployment is enabled. Use the following offline, read-only preview instead of a deployment dry run:

python bootstrap/lib/aifactory_scaleset_config.py --simple-mode-manifest
python bootstrap/lib/aifactory_scaleset_config.py --simple-mode-manifest --enable-application-gateway false

Provide tenant/subscription, region, prefix, repository and initial team identity inputs, plus a published AIF_SUBMODULE_REF. Existing Azure/GitHub authentication is required. Prefix validation accepts 2–16 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. The default suffix is 001; the cost-center default is 123456.

Fixed settings are AIF_TOPOLOGY=s, AIF_NETWORK_MODE=priv, AIF_ACCESS_HUB_MODE=i, AIF_IDENTITY_MODE=c, AIF_SEEDING_MODE=c, AIF_SEED_PROJECT_SP=false, AIF_SETUP_HUB_ACCESS=true, AIF_CONFIGURE_VPN_CLIENT=false, AIF_DEV_VNET_CIDR=172.16.0.0/20, and AIF_PROJECT_NUMBER=001.

Only project Storage, Key Vault and managed identities are always required. Foundry is optional and selected by default, together with its capability host, Basic AI Search, Cosmos DB and Application Insights. Selecting Foundry requires all three dependencies; its capability host cannot be selected without Foundry. The UI clears those three when Foundry is unchecked, after which Search and Cosmos DB can be selected independently. Explicit AIF_SIMPLE_PROJECT_RESOURCES_JSON=[] deploys only the baseline project foundation. Omitting the selection preserves the default Foundry bundle. A selection that lacks a required service is rejected before anything changes in Azure. Valid selections are ordered by the catalog.

Additional optional IDs are azure-machine-learning, aks-for-azure-ml, aks, databricks, datafactory, event-hubs, postgresql and container-apps. aks-for-azure-ml requires azure-machine-learning; standalone aks is independent. AML and Container Apps also require their linked Application Insights; this is a conditional dependency, not a globally required service. Include that dependency in explicit CLI selections (for example ["azure-machine-learning","application-insights"]). All selected services map to the existing pipeline flags, with canonical baseline SKUs (Event Hubs Standard is required for Private Link). Resource-provider registration follows the selection. ML/Databricks materialize only their selected first-party enterprise applications, never temporary public workspaces; a tenant administrator may need to provision those applications or supply their object IDs. Foundry-specific deployment and capability-host checks skip when Foundry is off; agent network injection is disabled, while the common, networking, project, data and ML phases still run.

The additive literal projectResourceSelection manifest contract has version 1 and strict dependency validation. Publish the matching source before using it. All model deployment toggles remain off and model SKU defaults stay DataZoneStandard. Switch on a model deployment before you run an agent.

Deploying a new Application Gateway is optional, not a prerequisite for private Foundry agents. New UI selections default off. Set AIF_ENABLE_APPLICATION_GATEWAY=false to avoid deploying a second billable gateway when a customer already has a central gateway, or when no application ingress is needed. This does not adopt, integrate with, or modify that existing gateway. The environment accepts only lowercase true or false; empty/noncanonical values fail before cloud operations. Omitting it preserves legacy enabled behavior for existing automation.

When false, gateway hostname/backend/certificate inputs may be blank and all gateway-specific feature/certificate checks, subnet reservation, NSG, identity, certificate role grant/private endpoint, frontend DNS, deployment and backend health checks are skipped. VPN, DNS Private Resolver, required private DNS zones and the selected project workloads remain enabled. A new Application Gateway is optional in every environment, Prod included.

This is an additive v2 capability (AIF_SIMPLE_OPTIONAL_GATEWAY_CONTRACT=1), not a replacement for v2. The manifest's literal appGatewayDeployment advertises default: false, omittedDefault: true, and supported: [false, true]. Publish the matching bootstrap and infrastructure source together and use the verified published commit before deploying; updating only the UI/API is insufficient.

Gateway inputs below are required only when deploying a new gateway:

Environment input Helper/API input Constraint AIF_ENABLE_APPLICATION_GATEWAY --enable-application-gateway / enable_application_gateway true or false; new UI false, omitted legacy true AIF_APP_GATEWAY_HOSTNAME --app-gateway-hostname / app_gateway_hostname Custom frontend FQDN covered by certificate DNS SAN AIF_APP_GATEWAY_BACKEND_FQDN --app-gateway-backend-fqdn / app_gateway_backend_fqdn Distinct private RFC1918 HTTPS backend, reachable from the new VNet, trusted TLS, unauthenticated GET / returns 200–399 AIF_APP_GATEWAY_CERT_SECRET_ID --app-gateway-certificate-secret-id / app_gateway_certificate_secret_id Versionless https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/secrets/<name> URI of an enabled, valid, exportable PFX certificate in an RBAC-enabled Dev-subscription vault

No certificate secret value is embedded in these inputs. When gateway deployment is enabled, the private-network Application Gateway subscription feature must already be registered; existing secure HTTPS validation and readiness checks remain. VPN gateway/resolver subnets are reserved before project allocation: 172.16.1.0/27, 172.16.1.32/28. The Application Gateway block 172.16.2.0/24 is reserved only when its deployment is enabled. Conflicting existing allocations are rejected, not moved or deleted.

The access hub includes billable VPN Gateway and DNS Private Resolver resources. VPN transport uses a public IP; Azure service access remains independently controlled. The exported VPN profile is a sensitive connection artifact; connect the client manually. Bastion Developer requires regional support, has no automatic paid-SKU fallback, and does not create an admin VM.

GITHUB_REPOSITORY_VISIBILITY=private|public defaults to private for this contract, unlike the generic .env.template repository default. An existing repository must be empty and match the requested visibility. Review generated code and non-secret metadata before publication. The ignore rules cover .env, filled-in settings, certificates and VPN files. Check for other secrets yourself before you publish a repository.

docs.title: Maintaining the reference
docs.text:
The generator reads only the named shared sources. It has no dependency on a separate configuration application or consumer workspace. From repository root:

python documentation/gh-io/tools/generate_parameters.py
python documentation/gh-io/tools/generate_parameters.py --check

The check compares the exact source-qualified union with generated row markers, rejects duplicate JSON keys/reference rows and detects stale defaults, descriptions, aliases and inventory counts. A setting that is assigned twice in a template is reported once, with both lines.

Targeted regression tests:

python -m unittest discover -s environment_setup/unit-tests/test-bicep/unit -p test_parameter_documentation.py -v

docs.title: Source coverage
docs.text:
Source Unique public keys yaml 411 env 409 bootstrap 93 helper 17 state 47 json.dev 419

Counts are source-qualified: a spelling present in YAML and JSON is covered in each source, not counted as two settings. Repeated template assignments are consolidated below (last assignment wins).

  • Source duplicate: env:ADMIN_COMMON_RESOURCE_SUFFIX, lines 159, 435; one reference row.
  • Source duplicate: env:ADMIN_PRJ_RESOURCE_SUFFIX, lines 160, 436; one reference row.
  • Source duplicate: env:USE_COMMON_ACR_OVERRIDE, lines 437, 461; one reference row.

docs.title: YAML and variables.json reference
docs.text: Exact YAML keys are under variables:; JSON paths are <section>.<key>. Y = YAML assignment; J.section = JSON value. JSON quoting and scalar types are preserved. A missing source is explicitly marked. GHA names include workflow bindings, fallbacks and reviewed template counterparts. A GHA name can be a fallback rather than an equal of the YAML key, so read the workflow before you swap one for the other.

docs.title: Services and feature switches

See esml-common/ai-gateway/apim/README.md. apimGatewayResourceGroup APIM_GATEWAY_RESOURCE_GROUP C Y: ""J.dev: "" Resource group containing the existing APIM service. Required by the separate AI gateway workflow when APIM is enabled. apimGatewayRetryCount APIM_GATEWAY_RETRY_COUNT O Y: "2"J.dev: "2" Sets how many times APIM retries after a backend answers 429 (throttled), from 1 to 50. Used only when ENABLE_APIM is true. The AI gateway pipeline reads it from variables.yaml or the GitHub variables, not from variables.json. apimGatewayServiceName APIM_GATEWAY_SERVICE_NAME C Y: ""J.dev: "" Existing APIM service with system-assigned managed identity enabled.
