docs.title: Parameters - required inputs
docs.text:
This checklist has the inputs you need for the orchestrator and the environment you chose. The complete reference has every setting with its default and its name in each format.

M means mandatory. C means required only when its condition applies. A default can fill a mandatory setting. Replace the placeholders with your own values.

The tools ask for these inputs when you create a Factory: see Create your AI Factory. The tables below give the names the pipelines use.

docs.title: Before editing
docs.text: Decide first Why it matters A new Factory, or a repository that was set up with v1.24 They are changed in different ways. Dev, Stage or Prod Each environment you deploy needs its own subscription, network range and pipeline access. GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps GitHub uses environments and variables. Azure DevOps uses service connections. Which services A service can need other services, more permissions and more budget.

docs.title: Scope, naming and project
docs.text:
M/C YAML / JSON key GitHub Actions key What to review M tenantId TENANT_ID Azure deployment tenant M dev_sub_id DEV_SUBSCRIPTION_ID Dev subscription and deployment identity permissions M admin_location, admin_locationSuffix AIFACTORY_LOCATION, AIFACTORY_LOCATION_SHORT Template region eastus2, suffix eus2; change together M admin_aifactorySuffixRG AIFACTORY_SUFFIX Template scale-set suffix -001; select the intended factory M project_number_000 PROJECT_NUMBER Three-digit project number, initially 001 M technical_admins_ad_object_id PROJECT_MEMBERS Entra object IDs; use group IDs when use_ad_groups / USE_AD_GROUPS=true M runNetworkingVar RUN_JOB1_NETWORKING Defaults true; skip only after confirming existing project networking C test_sub_id, prod_sub_id STAGE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, PROD_SUBSCRIPTION_ID Required for the environments you deploy. Use separate subscriptions to isolate Stage and Prod from Dev

Choose the resource-name prefix before you create the Factory. The templates have different defaults: admin_aifactoryPrefixRG is mrvel-1- in YAML and JSON, and AIFACTORY_PREFIX is acme-ai for GitHub.

docs.title: Orchestrator and identity
docs.text:
M/C Inputs Condition / guidance C GITHUB_USERNAME, GITHUB_NEW_REPO GHA repository setup; use owner/repo. Generic template visibility is public; inspect it before creation C azureDevOpsTenantId, dev_service_connection ADO route; organization tenant may differ from Azure deployment tenant C test_service_connection, prod_service_connection and corresponding *_seeding_kv_service_connection Only for deployed environments; use the actual authorized service-connection names M dev_admin_bicep_input_keyvault_subscription, dev_admin_bicep_kv_fw_rg, dev_admin_bicep_kv_fw Dev seeding-vault coordinates; GHA uses AIFACTORY_SEEDING_KEYVAULT_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, AIFACTORY_SEEDING_KEYVAULT_RG, AIFACTORY_SEEDING_KEYVAULT_NAME C Corresponding test_admin_bicep_* / prod_admin_bicep_* vault coordinates Stage/Prod when deployed; GHA environment overrides are not separate template names C azure_machinelearning_sp_oid / TENANT_AZUREML_OID and AZURE_MACHINELEARNING_SP_OID Required by the applicable Foundry/ML path; enterprise-application object ID, not application/client ID C databricksOID / DATABRICKS_OID Databricks enabled C Common/project service-principal secret-name fields Existing-SP/seeding route only. Federated managed-identity bootstrap can leave legacy secret references empty

AZURE_CLIENT_ID selects the federated identity of the GitHub workflows. Keep client secrets, personal access tokens and certificates out of the files you commit. Put them in the seeding Key Vault and name the secret in the setting.

docs.title: Network and service dependencies
docs.text:
M/C Inputs Condition / guidance M common_vnet_cidr, common subnet CIDRs; dev_cidr_range, test_cidr_range, prod_cidr_range Shared templates use 172.16.XX.0/18 with aligned 0 / 64 / 128; GHA uses COMMON_*_CIDR and DEV_CIDR_RANGE / STAGE_CIDR_RANGE / PROD_CIDR_RANGE C privDnsSubscription_param, privDnsResourceGroup_param Required when centralDnsZoneByPolicyInHub=true; GHA uses PRIV_DNS_SUBSCRIPTION_PARAM, PRIV_DNS_RESOURCE_GROUP_PARAM C Existing VNet/subnet identifiers Required when BYO_subnets / BYO_SUBNETS=true, and for each enabled service's subnet C project_IP_whitelist / PROJECT_MEMBERS_IP_ADDRESS The IP addresses that may reach the services, with hybrid or public networking C cmkKeyName / CMK_KEY_NAME, vault protection and permissions CMK enabled; review the relevant service's CMK exclusions C admin_aiSearchTier, admin_semanticSearchTier AI Search enabled; defaults basic and free. Search SKU free is incompatible with Private Link C Foundry + capability host + Storage + AI Search + Cosmos DB Required together for private Foundry agents that keep their data in your own resources

For private Foundry agents, switch these on together: enableAIFoundry / ENABLE_AI_FOUNDRY, enableAFoundryCaphost / ENABLE_FOUNDRY_CAPHOST, enableAISearch / ENABLE_AI_SEARCH, and enableCosmosDB / ENABLE_COSMOS_DB.

The two hub settings choose the hub mode. Both false is Standalone. enableAIFactoryHub=true is Own hub. centralDnsZoneByPolicyInHub=true is External hub, and it wins when both are true. See Hub and network modes.

docs.title: Optional Factory MCP and AI Gateway
docs.text:
You need these inputs only when you switch on the Factory MCP server or the AI gateway for project 001 in Dev.

Input Required when enableAIFactoryMCP plus Foundry and Container Apps Hosting the read-only Factory MCP. aifactoryMcpImage, aifactoryMcpApiImage MCP hosting; supply approved digest-pinned images from the expected registry. aifactoryMcpEntraAppId MCP hosting; an administrator prepares the app registration and required role. enableAIGatewaySKU plus Foundry Creating/adopting the dedicated AI Gateway integration. aiGatewaySkuResourceId Adopting an existing gateway rather than creating one. addAIFactoryMCP2AIGatewaySKU plus both components Registering MCP on the gateway. aiGatewaySkuOutboundSubnetId Registration with a new gateway; an adopted gateway must already have suitable outbound networking. aifactoryMcpClassicApimResourceIds Optional, with MCP hosting: classic APIM gateways that call the MCP with their system-assigned identity; an administrator assigns AiFactory.Mcp.Read to each identity. addAIFactoryMCP2APIM plus the apimGateway* APIM Publishing the MCP on the AI gateway pipeline's classic APIM: the project step admits the APIM identity, then the AI gateway pipeline deploys the MCP API and client subscription aifactory-mcp-client. aifactoryMcpContainerAppResourceId Optional, with MCP hosting: adopt an MCP app deployed outside the pipeline; only its caller lists grow.

The step prints, for each MCP caller, the exact admin-run command for the Microsoft Graph Bicep template esml-common/ai-gateway/entra/aifactory-mcp-app-role.bicep that assigns AiFactory.Mcp.Read; no pipeline writes Microsoft Graph.

All three switches are false by default, and false skips the step. See MCP and AI gateway. The pooled API Management gateway, Kong and Application Gateway have their own settings.

Earlier way: the launcher scripts

docs.title: Inputs of the launcher scripts
docs.text:
The launcher scripts read their inputs from environment variables that start with AIF_, ADO_ or GITHUB_. The region prompt of the create script defaults to swedencentral, while the templates default to eastus2. Simple mode sets more of the inputs for you. You give a host name, a backend and a certificate only when simple mode deploys an Application Gateway.

All inputs are in the launcher reference. Before you start a run, read which Factory, project and environment it targets and which delete settings are true.

The variables.json of a project that the Factory API created has two sections, dev and stage_prod. The template in the repository has a dev section only. See the two formats.

Create uses version 124 unless you give another, and update keeps the version that was saved. Name main to use the current development version.

docs.title: Every variable in variables.json
docs.text:
variables.json holds the settings of an AI Factory project and its scale set. This page lists all 419 variables of the shared template (section dev), with the default value and what each one does.

Change a variable through a tool, not by hand: see change a setting. For the matching Azure DevOps and GitHub names, see the complete reference.

Required says whether you must set the variable: Yes, No, or Depends when another choice decides it. A default in quotes is text: "true" and "false" are written as text in this file.

The project pipelines read variables.json. The separate AI gateway pipeline does not: it reads the apimGateway… and kongGateway… settings from variables.yaml (Azure DevOps) or the GitHub variables.

Group Variables Services and feature switches 98 Factory, project, naming and orchestration 104 Networking, DNS and existing resources 54 Operations, diagnostics and lifecycle 26 Per-environment SKUs and compute sizing 84 Identity, access and encryption 37 Models and deployments 16

docs.title: Services and feature switches
docs.text: Variable Default Required What it does AMLStudioUIPrivate "true" No AML Studio UI private access otherwise: false, only data plane is private; control plane is public. ENABLE_APIM "false" No Deploy APIM Azure OpenAI pool, token guard, 429-aware backend circuit breakers, and API policy. ENABLE_KONG "false" No Deploys Kong as an optional private edge proxy to APIM. acr_SKU "Premium" Yes ACR SKU mandatory: ACR SKU ensure: Premium required for private endpoints and CMK support. acr_adminUserEnabled "false" No ACR admin user enabled recommended: false, disable admin user for security. otherwise: true, enable for simpler dev access. acr_dedicated "true" Yes ACR dedicated (Premium tier) mandatory: ACR dedicated (Premium tier) ensure: must be true when using private endpoints or CMK. addAIFactoryMCP2AIGatewaySKU "false" No Opt-in project001 Dev registration of the Factory MCP tool server on the AI Gateway. Requires both components, private outbound reachability and administrator-granted access. False skips registration; it does not delete existing resources. addAIFactoryMCP2APIM "false" No Opt-in publication of the project001 Dev Factory MCP on the AI gateway pipeline's existing classic APIM (apimGateway* settings): the project step adds the APIM identity to the MCP callers, then the AI gateway pipeline deploys the MCP API and client subscription. Requires enableAIFactoryMCP and an administrator-granted app role. False skips both steps; it does not delete the API or the subscription. addAIFoundry "false" No Add new AI Foundry instance with new name otherwise: true, provisions a new AI Foundry with a new random name (for debugging or re-run) to get a fresh start. Still you should delete the old instance. addAIFoundryHub "false" No DEPRECATED. Do not enable. keep-as-is: DEPRECATED. Do not enable. addAISearch "false" No Add new AI Search instance otherwise: false, CreateIfNotExists logic. addAzureMachineLearning "false" No Add new Azure ML workspace addBastionHost "false" No Add Bastion Host in common RG apimGatewayAggregateTpm "" Depends 80-90% of the summed TPM across all GPT-5.5 backends. Required by the separate AI gateway workflow when APIM is enabled. apimGatewayApiId "azure-openai-gpt55" No Names the APIM API that the AI gateway pipeline creates for the pooled Azure OpenAI endpoint. Used only when ENABLE_APIM is true. The AI gateway pipeline reads it from variables.yaml or the GitHub variables, not from variables.json. apimGatewayApiPath "openai" No Sets the URL path of the AI gateway API in APIM; clients call that path. Letters, digits, underscore and hyphen, with a slash between segments. Used only when ENABLE_APIM is true. The AI gateway pipeline reads it from variables.yaml or the GitHub variables, not from variables.json. apimGatewayAssignOpenAIUserRole "false" No Requires roleAssignments/write in every backend subscription. apimGatewayBackendPoolName "aoai-gpt55-pool" No Names the APIM backend pool that groups the Azure OpenAI backends listed in apimGatewayBackendsJson. Used only when ENABLE_APIM is true. The AI gateway pipeline reads it from variables.yaml or the GitHub variables, not from variables.json. apimGatewayBackendsJson "[]" Depends JSON array; see esml-common/ai-gateway/apim/README.md. Required by the separate AI gateway workflow when APIM is enabled. apimGatewayCallerTpm "10000" No Fair-use TPM allocation per APIM subscription. apimGatewayConfigFile "" No Consumer-relative APIM JSON for the reviewed runner (apimGatewayManagedProvisioning:'true') keep-as-is: Empty builds an existing-APIM configuration from the apimGateway* variables. Examples: copy_to_local_settings/ai-gateway/apim.*.example.json. apimGatewayManagedProvisioning "false" No Run APIM through the reviewed plan -> what-if -> apply runner, which can also provision a private StandardV2 APIM keep-as-is: false keeps the classic deploy step. See esml-common/ai-gateway/apim/README.md. apimGatewayResourceGroup "" Depends Resource group containing the existing APIM service. Required by the separate AI gateway workflow when APIM is enabled. apimGatewayRetryCount "2" No Sets how many times APIM retries after a backend answers 429 (throttled), from 1 to 50. Used only when ENABLE_APIM is true. The AI gateway pipeline reads it from variables.yaml or the GitHub variables, not from variables.json. apimGatewayServiceName "" Depends Existing APIM service with system-assigned managed identity enabled. Required by the separate AI gateway workflow when APIM is enabled. apimGatewaySku "StandardV2" No SKU for the regular APIM pool/policy route, distinct from the dedicated AIGateway component. Check current Azure SKU, network and circuit-breaker support before deployment; this route does not support Consumption circuit breakers. apimGatewaySkuCapacity 1 No Number of units of the API Management SKU. Check the limits of the SKU and size it from the load you measure. apimGatewaySubscriptionId "" No Subscription containing APIM. Empty uses the environment subscription. cleanFoundryCaphost "false" No Clean up capability host on deletion otherwise: false, leaves capability host and its resources (such as VMs) in place when deleting the Foundry project. databricksOID "<optional>_ObjectID" Depends Databricks object ID mandatory: if enableDatabricks:'true' ensure: find Databricks object ID in Entra ID. databricksPrivate "true" No Databricks private control plane otherwise: false, only data plane is private; control plane is public. disable_whitelisting_for_build_agents "false" No Disable runner IP whitelisting otherwise: true, skip whitelisting (use only if runner already has network access). elasticCompanyName "Organization" Depends Elastic Cloud company name mandatory: if enableElasticsearch:'true' elasticDeploymentSize "small" No Elasticsearch deployment size otherwise: "medium" or "large". elasticEmail "admin@example.com" Depends Elastic Cloud account email mandatory: if enableElasticsearch:'true' ensure: valid email address. elasticFirstName "AI" Depends Elastic Cloud contact first name mandatory: if enableElasticsearch:'true' elasticLastName "Factory" Depends Elastic Cloud contact last name mandatory: if enableElasticsearch:'true' elasticSku "ess-consumption-2024_Monthly" No Elastic Cloud SKU elasticType "ElasticCloud" No Elasticsearch deployment type otherwise: "SelfManagedOnAKS" (future support). enableAFoundryCaphost "true" Depends Lets private Foundry agents keep their threads, files and vectors in your own Storage, AI Search and Cosmos DB. Needs those three services and enableAIFoundry. enableAIDocIntelligence "false" No Deploy Azure AI Document Intelligence enableAIFactoryAgentLiveVoice "false" No Opt-in project001 Dev live voice for the AI Factory Agent chat: deploys the private chat application with Azure Voice Live on the project Foundry account and a pulsing voice orb. Requires enableFactoryChatAgent (voice alone fails the step), Container Apps, Foundry and AI Search, an Entra single-page-app registration and read-only reader object IDs. False skips the step; it does not delete resources or remove roles. enableAIFactoryCreatedDefaultProjectForAIFv2 "true" No AI Factory default project for AIFv2 otherwise: false, Azure creates a default project with additional CosmosDB, Storage, AI Search, and connections. enableAIFactoryHub false No Own AI Factory Hub intent enableAIFactoryMCP "false" No Opt-in project001 Dev Factory MCP hosting through the matching project pipeline. Requires Foundry, Container Apps, approved image digests and an Entra application. False skips the step; it does not delete existing resources. enableAIFoundry "true" Depends Deploys the Microsoft Foundry account and project. Private agents also need enableAFoundryCaphost, AI Search, Cosmos DB and Storage. Check that your region offers the models you want. enableAIFoundryHub "false" No DEPRECATED. AI Foundry Hub (V1) service. Do not enable. Use enableAIFoundry instead. keep-as-is: DEPRECATED. AI Foundry Hub (V1) service. Do not enable. Use enableAIFoundry instead. enableAIGatewaySKU "false" No Opt-in project001 Dev dedicated AI Gateway create/adopt integration. Requires Foundry and the component prerequisites. Not the regular APIM/Kong route. False skips the step; it does not delete existing resources. enableAISearch "true" Depends Required capability-host vector store for private Foundry standard agents. mandatory: Required capability-host vector store for private Foundry standard agents. Required together for private Foundry agents that keep their data in your own resources. enableAISearchSharedPrivateLink "true" No AI Search shared private link otherwise: false, creates a private endpoint in the project vNet. enableAIServices "false" No DEPRECATED. Standalone AI Services account with Azure OpenAI endpoint. Do not enable. Use enableAIFoundry instead. keep-as-is: DEPRECATED. Standalone AI Services account with Azure OpenAI endpoint. Do not enable. Use enableAIFoundry instead. enableAKS "false" No Deploy standalone AKS cluster in project RG enableAMPLS "false" No Enable AMPLS in Hub otherwise: true, AMPLS created in Hub subscription; AppInsights in private/private mode. enableAdminVM "false" No Enable Admin VM in common RG enableAksForAzureML "false" No Deploy AKS for Azure ML inference enableAppInsightsDashboard "false" No Deploy Application Insights dashboard enableApplicationInsights "true" No Deploy project Application Insights enableAzureAIVision "false" No Deploy Azure AI Vision enableAzureMachineLearning "false" No Deploy Azure ML workspace enableAzureMcpServer "false" No Private, read-only MCP deployment; requires prepared project-scoped configuration. enableAzureOpenAI "false" No Deploy standalone Azure OpenAI enableAzureSpeech "false" No Deploy Azure AI Speech enableBing "false" No Deploy Bing Search enableBingCustomSearch "false" No Deploy Bing Custom Search enableBotService "true" No Deploy Azure Bot Service keep-as-is: Required for Microsoft Foundry agent scenarios. enableContainerApps "false" No Deploy Azure Container Apps enableContentSafety "false" No Deploy Azure AI Content Safety enableCosmosDB "true" Depends Required capability-host thread and agent-history store for private Foundry standard agents. mandatory: Required capability-host thread and agent-history store for private Foundry standard agents. Required together for private Foundry agents that keep their data in your own resources. enableDatabricks "false" No Deploy Databricks workspace enableDatafactory "false" No Deploy Azure Data Factory in project RG enableDatafactoryCommon "false" No Deploy Azure Data Factory in common RG enableDefenderforAIResourceLevel "false" No Defender for AI at resource level otherwise: true, enable Microsoft Defender for AI at per-resource level. enableDefenderforAISubLevel "false" No Defender for AI at subscription level otherwise: true, enable Microsoft Defender for AI at subscription level. enableDeleteForDisabledResources "false" No Decides what happens to a service that is switched off but exists in Azure. false, the default: the pipeline leaves it alone. true: the next run of the project pipeline deletes, in the project resource group, the resources that have the AI Factory name of a switched-off service, before it deploys the rest. It keeps Key Vault, storage accounts, Application Insights, dashboards and managed identities, and never touches the common resource group. Databases go with their data, and it purges deleted Foundry, AI Services, Azure OpenAI and Azure Machine Learning resources, which cannot be undone. Review the switched-off services before you set it to true. enableElasticsearch "false" No Deploy Elasticsearch keep-as-is: Elastic Cloud managed service. enableEncryptionAtHost "true" No Defender for Cloud encryption at host on new VMs and AKS node pools keep-as-is: Needs the subscription feature Microsoft.Compute/EncryptionAtHost (the bootstrap registers it). Existing VMs are never changed; false opts out. enableEventHubs "false" No Deploy Azure Event Hubs enableFactoryChatAgent "false" No Opt-in creation or versioning of the owned Enterprise Scale AI Factory prompt Agent in the selected project Foundry. Requires Foundry and a succeeded modelGPTXName deployment. False skips the step; it does not delete an existing Agent. enableFunction "false" No Deploy Azure Function App enableLogicApps "false" No Deploy Azure Logic Apps enablePersonas false No True selects groups-v1; false preserves configured legacy human/group grants. enablePostgreSQL "false" No Deploy Azure PostgreSQL enableProjectVM false No Turns on a private virtual machine in the project resource group, on the default subnet. An existing VM is not redeployed. enableRedisCache "false" No Deploy Azure Cache for Redis enableRedisManaged false No Independent private, Entra-only Azure Managed Redis. enableRetries "false" No Enable automatic job retries otherwise: true, enable automatic retries on failure for GenAI services deployment. enableSQLDatabase "false" No Deploy Azure SQL Database enableVmBackup "false" No Azure Backup for the admin and project VMs otherwise: true, creates or reuses a Recovery Services vault with a daily Enhanced policy and protects the VM. enableWebApp "false" No Deploy Azure Web App foundryApiManagementResourceId "" No APIM resource ID for Foundry integration otherwise: provide existing API Management resource ID to integrate with Microsoft Foundry. foundryDeploymentType "2" No <deprecated>Retained for configuration compatibility. AI Foundry now always uses the second-option account deployment. kongGatewayApimHost "" Depends APIM gateway hostname without protocol/path. Required by the separate AI gateway workflow when Kong is enabled; the consumer API key is an environment secret. kongGatewayCpu 2 No Sets the CPU cores of the Kong gateway container, as a whole number. Used only when ENABLE_KONG is true. The AI gateway pipeline reads it from variables.yaml or the GitHub variables, not from variables.json. kongGatewayImage "kong/kong-gateway:3.9" No Sets the container image of the Kong gateway. Used only when ENABLE_KONG is true. The AI gateway pipeline reads it from variables.yaml or the GitHub variables, not from variables.json. kongGatewayMemoryGb 4 No Sets the memory of the Kong gateway container in GB, as a whole number. Used only when ENABLE_KONG is true. The AI gateway pipeline reads it from variables.yaml or the GitHub variables, not from variables.json. serviceSettingDeployProjectVM "false" No Deploy VM in project resource group otherwise: true, deploy a jumpbox VM for use with Azure Bastion. updateAIFoundry "false" No Update AI Foundry properties otherwise: true, re-run to update AI Foundry properties and RBAC. updateCommonACR "true" No Redeploy shared ACR settings and private endpoint otherwise: false reuses the existing registry without rewriting it; project access assignments remain enabled.

docs.title: Factory, project, naming and orchestration
docs.text: Variable Default Required What it does AZURE_CLIENT_ID "" No Preferred credentialless deployment identity: client ID of a federated app or user-assigned managed identity. When set, workflows use OIDC instead of AZURE_CREDENTIALS. GITHUB_NEW_REPO "" Yes New GitHub repository path mandatory: New GitHub repository path ensure: format: GITHUB_NEW_REPO_VISIBILITY "public" No New repository visibility otherwise: private or internal. GITHUB_TEMPLATE_REPO "azure/enterprise-scale-aifactory" No GitHub template repository keep-as-is: Leave as-is if BYO repo. GITHUB_USERNAME "" Yes GitHub username or org mandatory: GitHub username or org GITHUB_USE_SSH "false" No Use SSH for git operations otherwise: true, use SSH instead of HTTPS. aca_w_registry_image "mcr.microsoft.com/azuredocs/containerapps-helloworld:latest" No Container Apps default image otherwise: replace with your own ACR image. adminUsername "esmladmin" No VM admin username admin_aiSearchTier "basic" Yes AI Search SKU tier mandatory: AI Search SKU tier ensure: 'free' is not allowed when using private endpoints. ['free', 'basic', 'standard', 'standard2', 'standard3', 'storage_optimized_l1', 'storage_optimized_l2'] admin_aifactoryPrefixRG "mrvel-1-" No AI Factory resource group prefix keep-as-is: Max 6 chars. otherwise: set your company prefix, e.g. "acme-ai-", "contoso-". admin_aifactorySuffixRG "-001" Yes AI Factory scaleset suffix mandatory: AI Factory scaleset suffix keep-as-is: For 1st scaleset. otherwise: increment to '-002', '-003' for additional scalesets. admin_commonResourceSuffix "-001" No Common resources suffix otherwise: change to reprovision new services in the same common RG while keeping old ones. admin_hybridBenefit "false" No Azure Hybrid Benefit for VMs otherwise: true, if you have eligible Windows licenses with Software Assurance (pay-as-you-go avoided). admin_ip_fw "" No Leave empty. Will be automatically set by the pipeline to the build agent IP. keep-as-is: Leave empty. Will be automatically set by the pipeline to the build agent IP. admin_keyvaultSoftDeleteDays 7 Depends Key Vault soft delete days mandatory: if cmk:'true' (purge protection required). otherwise: 90 days recommended; 0 to disable. admin_location "eastus2" Yes Azure region mandatory: Azure region admin_locationSuffix "eus2" Yes Region short name mandatory: Region short name admin_prjResourceSuffix "-001" No Project resources suffix otherwise: change to reprovision new services in the same project RG while keeping old ones. admin_projectType "all" Yes Selects the project type that sizes the project subnets: all (every subnet), genai-1 or esml. Any other value fails the networking step. Keep all. admin_semanticSearchTier "free" Yes Semantic search tier mandatory: Semantic search tier aiGatewaySkuResourceId "" No Resource ID of an existing AI Gateway SKU to adopt (never modified) keep-as-is: Empty creates an owned gateway in the project resource group. aiSearchFallbackLocationArrayDev ["francecentral","denmarkeast","italynorth","norwayeast","germanywestcentral"] No Up to five Search fallback regions in order, Germany last; [] or blank disables regional fallback independently of SKU retries. aiSearchFallbackLocationArrayStageProd ["francecentral","denmarkeast","italynorth","norwayeast","germanywestcentral"] No Up to five Search fallback regions for Test/Stage and Prod in order, Germany last; [] or blank disables regional fallback. Only Search service placement changes. aiSearchLocation "" No AI Search region override. Empty keeps the project region; use another supported region only when regional Search capacity is unavailable. aifactory-dash-01 "" No Existing Azure Portal AI Factory dashboard URL; never deploys a dashboard. aifactoryAgentConfigFile "" No Your own AI Factory Agent configuration (JSON, relative to the repository root, e.g. aifactory/agent/project001-dev.json) merged over the generated one keep-as-is: Tunes voice (realtime mode, languages), grants, costs and limits; never scopes, azure, location or the Entra client. Required to let the pipeline manage an app first deployed with 40-aifactory-agent/deploy.py. Only read when enableAIFactoryAgentLiveVoice:'true'. aifactoryAgentContainerAppsEnvironment "" No Name of the internal project Container Apps environment hosting the agent chat keep-as-is: Empty selects the single environment in the project resource group. aifactoryAgentEntraAppId "" Depends Client ID (GUID) of the dedicated Entra single-page-app registration used for sign-in to the agent chat mandatory: if enableAIFactoryAgentLiveVoice:'true'. Created once by an Entra admin with python -m aifactory_agent.browser_auth (SPA redirect URI = the application's HTTPS root, delegated scope access_as_user). Pipelines never write Microsoft Graph. aifactoryAgentReaderObjectIds "" Depends Comma-separated Entra object IDs (GUIDs) granted read-only chat access (knowledge.read, factory.read) in this project's Dev mandatory: if enableAIFactoryAgentLiveVoice:'true'. Write, delete and cost permissions are never granted by the pipeline. aifactoryAgentVoiceLanguages "" No Comma-separated speech input languages (BCP-47) for live voice keep-as-is: Empty uses en-US. Swedish needs an explicit entry such as sv-SE,en-US. Only read when enableAIFactoryAgentLiveVoice:'true'. aifactoryAgentVoiceName "" No Azure Speech voice used for spoken answers keep-as-is: Empty uses en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural. Only read when enableAIFactoryAgentLiveVoice:'true'. aifactoryMcpApiImage "" Depends Digest-pinned Factory API sidecar image mandatory: if enableAIFactoryMCP:'true'. Same format as aifactoryMcpImage. aifactoryMcpClassicApimResourceIds "" No Comma-separated resource IDs of classic API Management gateways (Microsoft.ApiManagement/service) allowed to call the AI Factory MCP keep-as-is: Requires enableAIFactoryMCP:'true'. Each APIM is only read (never modified); its system-assigned managed identity is added to the MCP application callers. An Entra admin assigns app role AiFactory.Mcp.Read to each identity; pipelines never write Microsoft Graph. aifactoryMcpContainerAppResourceId "" No Optional adoption of an AI Factory MCP Container App deployed outside the pipeline, in the project resource group. Only its caller lists grow; images, identity, secrets and ingress are never changed. Empty uses the pipeline-managed app. aifactoryMcpContainerAppsEnvironment "" No Name of the internal project Container Apps environment hosting the MCP keep-as-is: Empty selects the single environment in the project resource group. aifactoryMcpEntraAppId "" Depends Client ID (GUID) of the MCP API app registration exposing app role AiFactory.Mcp.Read mandatory: if enableAIFactoryMCP:'true'. Created once by an Entra admin; pipelines never write Microsoft Graph. aifactoryMcpImage "" Depends Digest-pinned AI Factory MCP image mandatory: if enableAIFactoryMCP:'true'. Format aifactory_branch_chosen "release/v1.24" No Submodule release branch aifactory_mcp_AppID_seeding_kv_name "<optional>esml-project001-mcp-app-id" No Seeding Key Vault secret name holding the AI Factory MCP API app registration client ID, written by esml-util/29b-create-mcp-api-sp-for-projects.sh. The MCP step uses it when aifactoryMcpEntraAppId is empty. aifactory_salt "" No Leave empty, 5 characters. A deteministic unique value, from COMMON RG aifactory_salt_random "" No Leave empty. 10-character unique random value derived from User-Assigned Managed Identity. Auto-populated by the pipeline. keep-as-is: Leave empty. 10-character unique random value derived from User-Assigned Managed Identity. Auto-populated by the pipeline. aifactory_version_major "1" No AI Factory major version keep-as-is: Used to determine which bicep files to use. aifactory_version_minor "24" No AI Factory minor version keep-as-is: 2025-09-20: 24 = release/v1.24 aisearchRetryCapcityArray "true" No Validate all candidates' quota headroom and retry only Azure AI Search capacity failures. aseSku "IsolatedV2" No App Service Environment SKU keep-as-is: Used only if byoASEv3:'true' or a dedicated ASE is provisioned. aseSkuCode "I1v2" No App Service Environment SKU code aseSkuWorkers 1 No App Service Environment worker count bastion_custom_name "" No Bastion name override for common RG RBAC keep-as-is: Empty uses the standard Bastion naming convention. bastion_subscription_resource_group "" No Bastion resource group override for common RG RBAC keep-as-is: Empty uses the common resource group. bingCustomSearchSku "G2" No Bing Custom Search SKU keep-as-is: ['G2'] G2 is custom search with grounding. botEnableM365PublicEndpoint "false" No Turns on only the Microsoft-filtered M365 Activity route of the chosen agent on a private Foundry account when publishing is prepared. Account network settings stay unchanged. Needs botFoundryAgentName. Outside Dev it resets to false. botFoundryAgentName "" No Names an existing Foundry agent (its exact name, not a version ID) to prepare for M365 and Teams publishing. When set, no standalone Bot is created. Empty skips the step. Needs enableBotService. botFoundryProjectResourceId "" No Sets the full ARM ID of the Foundry project that holds the agent to prepare for publishing. Empty skips the step. Needs enableBotService. clusteringPolicyRedisManaged "OSSCluster" No OSSCluster|EnterpriseCluster|NoCluster commonLakeNamePrefixMax8chars "mrvel" No Data lake storage name prefix keep-as-is: Max 8 characters. commonResourceGroup_param "" No BYO common resource group name otherwise: provide a custom name for the common resource group. containerAppsRetryCapacityArray "true" No Retry only Container Apps capacity failures, with 240 seconds before attempts 2 and 3. cosmosKind "GlobalDocumentDB" No Cosmos DB kind otherwise: "MongoDB". datalakeName_param "" No BYO data lake storage account name otherwise: provide a custom storage account name. dev_admin_bicep_input_keyvault_subscription "<todo>_SubID" Yes DEV seeding KV subscription ID mandatory: DEV seeding KV subscription ID ensure: subscription where the DEV seeding Key Vault resides. dev_admin_bicep_kv_fw "<todo>_Name_Dev" Yes DEV seeding KV name mandatory: DEV seeding KV name ensure: Key Vault name storing secrets mapped to PROJECT_SERVICE_PRINCIPAL_KV_S_NAME_APPID. dev_admin_bicep_kv_fw_rg "<todo>_ResourceGroup_DEV" Yes DEV seeding KV resource group mandatory: DEV seeding KV resource group ensure: resource group where the DEV seeding Key Vault resides. dev_sub_id "<todo>_SubID" Yes DEV subscription ID mandatory: DEV subscription ID evictionPolicyRedisManaged "NoEviction" No Sets the Azure Managed Redis eviction policy: NoEviction (rejects writes when memory is full), AllKeysLFU, AllKeysLRU, AllKeysRandom, VolatileLFU, VolatileLRU, VolatileRandom or VolatileTTL. Used only when enableRedisManaged is true. functionRuntime "dotnet" No Azure Function runtime otherwise: "python", "node", "java", "powershell". functionVersion "v7.0" No Azure Function runtime version highAvailabilityRedisManaged "Enabled" No Enabled|Disabled; Enabled -> Disabled is unsupported. kvNameFromCOMMON_param "" No BYO common Key Vault name otherwise: provide a custom Key Vault name. lakeContainerName "lake3" No Data lake container name logicAppType "Standard" No Logic Apps hosting type org-department-id "" No Project organizational department ID keep-as-is: Text, max 128 characters, not necessarily a GUID; identical across environments. No identity or authentication effect. org-department-name "" No Project organizational department name keep-as-is: Unicode text, max 200 characters; identical across environments, independent of cost center. No factory inheritance or Azure tag writes. persona_access_manifest "" No Repository-relative reviewed manifest for this environment/project. persona_access_mode "legacy" No Derived from enablePersonas; mode-only opt-in is supported when the flag is absent. postGresAdminEmails "email_adress_only" Depends PostgreSQL admin emails mandatory: if enablePostgreSQL:'true' ensure: valid comma-separated email addresses. postgreSQLRetryCapacityArray "true" No Retry only PostgreSQL regional/SKU capacity failures, with 240 seconds before attempts 2 and 3. prod_admin_bicep_input_keyvault_subscription "<todo>_SubID" Depends PROD seeding KV subscription ID mandatory: PROD seeding KV subscription ID ensure: subscription where the PROD seeding Key Vault resides. Required when deploying that environment. prod_admin_bicep_kv_fw "<todo>_Name_Prod" Depends PROD seeding KV name mandatory: PROD seeding KV name ensure: Key Vault name storing secrets mapped to PROJECT_SERVICE_PRINCIPAL_KV_S_NAME_APPID. Required when deploying that environment. prod_admin_bicep_kv_fw_rg "<todo>_ResourceGroup_Prod" Depends PROD seeding KV resource group mandatory: PROD seeding KV resource group ensure: resource group where the PROD seeding Key Vault resides. Required when deploying that environment. prod_sub_id "<todo>_SubID" Depends PROD subscription ID recommended: separate subscription from DEV. otherwise: can reuse dev_sub_id. Required when deploying that environment. projectPrefix "esml-" No Project resource group prefix projectSuffix "-rg" No Project resource group suffix project_number_000 "001" Yes Project number mandatory: Project number keep-as-is: For 1st project. otherwise: increment to '002', '003', etc. skipDiagAISearch false No Skips creating the AI Search diagnostic setting; by default its logs go to Log Analytics. Set true when an Azure Policy already sends the same logs to the same workspace, which otherwise fails with a 409 conflict. skipDiagAIServices false No Skips creating the AI Services diagnostic setting for a new account when enableAIServices is true. Set true when an Azure Policy already sends the same logs to the same workspace. skipDiagAOAI true No Skips the Azure OpenAI diagnostic setting, because an Azure Policy usually manages it. Set false to create it from Bicep; applies when enableAzureOpenAI is true. skipDiagContentSafety true No Skips the Content Safety diagnostic setting, because an Azure Policy usually manages it. Set false to create it from Bicep; applies when enableContentSafety is true. skipDiagDocIntelligence true No Skips the Document Intelligence diagnostic setting, because an Azure Policy usually manages it. Set false to create it from Bicep; applies when enableAIDocIntelligence is true. skipDiagSpeech true No Skips the Speech diagnostic setting, because an Azure Policy usually manages it. Set false to create it from Bicep; applies when enableAzureSpeech is true. skipDiagVision true No Skips the Vision diagnostic setting, because an Azure Policy usually manages it. Set false to create it from Bicep; applies when enableAzureAIVision is true. tag_costcenter "1234" No Project cost center tag keep-as-is: Metadata for per-project cost tracking on resource group level. tag_costceter_common "9999" No Common cost center tag keep-as-is: Metadata for Resource group cost tracking. tag_repository "aifactory" No Repository name tag tag_repository_branch "aifactory-001" No Repository branch tag otherwise: per scaleset 'aifactory-002', or per project 'aifactory-001/project001-main'. tags "{\"CostCenter\":\"$(tag_costceter_common)\",\"Description\":\"AI Factory common\",\"AIF-Repo\":\"$(tag_repository)\",\"AIF-Branch\":\"$(tag_repository_branch)\",\"AIF-Version\":\"$(aifactory_version_major).$(aifactory_version_minor)\",\"AIF-Submodule-Chosen-Branch\":\"$(aifactory_branch_chosen)\",\"AIF-Scaleset\":\"$(admin_aifactorySuffixRG)\",\"AIF-Environment\":\"$(dev_test_prod)\",\"AIF-Project Owners\":\"$(technical_admins_email)\",\"AIFactory project\":\"$(project_number_000)\",\"AIF-Networking\":\"$(allowPublicAccessWhenBehindVnet),$(enablePublicGenAIAccess),$(enablePublicAccessWithPerimeter)\",\"AIF-enableAIFactoryCreatedDefaultProjectForAIFv2\":\"$(enableAIFactoryCreatedDefaultProjectForAIFv2)\",\"AIF-disableAgentNetworkInjection\":\"$(disableAgentNetworkInjection)\",\"AIF-byoASEv3\":\"$(byoASEv3)\",\"AIF-BYO_subnets\":\"$(BYO_subnets)\"}" No Common resource tags as a JSON string; Azure DevOps macro expressions are preserved. tagsProject "{\"CostCenter\":\"$(tag_costcenter)\",\"Description\":\"RAG Chat 1\",\"AIF-Branch\":\"$(tag_repository_branch)/project$(project_number_000)\",\"AIF-Scaleset\":\"$(admin_aifactorySuffixRG)\",\"AIF-Environment\":\"$(dev_test_prod)\",\"AIF-Project Owners\":\"$(technical_admins_email)\",\"AIFactory project\":\"$(project_number_000)\",\"AIF-Networking\":\"$(allowPublicAccessWhenBehindVnet),$(enablePublicGenAIAccess),$(enablePublicAccessWithPerimeter)\",\"AIF-enableAIFactoryCreatedDefaultProjectForAIFv2\":\"$(enableAIFactoryCreatedDefaultProjectForAIFv2)\",\"AIF-disableAgentNetworkInjection\":\"$(disableAgentNetworkInjection)\",\"AIF-byoASEv3\":\"$(byoASEv3)\",\"AIF-BYO_subnets\":\"$(BYO_subnets)\"}" No Project resource tags as a JSON string; Azure DevOps macro expressions are preserved. test_admin_bicep_input_keyvault_subscription "<todo>_SubID" Depends STAGE seeding KV subscription ID mandatory: STAGE seeding KV subscription ID ensure: subscription where the STAGE seeding Key Vault resides. Required when deploying that environment. test_admin_bicep_kv_fw "<todo>_Name_Test" Depends STAGE seeding KV name mandatory: STAGE seeding KV name ensure: Key Vault name storing secrets mapped to PROJECT_SERVICE_PRINCIPAL_KV_S_NAME_APPID. Required when deploying that environment. test_admin_bicep_kv_fw_rg "<todo>_ResourceGroup_Test" Depends STAGE seeding KV resource group mandatory: STAGE seeding KV resource group ensure: resource group where the STAGE seeding Key Vault resides. Required when deploying that environment. test_sub_id "<todo>_SubID" Depends STAGE subscription ID recommended: separate subscription from DEV. otherwise: can reuse dev_sub_id. Required when deploying that environment. useCommonACR "true" No Use shared ACR across projects otherwise: false, each project gets its own ACR (higher cost). useCommonACR_override "true" No Use shared ACR override otherwise: false, each project gets its own ACR (higher cost). webAppRuntime "python" No Azure Web App runtime otherwise: "dotnet", "node", "java". webAppRuntimeVersion "3.11" No Azure Web App runtime version

docs.title: Networking, DNS and existing resources
docs.text: Variable Default Required What it does BYOContributorRoleID "b24988ac-6180-42a0-ab88-20f7382dd24c" No Contributor role ID keep-as-is: Azure built-in Contributor. otherwise: provide a custom role ID for finer-grained access control. BYO_subnets "false" No Bring your own subnets otherwise: true, uses pre-existing subnets defined by the BYO subnet variables below. acr_IP_whitelist "" No ACR IP allowlist otherwise: provide comma-separated IPv4 addresses if ACR network restrictions are needed. aiGatewaySkuOutboundSubnetId "" Depends Subnet ID for AI Gateway outbound VNet integration mandatory: if addAIFactoryMCP2AIGatewaySKU:'true' with a new gateway. Delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms, /27 or larger. allowPublicAccessWhenBehindVnet "true" No Public UI access when behind vNet recommended: false to enable fully private networking. byoASEv3 "false" No Use BYO App Service Environment v3 otherwise: true, use an existing ASEv3 specified in byoAseFullResourceId. byoAseAppServicePlanResourceId "" No BYO App Service Plan resource ID otherwise: provide full ARM resource ID of an existing App Service Plan within the ASEv3. byoAseFullResourceId "subscriptions/...yourASEnameS2" Depends BYO ASEv3 ARM resource ID. Note - remove leading slash / in Resource ID mandatory: if byoASEv3:'true' ensure: full ARM resource ID of the existing ASEv3. centralDnsZoneByPolicyInHub false No Centralized DNS via Hub policy otherwise: true, uses central private DNS zones in HUB resource group managed by Azure Policy. common_bastion_subnet_cidr "172.16.XX.192/26" Yes Bastion subnet CIDR mandatory: Bastion subnet CIDR keep-as-is: XX replaced by the selected environment range. ensure: within common_vnet_cidr. common_bastion_subnet_name "AzureBastionSubnet" Yes Bastion subnet name mandatory: Bastion subnet name keep-as-is: Required name for Azure Bastion. ensure: within common_vnet_cidr. common_pbi_subnet_cidr "172.16.XX.128/26" Yes Power BI gateway subnet CIDR mandatory: Power BI gateway subnet CIDR keep-as-is: XX replaced by the selected environment range. ensure: within common_vnet_cidr. common_pbi_subnet_name "snet-esml-cmn-pbi-001" Yes Power BI gateway subnet name mandatory: Power BI gateway subnet name ensure: within common_vnet_cidr. common_subnet_cidr "172.16.XX.0/26" Yes Common subnet CIDR mandatory: Common subnet CIDR keep-as-is: XX replaced by the selected environment range. ensure: within common_vnet_cidr. common_subnet_name "snet-esml-cmn-001" No Common subnet name common_subnet_scoring_cidr "172.16.XX.64/26" Yes Scoring subnet CIDR mandatory: Scoring subnet CIDR keep-as-is: XX replaced by the selected environment range. ensure: within common_vnet_cidr. common_vnet_cidr "172.16.XX.0/18" Yes Common vNet CIDR mandatory: Common vNet CIDR keep-as-is: XX is the network-aligned per-environment octet; Dev/Stage/Prod must not overlap. Address intent only, not actual peering. dev_cidr_range "0" Yes DEV network-aligned XX value mandatory: DEV network-aligned XX value keep-as-is: VNet 172.16.0.0/18. disableAgentNetworkInjection "false" No Disable agent network injection keep-as-is: false, requires Container Apps subnet in 172.16.0.0/12 or 192.168.0.0/16. otherwise: true, disables network injection. disableSubnetJoinAction "false" No Disable VNet subnet join RBAC recommended: false, grants Network Contributor role for subnet join actions (required for APIM, Container Apps, AKS). otherwise: true, skip if subnet permissions managed externally. enablePublicAccessWithPerimeter "true" No Public access with network perimeter recommended: false to enable fully private networking. enablePublicGenAIAccess "true" No Public GenAI access (control plane) recommended: false to enable fully private networking. kongGatewaySubnetCidr "" Depends Dedicated, unused /28 or larger subnet. Required by the separate AI gateway workflow when Kong is enabled; the consumer API key is an environment secret. kongGatewaySubnetName "snet-kong-001" No Names the subnet that the pipeline creates for Kong in the existing VNet. Its range comes from kongGatewaySubnetCidr (/28 or larger). Used only when ENABLE_KONG is true. The AI gateway pipeline reads it from variables.yaml or the GitHub variables, not from variables.json. kongGatewayVnetName "" Depends Names the existing VNet where the Kong subnet is created. Required when ENABLE_KONG is true. The AI gateway pipeline reads it from variables.yaml or the GitHub variables, not from variables.json. kongGatewayVnetResourceGroup "" Depends Names the resource group of the existing VNet that holds the Kong subnet. Required when ENABLE_KONG is true. docs.title: Azure resource library
docs.text:
This library lists 54 Azure resources of an AI Factory. 50 of them have a setting that switches them on, for a project or for the common part. The others are always there, or are an integration. Each card names the setting, links to its explanation and says whether it is on by default.

Type in the search box, or tick the boxes. Ticks in one row widen the choice, and rows narrow each other. Full stack has what an application needs around its AI: the front end, databases, a cache, Container Apps, AKS and API Management.

docs.title: Always there
docs.text: Every project also gets a storage account, managed identities and its own subnets. The common part of a scale set has the network, the data lake, a container registry and Log Analytics. They have no switch.

docs.title: Switch a resource on or off
docs.text:
Change the setting with a tool: see Add and update, or pass settings to esaf.upsert_project(...) as in Enable ESAF Agent Chat. Every setting is explained in Every variable in variables.json.

Before you switch a resource off, read what happens when you switch a service off.

Looking for code that uses a resource? Open the code templates library, or select the link on a card. The architecture images use the same names.

docs.title: 18. Get started with Factory tools
docs.text:
19: Add and update | 20: Remove and recover

Choose one tool below. The whole tutorial changes with your choice on the documentation site.

6 common scenarios all tools support

The Configuration Wizard, CLI, REST API and Python SDK cover the same six common scenarios, one call each. See the six ESAF scenarios.

Note: It uses the new registered Azure Factory approach (v1.25 and higher). You need the prepared API and accelerator source folders from your platform team.

docs.title: Choose your tool
docs.text:
CLI (PowerShell)Python SDKREST (curl)

The CLI gives you ready-made commands to type in PowerShell. Start here if you do not want to write a program.

docs.title: 1. Start the local demo service in Window A
docs.text:
Open PowerShell. Enter your prepared API folder when asked.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$ApiRoot = Read-Host 'Full path to the prepared API folder'
$Python = Join-Path $ApiRoot '.venv\Scripts\python.exe'
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Python -PathType Leaf)) {
    throw 'Ask your platform team to complete API setup first.'
}
Set-Location -LiteralPath $ApiRoot
$env:AIFACTORY_API_KEY = 'example-local-parity-smoke-only'
& $Python -m uvicorn src.api:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8876

Leave Window A running. The example key is only for this local demo. Do not use it for a real factory.

docs.title: 2. Set up Window B
docs.text:
Open a second PowerShell window and paste this entire block. Variables are not shared between windows.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$ApiRoot = Read-Host 'API folder used in Window A'
$AcceleratorRoot = Read-Host 'Accelerator source folder'
$Python = Join-Path $ApiRoot '.venv\Scripts\python.exe'
$SdkSource = Join-Path $AcceleratorRoot 'environment_setup\azurefactory-cli\src'
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Python -PathType Leaf) -or
    -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $SdkSource 'azurefactory\client.py'))) {
    throw 'Check the API and accelerator folders.'
}
$env:PYTHONPATH = $SdkSource
$env:AIFACTORY_API_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:8876'
$env:AIFACTORY_API_KEY = 'example-local-parity-smoke-only'
$DemoRoot = Join-Path $env:TEMP ('factory-smoke-' + [guid]::NewGuid())
$env:FACTORY_FOLDER = Join-Path $DemoRoot 'azurefactory'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $env:FACTORY_FOLDER | Out-Null

docs.title: 3. Check the connection
docs.text:
& $Python -m azurefactory health
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'The service is not reachable.' }
& $Python -m azurefactory catalog list --folder $env:FACTORY_FOLDER
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'The factory list could not be read.' }

Expect a healthy service and an empty factory list. You have not created a factory yet. You are finished; no developer tests are required. Stop the idle demo service with Ctrl+C in Window A.

More info

If port 8876 is busy, use a free port in both windows; do not stop an unrelated service. 127.0.0.1 means your own computer. The normal API source default is 8765; a desktop app can use a different port.

Optional compatibility information, while Window A is running:

& $Python -m azurefactory doctor
& $Python -m azurefactory schema --openapi
& $Python -m azurefactory bootstrap capabilities

These checks do not guarantee that an Azure deployment will succeed. Python is used here to launch the existing CLI package without requiring a separate azurefactory.exe installation.

docs.title: 4. Next: the six scenarios, one command each
docs.text:
With a real factory folder, each scenario is one command. The connection is set once: the same AIFACTORY_API_URL and AIFACTORY_API_KEY, plus ESAF_FOLDER, the absolute azurefactory folder on the API host. List the commands, without running any of them on this empty demo folder:

$env:ESAF_FOLDER = $env:FACTORY_FOLDER
& $Python -m azurefactory esaf --help
Scenario Command 1. Init AI Factory azurefactory esaf init-factory 2. Add scaleset azurefactory esaf add-scale-set 002 dev --cidr 10.141.0.0/16 3. Add or update project azurefactory esaf upsert-project 002 dev 4. Delete project azurefactory esaf delete-project 002 dev 5. Delete scaleset azurefactory esaf delete-scale-set 002 dev 6. Delete AI Factory azurefactory esaf delete-factory

Each command is the approval and changes Azure; add --wait to follow the job to its end. The environment (dev, stage, prod) is required on scale-set and project commands. Guide 19 runs Scenarios 1-3 and guide 20 Scenarios 4-6.

The SDK provides Python helpers for your scripts or applications. These are ordinary Python examples: save them as .py files or run them in your Python editor. No PowerShell strings are involved.

docs.title: 1. Start the local demo service
docs.text:
If your platform team already started the demo service, go to step 2. Otherwise save this as start_factory_demo.py. In your editor, select the prepared API folder's .venv Python interpreter, then run this file.

import os
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import uvicorn

api_root = Path(input("Prepared API source folder: ").strip()).resolve()
if not (api_root / "src" / "api.py").is_file():
    raise SystemExit("Select the prepared API source folder.")

os.chdir(api_root)
sys.path.insert(0, str(api_root))
os.environ["AIFACTORY_API_KEY"] = "example-local-parity-smoke-only"
uvicorn.run("src.api:app", host="127.0.0.1", port=8876)

Leave it running. The key above is for this empty local demo only.

docs.title: 2. Run a real Python example
docs.text:
Open another editor terminal or Python process. Save this as factory_smoke.py and run it with Python 3.10 or later. Enter the accelerator source folder and the demo key when asked. You can also use the ready-to-run Python file.

import getpass
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tempfile

accelerator = Path(input("Accelerator source folder: ").strip()).resolve()
sdk_source = accelerator / "environment_setup" / "azurefactory-cli" / "src"
if not (sdk_source / "azurefactory" / "client.py").is_file():
    raise SystemExit("The selected folder does not contain the Factory SDK.")
sys.path.insert(0, str(sdk_source))

from azurefactory import AzureFactoryClient

url = input("Demo API URL [http://127.0.0.1:8876]: ").strip() or "http://127.0.0.1:8876"
key = getpass.getpass("Demo API key: ")
if not key:
    raise SystemExit("Enter the local demo key.")
client = AzureFactoryClient(base_url=url, api_key=key)

print(json.dumps(client.health(), indent=2))
folder = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="factory-smoke-")) / "azurefactory"
folder.mkdir()
print(f"Empty local demo folder: {folder}")
print(json.dumps(client.catalog_list(str(folder)), indent=2))

Expect a healthy service and an empty factory list. No extra test step is required. Stop your idle demo service when finished.

More info

The SDK sends HTTP requests to the API service; it does not replace that service. This example imports the reviewed SDK source without installing packages. The SDK itself uses Python's standard library.

If the package is already installed in your selected interpreter, omit the source-folder prompt and sys.path setup and start with:

from azurefactory import AzureFactoryClient

client = AzureFactoryClient()  # Uses AIFACTORY_API_URL and AIFACTORY_API_KEY.
print(client.health())

Set those environment variables through your approved secret mechanism. Do not put a real API key in a Python file or notebook you share. The local temporary folder works because the API runs on the same computer.

docs.title: 3. Next: the six scenarios, one call each
docs.text:
With a real factory folder, each scenario is one method of from azurefactory import esaf. The connection is set once with esaf.connect() (or the variables ESAF_FOLDER, AIFACTORY_API_URL and AIFACTORY_API_KEY). Add these lines to the end of factory_smoke.py to connect esaf to the demo folder and read it; they change nothing:

from azurefactory import esaf

session = esaf.connect(folder=str(folder), url=url, api_key=key)
print(session.client.catalog_list(session.folder)["factories"])
print(esaf.__all__)
Scenario Method 1. Init AI Factory esaf.init_factory() 2. Add scaleset esaf.add_scale_set("002", "dev", cidr="10.141.0.0/16") 3. Add or update project esaf.upsert_project("002", "dev") 4. Delete project esaf.delete_project("002", "dev") 5. Delete scaleset esaf.delete_scale_set("002", "dev") 6. Delete AI Factory esaf.delete_factory()

Each method is the approval and changes Azure, so do not call them on this demo folder. Each returns a job: job.wait() follows it to its end. The environment ("dev", "stage", "prod") is required on scale-set and project calls. Guide 19 runs Scenarios 1-3, guide 20 Scenarios 4-6, and the ESAF usage guide explains every parameter.

REST lets you send requests directly, without the Factory CLI or Python SDK. This example uses Bash and curl. On Windows, use Git Bash, not PowerShell, for the commands in this tab.

docs.title: 1. Connect to the prepared demo service
docs.text:
Ask your platform team to start the local demo API, or use the optional startup instructions below. Keep the service running while trying step 2.

More info

To start the prepared API yourself from Git Bash on Windows, enter its Windows folder path. cygpath converts the path for Git Bash:

read -r -p "Prepared API folder (Windows path): " api_windows
api_root="$(cygpath -u "$api_windows")"
cd "$api_root" || exit 1
AIFACTORY_API_KEY='example-local-parity-smoke-only' \
  .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m uvicorn src.api:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8876

Leave this terminal running and use another Git Bash terminal for step 2. On Linux/macOS, start the service from its prepared environment instead; the following curl requests are unchanged.

docs.title: 2. Set the address, key and empty local folder
docs.text:
Use the address/key of the local demo, not a production factory. curl must support --fail-with-body.

read -r -p "Demo API URL [http://127.0.0.1:8876]: " API_URL
API_URL="${API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8876}"
API_URL="${API_URL%/}"
read -r -s -p "Demo API key: " API_KEY
printf '\n'
test -n "$API_KEY" || { printf 'An API key is required.\n' >&2; exit 1; }

demo_root="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir "$demo_root/azurefactory"
if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  FACTORY_FOLDER="$(cygpath -w "$demo_root/azurefactory")"
else
  FACTORY_FOLDER="$demo_root/azurefactory"
fi

This folder is on the same computer as the demo API. A real operation uses the actual folder on the computer running the API.

docs.title: 3. Read health and the factory list
docs.text:
curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body --noproxy '*' \
  "$API_URL/health" || exit 1
printf '\n'

curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body --noproxy '*' --get \
  "$API_URL/api/v1/factory-catalog" \
  --header "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "folder=$FACTORY_FOLDER" || exit 1
printf '\n'

Expect a healthy service and an empty factory list. You are finished. Stop the idle demo server with Ctrl+C in its terminal when done.

More info

Interactive API help: http://127.0.0.1:8876/docs. The exact HTTP definitions are at /openapi.json. Curl sends HTTP requests; it is not the azurefactory CLI. Do not send privileged requests from browser JavaScript with an API key.

docs.title: 4. Next: the six scenarios, one request each
docs.text:
With a real factory folder, each scenario is one POST to /api/v1/esaf/<scenario>, answered with 202 Accepted and a job id. List the routes the demo API serves:

curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body --noproxy '*' "$API_URL/openapi.json" \
  | grep -o '"/api/v1/esaf/[^"]*"' | sort -u
Scenario Request body (besides "folder" and "approved": true) POST /api/v1/esaf/init-factory nothing, or creation_request POST /api/v1/esaf/add-scale-set "scale_set": "002", "environment": "dev", "cidr": "10.141.0.0/16" POST /api/v1/esaf/upsert-project "project": "002", "environment": "dev" POST /api/v1/esaf/delete-project "project": "002", "environment": "dev" POST /api/v1/esaf/delete-scale-set "scale_set": "002", "environment": "dev" POST /api/v1/esaf/delete-factory nothing

"approved": true is required: sending the request is the approval and changes Azure, so do not send them to this demo folder. Read the job with GET /api/v1/esaf/jobs/{job_id}?folder=... about once a second. Guide 19 sends Scenarios 1-3 and guide 20 Scenarios 4-6.

docs.title: Next: a real registered factory
docs.text: Use guide 19 or guide 20 with your real service address and private key. Do not reuse the public demo key or its empty folder. The documentation site remembers the selected tool.

docs.title: The five steps
docs.text: Step Meaning Remember Check / preflight Validates your configuration and environment. Resolve any reported problems first. Prepare Shows changes for review. No deployment yet. Review and approve Check the factory, environment and changes. Approve only what you intend. Confirm / start For deployment, sends the approved configuration to the configured ADO/GHA pipeline and starts it. A settings-only confirmation saves settings; it does not deploy. Follow progress Reads status and output from the current deployment run. Check a missing response before trying again.

docs.title: First identify which variables.json you mean
docs.text: File / location Ownership and editing rule Registered azurefactory\factories\<key>\scalesets\<suffix>\projects\projectNNN\variables.json Written by the service. Use supported settings requests; manual changes are not automatically loaded and can be overwritten. Registered azurefactory\register.json, bindings, receipts and encrypted profiles Maintained by the service. Do not edit them to change factory identity, approve work or bypass errors.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Problem What to do A variable or path is missing Run the setup for your chosen tab in the same terminal/process as its requests. Connection refused Start the service and check the address/port. Wrong key / 401 Use the key belonging to that service. Python cannot import the SDK Check the source folder or selected Python environment. Blocked operation / missing response Read the message and check the existing run. Do not repeat a deployment or deletion blindly. More info Alternative and Legacy ways

Next - 19. Add and update an AI factory

docs.title: Setup and versions
docs.text:
Use compatible API and client versions. A published source update is not an installed upgrade. The original parity baseline was API d52463f and accelerator eb077742; named convenience helpers were added in 0da0d85b. Environment-only placement needs the newer API implementation; an older API may return 422. Do not reset another person's checkout or change a deployment pin just to follow a tutorial.

The API key does not grant Azure permissions. Settings saves, deployments and deletions have separate approval steps. Keep keys and review files private. API paths refer to the computer running the service.

docs.title: Support labels
docs.text: Label Meaning implemented Available in the reviewed code; check the installed version. generic-access only Use a general request rather than a named shortcut. conditional/blocked Software, permissions, settings and deployment checks must pass. not implemented The complete behavior is not available.

docs.title: Three-interface coverage
docs.text: Capability REST Python SDK CLI Important limit Health, schema, capabilities and account checks implemented implemented implemented doctor is an extra CLI helper. Create factory configuration implemented implemented implemented Saves settings only. Clone/add scale set/project/placement implemented implemented implemented Does not copy deployed resources or data. Latest successful placement in a selected environment implemented in newer API source implemented implemented Successful recorded common deployment required; no implicit environment. Read/replace registered settings implemented implemented implemented Review and save separately from deployment. Parameter editing and override removal implemented implemented implemented Removing an override is not deleting a resource. Remove never-deployed local drafts implemented implemented implemented Checked local removal only. GitHub workflow status/watch implemented implemented implemented Not an ADO watcher. Sample reports, saved results and costs implemented implemented implemented Actual billing requires Azure reads. Deployment and registered bootstrap conditional/blocked conditional/blocked conditional/blocked Requires compatible setup and runtime. Whole-factory deletion/status/recovery conditional/blocked conditional/blocked conditional/blocked Projects finish before common teardown. Project/scale-set Azure deletion conditional/blocked implemented preparation implemented preparation Actual deletion still needs all ownership/retention checks. Captured Dev-to-Stage-to-Prod promotion not implemented as execution not implemented as execution not implemented as execution Capturing/reviewing inputs is not target deployment.

docs.title: The eight scenarios
docs.text: Scenario Support and limit Guide A. New factory, hub/VPN, project001 and environments implemented configuration; conditional/blocked deployment. 19 B. Add an AI Factory scale set implemented configuration; conditional/blocked deployment. Not VMSS. 19 C. Choose latest successful eligible scale set implemented in an explicit environment on a compatible API. 19 E. Add/update/remove settings and resources Settings are implemented; Azure changes are conditional/blocked. 19/20 G. Delete a project Named preparation is implemented; execution is conditional/blocked. 20 H. Keep hub/VPN/dependencies during factory deletion conditional/blocked; resources that must stay can block group deletion. 20 D. Promote captured configuration/version across environments not implemented as a complete deployment operation. 19 F. Choose APIM versus Kong Unified selection is not implemented; component support is conditional/blocked. 19

docs.title: Optional developer regression tests
docs.text:
These are not needed to use any of the three tools. The offline consumer 114 harness checks the interfaces with simulated provider results; it makes no Azure changes and does not need a running demo server. Its README contains the runner. The earlier 25 passed, 1 warning result was successful; the httpx deprecation warning was not an instruction to install another dependency.

Offline test instructions. Consumer 114 is not an Azure sandbox; consumer 113 is not used here.

docs.title: References
docs.text: CLI/SDK reference, API examples, canonical API guide.

docs.title: Choose how to author configuration: file-first or wrapper-first
docs.text:
The default registered-factory route uses commands/helpers (wrapper-first) to save settings. You may write request JSON, but do not hand-edit registered catalog files.

File-first applies to an exact consumer-owned variables.json used by a supported older pipeline. Check the file, project and environment; keep a private backup, edit only intended values, validate them, and separately review deployment. Saving JSON does not publish provider variables, run pipelines or delete resources.

File / location Editing rule Accelerator environment_setup\aifactory\variables.json Shared defaults, not a customer-settings shortcut. Legacy consumer aifactory\variables.json or selected project JSON Manual editing may apply; confirm which file the pipeline actually reads. .env, ADO variables.yaml, GitHub Environment variables Separate inputs with explicit save/publish steps; no automatic synchronization.

Legacy config review/save and ConfigurationDraft preserve persistent JSON. Reload after manual changes; an old review is no longer valid. Migration to a registered factory is a separate operation. Legacy submitted means the local script exited zero, not that Azure succeeded.

Advanced CLI enrollment is a separate local implementation, not equivalent REST/SDK provisioning. It can create resources and grant roles. See guide 19's tool-specific alternatives and the canonical reference.

More info

There is no two-way sync from arbitrary JSON edits into the register. Registered project exports can be overwritten. Never reconstruct _json_source or change review hashes to replay a stale save.

The pipeline JSON reader applies dev, then stage_prod for non-Dev, then exact test/prod overrides when present. Registered snapshots use dev and stage_prod with placement checks; these formats are not interchangeable.

Legacy JSON editing | Pipeline reader

docs.title: 19. Add and update an AI factory
docs.text: Choose one tool tab for this whole tutorial. Each tab starts with the simplest way: Scenarios 1-3 in one call each (ESAF: init_factory, add_scale_set, upsert_project), where the API prepares, checks and confirms every review for you. The step-by-step operations follow, for when you review each change yourself before it is applied: they select real targets, prepare changes and stop for review before confirmation. Start with 18 — connection and compatibility checks; use 20 — removal and recovery for deletion or an uncertain result. 17 maps the six scenarios across the tools. On GitHub, expand the matching tool section. The documentation website uses one linked tab selector for the same content.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Obtain the owning API's URL and key from your operator. A demo address/key is not for real resources. These administrative endpoints currently require local-host access. Keep the key out of browser code, source control and output.
  • folder, repo_root and import paths refer to the API host. Request files and reviews below are client-local. A needs an operator-created, empty azurefactory folder; B–E need the real registered catalog, not a smoke-test root.
  • No deployment yet: confirming configuration saves settings (job: null). Runtime confirmation is separate and can create billable resources, publish Git changes and start pipelines. can_execute: true is not approval or proof of success.
  • STOP and review the exact folder, IDs, environment, tenant/subscription, version, changes, ownership, warnings and expiry. Keep reviews in private, persistent storage outside Git and temporary cleanup folders; verify its access permissions. Checksums detect file changes; they are not signatures or approval.
  • Never retry an uncertain write, or switch tools to repeat it. Inspect saved state first. A timeout stops waiting, not the deployment.
  • Settings saves and typed unset do not delete Azure resources. null is not a general unset. Changes to shared stage_prod settings can affect both Stage and Prod: replacing shared values can lose settings the other environment uses. Review both; do not assume Stage-only isolation. A parameter profile reset discards all old protected parameter settings in that scale set, even when one project is selected; do not use it to bypass an error.
More info Intent Support and limit A. New factory, selected Dev/Stage/Prod, project001, own hub intent; clone implemented configuration preparation and confirmation. The short request does not configure or deploy a complete VPN/hub. B. Add a scale set and/or project implemented; separate configuration changes. An AI Factory scale set is an environment/network/subscription grouping, not Azure VMSS. C. Latest successful scale in an explicit environment implemented in newer API source. Environment-only placement is not yet in the published API baseline; install-compatible host required, no implicit Dev. D. Stage/Prod placement versus captured promotion Placement is implemented. Executing a captured successful Dev configuration/version through Stage and Prod is not implemented. Backend capture/review work is in progress, not a published executable promotion route. E. Typed parameters and scoped settings implemented, including named CLI/SDK preparation and typed review receipts. Runtime and registered Full bootstrap conditional/blocked by host/runtime versions, permissions, bindings, ownership, identity, runners and network readiness. Migration, draft identity correction, direct binding configuration, registered creation API generic-access only where supported; no invented dedicated helpers. Unified APIM-versus-Kong deployment choice not implemented. Newer MCP/AI Gateway component pipelines have conditional/blocked support; Application Gateway is a different product and its registered workflow is blocked.

Read the chosen API's capabilities and OpenAPI before using a request. A newer client cannot supply a missing server/runtime feature. DEV/001, STAGE/001 and PROD/001 are different targets; 001 is not a UUID. API environments are dev, stage, prod (some Azure naming uses test for Stage).

docs.title: Choose your tool
docs.text: CLI (PowerShell)Python SDKREST (curl)

docs.title: Scenarios 1-3 in one command each (ESAF)
docs.text:
Each scenario is one azurefactory esaf command. The Config Wizard API runs it as one job: it prepares, checks and confirms every review, waits for a busy configuration lock and retries a failed run. Running a command is the approval: it changes Azure. Start the API first, from the app: see Quickstart: Install the ESAF tools. You don't need the API's source code.

Connect once in this window: the API address and the key you entered in the app, and ESAF_FOLDER, the absolute azurefactory folder on the API host. Then install the CLI from your approved accelerator checkout:

$env:AIFACTORY_API_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:8765'
$env:AIFACTORY_API_KEY = Read-Host 'API key you entered in the app'
$env:ESAF_FOLDER = (Resolve-Path (Read-Host 'Absolute azurefactory folder on the API host')).Path
$AcceleratorRoot = Read-Host 'Absolute path to your approved accelerator checkout'
python -m pip install -e (Join-Path $AcceleratorRoot 'environment_setup\azurefactory-cli')

Then run the scenarios. --wait follows each job to its end, reading it every second:

azurefactory esaf init-factory --creation-request-json .\creation-request.json --wait
azurefactory esaf add-scale-set 002 dev --cidr 10.141.0.0/16 --wait
azurefactory esaf upsert-project 002 dev --scale-set 001 --wait
azurefactory esaf upsert-project 002 dev --scale-set 001 --settings-json .\project-settings.json --wait
Command Arguments and options init-factory Without options it submits the folder's saved factory draft (for example saved in the Config Wizard). --creation-request-json FILE saves a new factory from a full-bootstrap creation body ({"contract_version": 1, "mode": "full-bootstrap", "action": "create-factory", "folder", "orchestrator", "config": {...}, "factory_key", "region_short_name"}) and starts it in the same call. add-scale-set SUFFIX ENVIRONMENT SUFFIX is three digits (002); ENVIRONMENT is dev, stage or prod. --cidr is the new scale set's VNet range; the pipeline computes the subnets (with BYOSubnet they already exist). --max-projects defaults to 7. Tenant, subscription and orchestrator come from the environment's existing scale set. An existing scale set is resumed, not registered again. upsert-project NUMBER ENVIRONMENT Adds the project if it is new, otherwise updates it, then deploys it. --scale-set is needed only when the environment has more than one scale set. --settings-json FILE holds the settings to replace, for example {"tag_costcenter": "lab"}. All --folder overrides ESAF_FOLDER; --factory selects a factory when the folder holds several; --retries (0-5, default 2) and --version-ref; --wait.

Without --wait the command prints the job id; follow it later with azurefactory esaf job <job id> --wait. Exit code 0 means succeeded (or still running), 3 blocked by the server's review (its blockers are printed), 5 failed.

Step-by-step alternative. Everything below in this tab prepares each change, stops for your review and confirms it separately. Use it when you must review a change before it is applied, or for operations the one-call methods do not cover (clone, placements, typed parameters).

docs.title: Connect and define the local helpers
docs.text:
Use Windows PowerShell 5.1+ or PowerShell 7, an existing API Python environment and the approved accelerator checkout. No console-script installation or variables from another tab are required. These snippets run in one shell.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$ApiRoot = Read-Host 'Absolute path to your existing API checkout'
$AcceleratorRoot = Read-Host 'Absolute path to your approved accelerator checkout'
$Python = Join-Path $ApiRoot '.venv\Scripts\python.exe'
$SdkSource = Join-Path $AcceleratorRoot 'environment_setup\azurefactory-cli\src'
if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $Python -PathType Leaf) -or
    !(Test-Path -LiteralPath $SdkSource -PathType Container)) { throw 'Check existing tool paths.' }
$env:PYTHONPATH = $SdkSource
$env:AIFACTORY_API_URL = Read-Host 'Operator-provided owning API URL, without trailing slash'
if (!$env:AIFACTORY_API_URL) { throw 'Do not use an implicit demo URL.' }
if (!$env:AIFACTORY_API_KEY) {
    $Secret = Read-Host 'Operator-provided API key' -AsSecureString
    $Pointer = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::SecureStringToBSTR($Secret)
    try { $env:AIFACTORY_API_KEY = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::PtrToStringBSTR($Pointer) }
    finally { [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::ZeroFreeBSTR($Pointer) }
}
if (!$env:AIFACTORY_API_KEY) { throw 'Missing API key.' }
& $Python -m azurefactory health
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'API unavailable.' }
& $Python -m azurefactory doctor
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Incompatible host; stop.' }
$FactoryFolder = Read-Host 'Exact absolute azurefactory folder ON THE API HOST'
if (![IO.Path]::IsPathRooted($FactoryFolder)) { throw 'Use an absolute API-host path.' }
$ReviewRoot = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA ('AzureFactory\reviews\' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ReviewRoot -Force | Out-Null

function New-ReviewPath([string]$Label) {
    return (Join-Path $ReviewRoot ($Label + '-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N') + '.json'))
}
function Write-ReviewJson($Value, [string]$Label) {
    $Path = New-ReviewPath $Label
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($Path, (ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $Value -Depth 100),
        [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
    return $Path
}
function Read-Catalog {
    $Text = & $Python -m azurefactory catalog list --folder $FactoryFolder
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Catalog read failed.' }
    $Value = ($Text -join "`n") | ConvertFrom-Json
    if ($Value.contract_version -ne 1 -or $Value.mode -ne 'catalog') { throw 'Not a registered catalog.' }
    return $Value
}
function Read-Target([switch]$Scale, [switch]$Project, [switch]$Placed) {
    $Catalog = Read-Catalog
    $Catalog.factories | Select-Object id,key,region,version_ref | Format-Table | Out-Host
    $Id = Read-Host 'Exact factory UUID'
    $Found = @($Catalog.factories | Where-Object { $_.id -eq $Id })
    if ($Found.Count -ne 1) { throw 'Select exactly one listed factory.' }
    $Factory = $Found[0]; $SelectedScale = $null; $SelectedProject = $null
    if ($Scale) {
        $Factory.scale_sets | Select-Object id,environment,suffix,tenant_id,subscription_id | Format-Table | Out-Host
        $Id = Read-Host 'Exact scale-set UUID'
        $Found = @($Factory.scale_sets | Where-Object { $_.id -eq $Id })
        if ($Found.Count -ne 1) { throw 'Select exactly one listed scale.' }
        $SelectedScale = $Found[0]
    }
    if ($Project) {
        $Factory.projects | Select-Object id,number,display_name,placements | Format-List | Out-Host
        $Id = Read-Host 'Exact project UUID'
