  '{contract_version:1, folder:$folder, factory_id:$factory, expected_revision:$revision,
    action:("delete-draft-" + $kind)}
   + (if $scale == "" then {} else {scale_set_id:$scale} end)
   + (if $project == "" then {} else {project_id:$project} end)' > "$request_path"

docs.title: Grant deletion permission first (C, D and E)
docs.text:
Under single-writer coordination, the factory's enrollment in the provider repository must permit deletion (allow_delete=true) before C, D or E can execute; new enrollments disallow it. Granting it is its own reviewed change of the provider state: it never changes Azure, deletes nothing and lifts none of the other blockers below. A 404/405 without the operation's own detail means the API lacks the authorize-deletion routes; there is no fallback. After approval, confirm once with the exact phrase ALLOW DELETE <factory key>, then run setup again before building the deletion request. Revoke it the same way with mode:"revoke" and REVOKE DELETE <factory key>.

jq -n --arg folder "$folder" --arg factory "$factory_id" \
  '{contract_version:1, folder:$folder, factory_id:$factory, mode:"allow"}' > "$review_dir/authorize-request.json"
post_json "$review_dir/authorize-preview.json" /api/v1/operations/authorize-deletion/prepare \
  "$review_dir/authorize-request.json"
jq . "$review_dir/authorize-preview.json"
jq -e --arg factory "$factory_id" '.operation_mode == "provider-state" and .azure_writes == false
  and .factory_id == $factory and .mode == "allow" and .can_execute == true and (.blockers | length == 0)
  and (.capabilities | index("authorize-deletion-v1") != null)' "$review_dir/authorize-preview.json" >/dev/null
# STOP. After approval, type the exact phrase and POST it once; never retry an uncertain result.
read -r -p 'Exact confirmation phrase from the preview: ' phrase
jq -e --arg phrase "$phrase" '.confirmation_phrase == $phrase' "$review_dir/authorize-preview.json" >/dev/null
jq --arg folder "$folder" --arg phrase "$phrase" \
  '{contract_version:1, folder:$folder, confirmation_id, preview_hash, confirmation_phrase:$phrase}' \
  "$review_dir/authorize-preview.json" > "$review_dir/authorize-confirm.json"
post_json "$review_dir/authorize-result.json" /api/v1/operations/authorize-deletion/confirm \
  "$review_dir/authorize-confirm.json"
jq . "$review_dir/authorize-result.json"

docs.title: C. Delete project resources in selected environments
docs.text:
Use unique environments in any order. Both independent choices must be JSON booleans, not strings: false keeps the named resources; true includes them for deletion. Subnet permission does not approve shared-group deletion.

Modern layout 2 is required. Blob and single-writer factories both support it; grant a single-writer factory's deletion permission first (authorize-deletion). The selected source needs selective-project-resources-v1 and one exact registered placement per chosen environment. Ordinary project deletion uses the selective lifecycle path; do not assume GitHub Actions or the whole-factory ordered-pipeline path.

jq -e '.layout_version == 2' "$review_dir/catalog.json" >/dev/null
read -r -p 'Exact project UUID: ' project_id
read -r -p 'Environments, comma-separated: dev, stage, prod: ' environment_text
environments=$(jq -nc --arg value "$environment_text" '$value | split(",") | map(gsub("^\\s+|\\s+$"; ""))')
jq -e 'length > 0 and length <= 3 and length == (unique | length)
  and all(.[]; . == "dev" or . == "stage" or . == "prod")' <<< "$environments" >/dev/null
read -r -p 'Include project subnets? true or false: ' include_subnets
read -r -p 'Include Key Vault and project resource group? true or false: ' include_group
[[ "$include_subnets" == true || "$include_subnets" == false ]]
[[ "$include_group" == true || "$include_group" == false ]]
jq -n --arg folder "$folder" --arg factory "$factory_id" --arg revision "$revision" \
  --arg project "$project_id" --argjson environments "$environments" \
  --argjson subnets "$include_subnets" --argjson group "$include_group" \
  '{contract_version:1, folder:$folder, factory_id:$factory, expected_revision:$revision,
    action:"delete-project", project_id:$project,
    deletion_options:{environments:$environments, include_project_subnets:$subnets,
      include_keyvault_and_resource_group:$group}}' > "$request_path"
expected_mode=runtime

Verified group deletion updates affected deployment settings; removing every placement can remove local project configuration. Services-only deletion keeps it. Neither removes factory/scale-set configuration. Azure soft-delete and retention rules still apply.

docs.title: D. Delete a scale set's runtime resources
docs.text:
This is not draft removal. Shared dependencies, retained resources and active projects can block it. Inspect exact delete and retain lists; a group row alone is not approval to delete that group.

read -r -p 'Exact scale-set UUID for runtime deletion: ' scale_set_id
jq -n --arg folder "$folder" --arg factory "$factory_id" --arg revision "$revision" \
  --arg scale "$scale_set_id" \
  '{contract_version:1, folder:$folder, factory_id:$factory, expected_revision:$revision,
    action:"delete-scale-set", scale_set_id:$scale}' > "$request_path"
expected_mode=runtime

docs.title: E. Delete the whole factory — separate named operation
docs.text:
Whole-group deletion cannot preserve selected resources inside deleted groups. Protected hub/VPN/platform/bootstrap resources, coordination storage, the executing identity and private runners must be outside them. The one exception is a factory-owned integrated hub (VPN gateway, Bastion, DNS private resolver) and private runner that the factory's own bootstrap created in its own groups: those go only with bootstrap proof (deletion_plan.access_hubs). A hub-connected factory can lose only its own Bastion Developer or DNS resolver that way, never a VPN gateway. Connectivity hub resource groups and shared hubs are never deleted. Entra groups and Git repositories/history stay. No Key Vault purge occurs; other external dependencies need separate review.

Execution is conditional on named ordered-pipeline support and Blob coordination. The API's frozen accelerator pin lacks the ordered runtime contract; client publication does not upgrade it. No automatic mode change occurs. Every registered project GHA or ADO pipeline in every environment must finish before shared-group removal. Configuration cleanup follows verified completion, not simply pipeline submission.

A never-enrolled bootstrap draft (no registered ownership, no lease store or pipeline) instead gets a bootstrap-operator-teardown-v1 plan from the same prepare. It is conditional on an API and published runtime that advertise bootstrap_operator_teardown, needs no Blob coordination or pipelines, and is executed by the operator: it first removes only the factory's own DNS links and peerings inside the configured connectivity hub, then deletes the bootstrap-proven groups, groups last. A failed run keeps the draft; prepare again from fresh inventory.

jq -n --arg folder "$folder" --arg factory "$factory_id" --arg revision "$revision" \
  '{contract_version:1, folder:$folder, factory_id:$factory, expected_revision:$revision}' > "$request_path"
prepare_route=/api/v1/operations/delete-aifactory/prepare
confirm_route=/api/v1/operations/delete-aifactory/confirm
expected_mode=runtime
operation=delete-aifactory

docs.title: 3. Prepare, save the raw preview, and STOP
docs.text:
All choices above join this flow. Unlike a CLI/SDK typed receipt, preview.json is the raw API preview. It cannot be passed to a receipt-based CLI confirmation.

post_json "$preview_path" "$prepare_route" "$request_path"
jq . "$preview_path"
check_preview() {
  jq -e --arg mode "$expected_mode" --arg operation "$operation" --slurpfile request "$request_path" '
    $request[0] as $r |
    .contract_version == 1 and .can_execute == true
    and (.can_execute | type) == "boolean"
    and (.blockers | type) == "array" and (.blockers | length) == 0
    and .operation_mode == $mode and .source_revision == $r.expected_revision
    and (.source_revision | type) == "string" and (.source_revision | test("^[a-f0-9]{64}$"))
    and .target.id == $r.factory_id
    and (if $operation == "parameters" then true else
      .factory_id == $r.factory_id
      and .scale_set_id == ($r.scale_set_id // null) and .project_id == ($r.project_id // null)
    end)
    and (.confirmation_id | type) == "string" and (.confirmation_id | length) > 0
    and ((.expires_at | sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) > now)
    and (if $r.action == "delete-project" then
      (.deletion_options.include_project_subnets | type) == "boolean"
      and (.deletion_options.include_keyvault_and_resource_group | type) == "boolean"
      and .deletion_options.include_project_subnets == $r.deletion_options.include_project_subnets
      and .deletion_options.include_keyvault_and_resource_group == $r.deletion_options.include_keyvault_and_resource_group
      and (.deletion_options.environments | sort) == ($r.deletion_options.environments | sort)
    else true end)' "$preview_path" >/dev/null
}
check_preview

The expiry check accepts the API's UTC timestamp; malformed/unsupported dates fail closed. Review the request and full response: scope, environment, tenant/subscription, source/revision, mode, settings, exact resources to delete/keep, both project choices, warnings and blockers.

Parameter previews identify the target factory and source revision, not separate top-level scale/project IDs. Review those IDs in the saved request and the earlier parameter read; the server binds them to the confirmation ID.

For whole-factory only, also define and run this structural plan check. It is not the SDK's complete plan/hash validator: inspect the entire saved plan, its hash, immutable source, pipelines and manifests. The server revalidates its stored plan at confirmation; never hand-edit a preview.

check_whole_preview() {
  jq -e --slurpfile request "$request_path" '
    $request[0] as $r | . as $p | .deletion_plan as $plan |
    .action == "delete-factory" and .folder == $r.folder
    and (.capabilities | index("delete-aifactory-v1")) != null
    and .deletion_scope == "whole-factory" and .deletion_options == null
    and .preserve_entra_groups == true and .retain_saved_configuration == false
    and .target.id == $r.factory_id and .confirmation_phrase == ("DELETE " + .target.key)
    and (.preview_hash | test("^[a-f0-9]{64}$"))
    and .deletion_retention_policy.mode == "preserve-reusable-infrastructure"
    and .deletion_retention_policy.required_execution_contract == "ordered-project-pipelines-v1"
    and .deletion_retention_policy.execution_scope == "whole-resource-groups"
    and .deletion_retention_policy.selective_retention_supported == false
    and (.deletion_retention_policy.limitations | type == "array" and length > 0)
    and $plan.retention_policy == .deletion_retention_policy
    and $plan.contract == "ordered-project-pipelines-v1"
    and $plan.factory_id == $r.factory_id and $plan.policy == "all-projects-before-common"
    and ($plan.plan_hash | test("^[a-f0-9]{64}$"))
    and ($plan.source_commit | test("^[a-f0-9]{40}$"))
    and ($plan.stages | type == "array" and length > 0)
    and ([ $plan.stages[].id ] | length == (unique | length))
    and all($plan.stages[]; .kind == "project" or .kind == "common")
    and ([$plan.stages[] | select(.kind == "project") | .id] as $projects |
      all($plan.stages[] | select(.kind == "common"); .depends_on == $projects))
    and ([$plan.stages[].kind] | . == (map(select(. == "project")) + map(select(. == "common"))))
    and all($plan.stages[] | select(.kind == "project");
      .depends_on == [] and .inputs == {
        enableDeleteForDisabledResources:true, deleteAllServicesForProject:true,
        deleteKeyvaultAlso:true, deleteAllForProject:true}
      and .lifecycle_order == ["foundry-capability-hosts","target-project-search-shared-private-links",
        "service-managed-lifecycle","project-resources","project-network"]
      and (.pipeline.provider == "gha" or .pipeline.provider == "ado")
      and (.pipeline.commit | test("^[a-f0-9]{40}$")))
    and (.deletion_targets | type == "array" and length > 0)
    and all(.deletion_targets[]; .retain == [] and (.resource_id as $id | .delete | index($id)) != null)
    and all(($plan.protected_resources + $plan.retained_resources)[]; . as $keep |
      all($p.deletion_targets[]; (.resource_id | ascii_downcase) as $group |
        ($keep | ascii_downcase | (. != $group and (startswith($group + "/") | not)))))' "$preview_path" >/dev/null
}
if [[ "$operation" == delete-aifactory ]]; then check_whole_preview; fi
printf '%s\n' 'STOP. Review the saved request and preview and obtain separate approval.'

docs.title: 4. After approval, POST confirmation exactly once
docs.text:
Run this block separately, after human review. Retype the confirmation ID from this fresh, unexpired preview; whole-factory deletion additionally needs the exact phrase and server hash. The local attempt marker remains even if the response is lost. Do not remove it to retry.

check_preview
if [[ "$operation" == delete-aifactory ]]; then check_whole_preview; fi
confirmation_id=$(jq -er '.confirmation_id' "$preview_path")
read -r -p 'After approval, retype the exact factory UUID: ' approved_factory
[[ "$approved_factory" == "$factory_id" ]]
read -r -p 'Retype the confirmation_id from this reviewed preview: ' approved_id
[[ "$approved_id" == "$confirmation_id" ]]
read -r -p 'Type CONFIRM-ONCE: ' approval
[[ "$approval" == CONFIRM-ONCE ]]
if [[ "$operation" == delete-aifactory ]]; then
  read -r -p 'Type the exact server confirmation_phrase: ' phrase
  [[ "$phrase" == "$(jq -er '.confirmation_phrase' "$preview_path")" ]]
  jq -n --arg folder "$folder" --arg phrase "$phrase" --slurpfile preview "$preview_path" \
    '{contract_version:1, folder:$folder, confirmation_id:$preview[0].confirmation_id,
      preview_hash:$preview[0].preview_hash, confirmation_phrase:$phrase}' > "$review_dir/confirm-request.json"
else
  jq -n --arg folder "$folder" --arg id "$confirmation_id" \
    '{contract_version:1, folder:$folder, confirmation_id:$id}' > "$review_dir/confirm-request.json"
fi
check_preview
printf '%s\n' "$confirmation_id" > "$review_dir/confirmation-attempted.txt"
post_json "$review_dir/confirmation-result.json" "$confirm_route" "$review_dir/confirm-request.json"
jq . "$review_dir/confirmation-result.json"
if jq -e '.job.id | type == "string" and length > 0' "$review_dir/confirmation-result.json" >/dev/null; then
  jq -r '.job.id' "$review_dir/confirmation-result.json" > "$review_dir/job-id.txt"
fi

Configuration-only confirmation may return catalog without a job. Runtime confirmation returns job.id; the response and ID are saved before any observation. HTTP success alone does not prove resource deletion.

docs.title: 5. Observe, or finish local whole-factory cleanup
docs.text:
If a confirm response was lost, list jobs using the same identity and correlate action, exact scope, source and time. Never choose the first job. If unsure, stop and ask the owning operator to inspect the records.

stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$RANDOM"
get_json "$review_dir/jobs-$stamp.json" /api/v1/factory-catalog/jobs --data-urlencode "folder=$folder"
jq . "$review_dir/jobs-$stamp.json"
read -r -p 'Exact correlated job UUID from saved result or job list: ' job_id
[[ "$job_id" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$ ]]
get_json "$review_dir/status-$stamp.json" "/api/v1/factory-catalog/jobs/$job_id" --data-urlencode "folder=$folder"
jq . "$review_dir/status-$stamp.json"
get_json "$review_dir/logs-$stamp.json" /api/v1/factory-catalog/terminal \
  --data-urlencode "folder=$folder" --data-urlencode "job_id=$job_id" --data-urlencode 'cursor=0'
jq . "$review_dir/logs-$stamp.json"

Repeat GETs only with new output filenames to observe progress; there is no REST poll endpoint. Statuses are queued, running, succeeded, failed, interrupted. Timeout stops waiting, not the job. Missing logs do not prove deletion or make another confirmation safe.

For a job whose action is exactly delete-factory, read named status:

get_json "$review_dir/whole-status-$stamp.json" /api/v1/operations/delete-aifactory/status \
  --data-urlencode "folder=$folder" --data-urlencode "job_id=$job_id"
jq . "$review_dir/whole-status-$stamp.json"

Review pipeline_runs, deletion_plan, reconciliation_required and saved completion records. If Azure completion was verified but local cleanup was interrupted, this separate request asks for local reconciliation only:

read -r -p 'Retype the reviewed delete-factory job UUID for local cleanup: ' approved_job
[[ "$approved_job" == "$job_id" ]]
jq -n --arg folder "$folder" --arg job "$job_id" \
  '{contract_version:1, folder:$folder, job_id:$job}' > "$review_dir/reconcile-request.json"
post_json "$review_dir/reconcile-result.json" /api/v1/operations/delete-aifactory/reconcile "$review_dir/reconcile-request.json"
jq . "$review_dir/reconcile-result.json"

Reconciliation does not call Azure, restart pipelines or retry deletion; missing verified records keep it blocked. General project/scale-set recovery is not implemented here. Never clear locks or re-register as a shortcut.

docs.title: 6. Optional read-only checks and reports
docs.text:
Health/schema/sign-in checks do not establish deployment success. These documented REST calls are implemented; there is no /doctor endpoint (doctor is a CLI-side compatibility check).

get_json "$review_dir/health.json" /health
jq . "$review_dir/health.json"
get_json "$review_dir/schema.json" /api/v1/schema
jq . "$review_dir/schema.json"
get_json "$review_dir/openapi.json" /openapi.json
get_json "$review_dir/capabilities.json" /api/v1/creation/capabilities
jq . "$review_dir/capabilities.json"
read -r -p 'Exact scale-set UUID for an authorized Azure sign-in check: ' observed_scale
jq -n --arg folder "$folder" --arg factory "$factory_id" --arg scale "$observed_scale" \
  '{aifactory_folder:$folder, factory_id:$factory, scale_set_id:$scale}' > "$review_dir/auth-request.json"
post_json "$review_dir/auth-status.json" /api/v1/azure/auth/status "$review_dir/auth-request.json"
jq . "$review_dir/auth-status.json"

docs.title: GitHub Actions status and read-only event stream — not ADO
docs.text:
These calls do not start pipelines. Use the exact recorded repository/run; for ADO use its provider results and the original catalog job.

read -r -p 'Exact GitHub OWNER/REPO recorded for this operation: ' repository
read -r -p 'Exact GitHub Actions numeric run ID: ' run_id
get_json "$review_dir/workflow-status.json" /api/v1/workflow-runs/status \
  --data-urlencode "repository=$repository" --data-urlencode "run_id=$run_id"
jq . "$review_dir/workflow-status.json"
call_api "$review_dir/workflow-events.sse" /api/v1/workflow-runs/events \
  --get --no-buffer --max-time 120 --header 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  --data-urlencode "repository=$repository" --data-urlencode "run_id=$run_id" --data-urlencode 'follow=true'
cat "$review_dir/workflow-events.sse"

The events file contains SSE, not JSON. curl exit 28 means its observation deadline expired; inspect the partial file and current status, not another confirmation. Reconnect GETs with a returned after cursor to resume. Reconnecting or closing a stream neither reruns nor cancels the workflow.

docs.title: Sample metrics, saved metrics and Azure billing
docs.text:
get_json "$review_dir/monitoring-catalog.json" /api/v1/monitoring/catalog
jq . "$review_dir/monitoring-catalog.json"
jq -n '{source:"sample", report_id:"showback"}' > "$review_dir/sample-report-request.json"
post_json "$review_dir/sample-report.json" /api/v1/monitoring/report "$review_dir/sample-report-request.json"
jq . "$review_dir/sample-report.json"
jq -n '{source:"sample"}' > "$review_dir/sample-summary-request.json"
post_json "$review_dir/sample-summary.json" /api/v1/monitoring/summary "$review_dir/sample-summary-request.json"
jq . "$review_dir/sample-summary.json"
jq -n '{source:"sample", report_id:"showback", format:"csv"}' > "$review_dir/export-request.json"
post_json "$review_dir/sample-showback.csv" /api/v1/monitoring/export "$review_dir/export-request.json"
jq -n --arg folder "$folder" --arg factory "$factory_id" \
  '{folder:$folder, factory_id:$factory}' > "$review_dir/saved-request.json"
post_json "$review_dir/saved-results.json" /api/v1/monitoring/evidence/read "$review_dir/saved-request.json"
jq . "$review_dir/saved-results.json"
jq -e '.contract == "aifactory.monitoring-evidence.v1"
  and .status == "available" and (.rows | type) == "array"
  and (.native_bindings | type) == "array"' "$review_dir/saved-results.json" >/dev/null
jq '{source:"live", rows:.rows, native_bindings:.native_bindings}' \
  "$review_dir/saved-results.json" > "$review_dir/saved-summary-request.json"
post_json "$review_dir/saved-summary.json" /api/v1/monitoring/summary "$review_dir/saved-summary-request.json"
jq . "$review_dir/saved-summary.json"
jq '. + {report_id:"showback"}' "$review_dir/saved-summary-request.json" > "$review_dir/saved-report-request.json"
post_json "$review_dir/saved-report.json" /api/v1/monitoring/report "$review_dir/saved-report-request.json"
jq . "$review_dir/saved-report.json"

sample uses demonstration data. Saved metrics do not collect/import data or start jobs; projection runs only when saved results are available. Keep the original envelope, warnings and source errors alongside reports. absent, incompatible or unavailable is not zero cost or good health. live here means supplied stored observations, not automatic Azure collection.

This last request performs an Azure Cost Management read. Use only an explicitly permitted subscription; late/zero billing does not prove deletion.

read -r -p 'Exact authorized subscription UUID for billing reads: ' subscription_id
read -r -p 'Billing month YYYY-MM: ' month
jq -n --arg subscription "$subscription_id" --arg month "$month" --arg folder "$folder" \
  '{subscription_ids:[$subscription], month:$month, aifactory_folder:$folder}' > "$review_dir/cost-request.json"
post_json "$review_dir/resource-group-costs.json" /api/v1/monitoring/resource-group-costs "$review_dir/cost-request.json"
jq . "$review_dir/resource-group-costs.json"

More info

docs.title: Scoped settings replacement alternative
docs.text:
For nonsecret catalog settings rather than ARM parameter unset/reset, begin a new review with setup. Supply only intentional replacements; omitted keys stay unchanged. This is configuration only, even when setting a service flag false. It uses the normal catalog prepare/confirm routes above.

read -r -p 'Path to a reviewed nonsecret replacement-settings JSON object: ' settings_path
jq -e 'type == "object"' "$settings_path" >/dev/null
jq -n --arg folder "$folder" --arg factory "$factory_id" --arg revision "$revision" \
  --slurpfile settings "$settings_path" \
  '{contract_version:1, folder:$folder, factory_id:$factory, expected_revision:$revision,
    action:"configure-settings", settings:$settings[0]}' > "$request_path"

Continue with the separate prepare/review/confirm steps in this tab. Routes without a friendly CLI/SDK wrapper are generic-access only in those clients; the named removal wrappers already exist. REST always uses the actual HTTP contracts, not CLI receipt formats.

docs.title: Alternative and Legacy ways
docs.text:
Prefer manual configuration editing? Read file-first versus wrapper-first configuration. Deleting a JSON key or setting a service flag false does not approve or perform Azure deletion. Use the selected tab's reviewed flow for resource removal.

Legacy saved-creation removal and /projects/delete or /scale-sets/delete routes are not substitutes for catalog runtime deletion. Legacy submitted means the local script exited zero, not pipeline submission/success or verified Azure deployment; deployment_verified remains false.

An expired unused review can be prepared again from fresh settings. An uncertain confirmed operation must be inspected and resolved first. Automatic flag-to-delete behavior, selective retention inside whole-factory deleted groups, and generic force/retry/cancel-on-timeout recovery are not implemented. Do not use legacy paths to bypass a blocker.

docs.title: Unblock a factory after a failed single-writer run
docs.text:
If every prepare, deploy or delete stops with "Private repository enrollment ... has an active/uncertain claim; reconcile it first", a failed run still holds the single-writer claim. Review what that run changed in Azure, then release only its claim with azurefactory reconcile-run-claim prepare --folder <azurefactory folder> --factory-id <factory UUID> --run-id <failed run ID> --save-receipt <file> followed by azurefactory reconcile-run-claim confirm --receipt <file> and the phrase RELEASE <run ID> (SDK: reconcile_run_claim_prepare / reconcile_run_claim_confirm; REST: POST /api/v1/operations/reconcile-run-claim/prepare and /confirm). It is implemented but blocked unless you own the job that dispatched the run, its run and worker receipts are terminal, its GitHub Actions/Azure DevOps run completed and nothing else is queued or running. One compare-and-swap clears the claim, keeps every record and adds an audit record; Azure is not changed and nothing is retried. Never edit refs/heads/aifactory-state/single-writer-v1 by hand. Details: CLI readme.

More info

docs.title: Support labels and compatibility
docs.text:
• implemented — the command, SDK method or HTTP route exists.
  • generic-access only — a documented API contract is accessible through generic requests but lacks a friendly wrapper; this does not describe the named project/scale-set/draft removal wrappers on this page.
  • conditional — execution still needs the installed host/source/runtime capabilities, correct coordination, ownership, retention and permissions.
  • blocked — a check failed or required proof is missing; stop and resolve it.
  • not implemented — no supported feature is provided; do not infer a fallback.

This page was checked against accelerator client source at 300234cd, including the named wrappers introduced at 0da0d85b and the environment-order review fix at 2ae10aa9. Environments can be requested in any order but must be unique; both project deletion flags must be actual booleans.

The API baseline is d52463f. Its frozen accelerator pin 3e9102ee07c959d91e5ac508432bd1545d258a15 is not changed by this guide and does not provide the named ordered-pipeline runtime. Published source advertises factory_deletion_pipeline_coordination_modes: ["blob", "single-writer"]: a single-writer factory runs the same ordered pipeline (project workers first, then common teardown) under one repository deletion-cohort claim instead of Blob leases, and supports selective project deletion. The API checks the selected immutable source and enrolled mode. No client publication, optional preflight or offline test approves execution.

docs.title: Whole-factory plan and retention contract
docs.text:
deletion_retention_policy must equal deletion_plan.retention_policy:

Field Required value mode preserve-reusable-infrastructure required_execution_contract ordered-project-pipelines-v1 execution_scope whole-resource-groups selective_retention_supported false limitations Nonempty server-provided limitations, reviewed verbatim

All project stages must precede common stages; common stages depend on every registered project placement. Each project stage explicitly sets enableDeleteForDisabledResources, deleteAllServicesForProject, deleteKeyvaultAlso and deleteAllForProject to boolean true. The order is capability hosts, target-project Search shared private links, service-managed lifecycle, project resources, then project network. Pipeline success and verified absence of the exact resources are both required. Configuration references alone do not establish actual inventory or preservation.

A factory that its Full bootstrap created but that was never registered or enrolled (a catalog draft with no lease store or pipeline, such as dc-batman4) gets a bootstrap-operator-teardown-v1 plan from the same delete-aifactory prepare. Its unlink-hub stage removes only this factory's own private DNS links and both sides of its peerings inside the configured connectivity hub; the operator-teardown stage then deletes the bootstrap-proven groups in dependency order, groups last. The CLI and SDK reject any link outside a protected hub, any deletion that touches the hub, and any change after the plan hash. Verified absence removes the draft from the catalog.

deletion_plan.access_hubs is [] unless the factory's own groups hold a factory-owned integrated access hub (factory-owned-access-hub-v1): the VPN gateway, Bastion, DNS resolver, private DNS zones or private runner that its integrated access-hub bootstrap created. A hub-connected factory keeps its VPN gateway in the shared hub, so its entry can cover only the Bastion Developer (it cannot traverse peering, so the bootstrap puts it in the common VNet) or a DNS resolver or ruleset in its own groups; a VPN gateway there blocks. The API proves this from consumed bootstrap stage records only and refuses when any other registered factory or scale set references the hub. Each entry lists proven_resource_ids, the exact deleted_resources from the common stage, the bootstrap evidence and executor: "operator-after-project-barrier". The runtime requires every DNS zone link and VNet peering to target only VNets the cohort deletes, blocks site connections, and tears the hub and runner down last, after every project pipeline. A shared hub such as aifactory-connectivity stays protected; the SDK, CLI and MAUI reject a VPN gateway or Bastion deletion outside access_hubs.

deletion_plan.shared_hub_links is [] unless a hub-connected factory's bootstrap created a hub-side VNet peering or private DNS links (named aif-<hash>) inside the shared connectivity hub (shared-hub-spoke-links-v1). Each entry names the kept hub_resource_group_ids, the links to remove (each with the spoke VNet it targets), retained_links (links to this factory's VNet that the bootstrap records do not prove; they are never deleted) and executor: "operator-after-common-teardown". The operator removes those links as the very last step, after every project pipeline and the whole common teardown, and only while each link still targets its spoke VNet and that VNet is verifiably gone; a link Azure already cleared counts as removed. The hub VNet, gateway, Bastion, DNS resolver, zones, rulesets, the hub group and every other factory's links stay. The CLI renders the section and rejects any link outside the hub, any link to a VNet the same scale set does not delete, and any hub group that a stage deletes.

Draft guards also check protected parameter profiles, ownership, registered pipeline connections, bootstrap references and projects shared across scale sets. An optional scale_set_id on project resource deletion identifies an existing placement; it does not replace or broaden the explicit environments.

docs.title: Get started - Agent & ML Factory SDK: Project team
docs.text:
Build the code of your workload in your project. The shared engines of the factories stay as they are. To configure and administer the Factory itself, use the core-team CLI, Python SDK and REST tutorials.

Your workload Start here Your first result Agent, RAG or multi-agent application Agent Factory SDK List the catalog, then make a plan for one target without calling Azure. Machine-learning model ML Model Factory SDK Validate a scenario and see its route. You can also train on a local CSV file.

Looking for a template to start from? Search the code templates library.

docs.title: Work on your machine first
docs.text:
1. Copy the examples into the repository of your project, and keep your configuration there.
  2. Install the packages into the Python environment of the component, rather than upgrading them globally.
  3. Keep tenant settings, credentials and generated files out of a public repository.
  4. Run the offline examples first. They need no Azure sign-in and create nothing in Azure.
  5. Before a live step, check the target with your platform team: the identity, the private network, the terms of the dataset and the budget. A live step stops when the project lacks something it needs. Fix that first, then run it again.

Each tutorial links to its full guide, the source code and the notebooks.

docs.title: Agent Factory SDK
docs.text: Maintained source guide

docs.title: Project-team quickstart
docs.text: Use the existing agent_factory Python modules for agent definitions and single-target operator commands. This is different from the core team's azurefactory administration client. There is no separate published AgentFactoryClient to install.

docs.title: 1. Prepare your project copy
docs.text:
From the repository root, or use the equivalent copied directory aifactory-usecase-code\40-agent-factory in the repository of your project:

Set-Location .\usecase_code\40-agent-factory
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m agent_factory --help

Keep your project configuration outside generated use-case code: copy config.example.json to aifactory\agent-factory\config.json, then have the operator resolve the target key, environment, variables-file path and selected storage profile. Do not run the unresolved example against Azure. See configuration ownership and storage selection.

docs.title: 2. Inspect agent definitions offline with Python
docs.text:
Save this as inspect_agents.py in the Agent Factory root and run .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe .\inspect_agents.py. It reads the maintained catalog without credentials, network access, model calls, deployment or local writes.

import json
from agent_factory.catalog import agent_catalog

agents = agent_catalog()
print(json.dumps([
    {"name": agent["name"], "kind": agent["kind"],
     "framework": agent["framework"], "role": agent["metadata"]["aifactory.role"]}
    for agent in agents
], indent=2))

The default catalog contains knowledge/reviewer/documentation prompt agents, hosted framework examples and a multi-agent helpdesk team. An entry defines an agent. It says nothing yet about what is deployed in your project. Read the real catalog, prompt agents, hosted examples and multi-agent examples.

docs.title: 3. Make an offline single-target plan
docs.text:
Save this separate program as plan_agents.py in the same directory. Supply the absolute path to your reviewed project configuration and its exact target key when prompted. plan validates your local configuration only. It doesn't sign in to Azure, look up resources or test the connection.

import json
from pathlib import Path
from agent_factory.cli import parser, run

config_path = Path(input("Reviewed configuration path: ").strip()).resolve(strict=True)
target_key = input("Exact target key from that configuration: ").strip()
if not target_key:
    raise ValueError("Select one target explicitly.")
arguments = parser().parse_args([
    "plan", "--config", str(config_path), "--target", target_key,
])
plan = run(arguments)
assert plan["mutations"] is False
print(json.dumps({"mutations": plan["mutations"],
                  "agents": [agent["name"] for agent in plan["agents"]]}, indent=2))

The equivalent CLI plan is also offline:

$config = Read-Host "Absolute reviewed configuration path"
$target = Read-Host "Exact target key"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m agent_factory plan --config $config --target $target

docs.title: 4. Optional live work: review before applying
docs.text:
Stop after the plan unless the operator has reviewed the target, existing Foundry/model resources, selected data account, dataset terms, private DNS, identity permissions and cost budget. discover and preflight read Azure; they are not offline tests. Ingestion, knowledge configuration and deployment are distinct mutations requiring --apply; invocation can incur model costs.

Follow the maintained operator commands and ingestion/knowledge/deployment sequence for one explicit --target. Ask your platform team before you enable public access, approve a private link or change a policy, and use the resource names of your project. Python integrations use the actual selection and command entry points, OAuth-backed project_client and prompt lifecycle and hosted deployment implementation; the operator CLI preserves the same ownership, storage and grounding checks.

For source-bound RAG use 45-rag-agent, not an unbounded storage scan. Continue with the ML Model Factory SDK when your project also trains models.

docs.title: ML Model Factory SDK
docs.text: Maintained source guide

docs.title: Project-team quickstart
docs.text: The Python import is ml_model_factory; install from the maintained usecase_code\50-ml-model-factory project or its copy in the repository of your project. Configure scenarios under user-config; do not edit shared engines or generated notebooks.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the local environment
docs.text:
From the repository root:

Set-Location .\usecase_code\50-ml-model-factory
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e ".[train]"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ml_model_factory --help
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ml_model_factory validate --scenario user-config\model\scenarios\diabetes.json
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ml_model_factory usecases --pattern batch --task-folder classification --technology notebook

Use Python 3.10–3.13 and the declared dependency ranges. Package installation needs access to your approved package feed; the following examples themselves make no cloud calls. train installs local training dependencies, not Azure credentials or compute.

docs.title: 2. Validate configuration and inspect a route with Python
docs.text:
Save as inspect_model.py in the model-factory root and run .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe .\inspect_model.py. This reads the existing scenario and catalog without downloading data, training or writing files.

import json
from pathlib import Path
from ml_model_factory.config import load_json, validate_scenario
from ml_model_factory.usecases import describe, find

scenario = validate_scenario(load_json(Path("user-config/model/scenarios/diabetes.json")))
route = find("batch", "classification", "notebook")
print(json.dumps({"scenario": scenario["name"],
                  "features": scenario["features"],
                  "route": describe(route, [scenario])}, indent=2))

Choose batch, online or streaming, then a task and technology from the use-case catalog. The local classification notebook and its prerequisites reuse the same engines. A supported catalog entry or rendered notebook is not evidence that its cloud training or serving route has succeeded.

docs.title: 3. Optional local CSV preparation, training and evaluation
docs.text:
Prerequisites: an already-reviewed, local diabetes.csv matching the scenario's features and label, dataset licensing/terms, and the local train dependencies above. Data is not bundled with the starter. No Kaggle credentials or network download is hidden here; see the explicit ingest implementation if you separately choose ingestion.

This teaching scenario is not clinical decision support. Review missing values, cohort representativeness and intended use. Do not substitute arbitrary data, lower quality thresholds or treat a passing tutorial as production approval.

Save as train_local.py in the model-factory root and run it with the component interpreter. Each run uses a fresh output folder and preserves the scenario's split, estimator and quality gates. Only local artifacts are produced.

import json
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4
from ml_model_factory.config import load_json, validate_scenario
from ml_model_factory.data import prepare
from ml_model_factory.training import train
from ml_model_factory.evaluation import evaluate

scenario = validate_scenario(load_json(Path("user-config/model/scenarios/diabetes.json")))
csv_path = Path(input("Path to the reviewed local diabetes.csv: ").strip()).resolve(strict=True)
run_dir = Path("ml-environment/outputs/diabetes") / ("local-" + uuid4().hex)
prepared, model, report = run_dir / "prepared", run_dir / "model", run_dir / "report"
manifest = prepare(scenario, csv_path, prepared)
train(scenario, prepared, model)
evaluation = evaluate(scenario, prepared, model, report)
print(json.dumps({"output": str(run_dir), "split_rows": manifest["split_rows"],
                  "metrics": evaluation["metrics"]}, indent=2))

Inspect prepared\manifest.json, the local MLflow model and report\metrics.json, quality-gate.json, comparison.json and responsible-ai.json. A failed gate raises an error and records the failure; stop and investigate rather than changing its result. This code neither registers a model nor deploys an endpoint.

CLI equivalents are prepare --scenario ... --input ... --output ..., train --scenario ... --prepared ... --model-output ... and evaluate --scenario ... --prepared ... --model ... --output ...; use python -m ml_model_factory <command> --help for the exact arguments.

docs.title: 4. Optional Azure work and gated registration
docs.text:
First create your own runtime.local.json with operator-reviewed existing workspace, compute, environment and storage bindings; see project-specific settings, offline preview and the model-factory guide. Install the declared azure extra only for that path. Approved identity/private connectivity, compatible pinned environments and cost budgets are prerequisites, not outcomes of this tutorial.

For Azure ML SDK v2, the real functions are render, submit, registration_definition and register. render writes local job definitions; submit creates a billed cloud run. Registration requires a completed factory pipeline with matching scope, evaluation lineage and a passing downloaded quality gate. Local training files alone cannot satisfy that cloud registration contract.

The following is a function definition only; it makes no cloud call until you explicitly invoke it after reviewing the completed job and its target. Keep the real champion's compatible held-out evaluation and selection policy. The first-model case is a separate explicit policy decision, not a default.

from pathlib import Path
from ml_model_factory.config import load_json, validate_runtime
from ml_model_factory.azureml import register

def register_reviewed_winner(runtime_path: Path, completed_job_name: str,
                             model_name: str, policy_path: Path,
                             champion_report_path: Path) -> str:
    runtime = validate_runtime(load_json(runtime_path))
    policy = load_json(policy_path)
    champion = load_json(champion_report_path)
    return register(completed_job_name, runtime, model_name,
                    selection_policy=policy, champion_evaluation=champion)

See the full SDK/CLI registration and selection tutorial and actual SDK wrapper / CLI v2 wrapper. Endpoint deployment is a further reviewed operation; serving CLI mutations preview unless --execute is supplied. Cloud routes can still fail because of environment, data, networking or backend limitations. No live ML success is claimed here, and no implementation repair or gate bypass is part of onboarding.

For agent workloads, start with the Agent Factory SDK.

docs.title: Setup docs: set up your AI Factory
docs.text: Go from an empty Azure subscription to a working AI Factory with its first project and its first agent. These pages are for the platform team (the core team) that creates and runs the Factory.

docs.title: Many tools, one goal
docs.text: Every tool is an L1 client of the same Factory API, so the result is the same whichever you pick. The app, the azurefactory CLI (in PowerShell or Bash), the Python SDK and REST all send the same six scenario calls. See the onion architecture for the layers below your tool.

docs.title: Run it guided
docs.text: The ESAF Tutorial Guide is a Windows app (installed as ESAF Tutorials) that runs the same quickstarts with you. It types each command, checks every step and plays a video of each scenario. Pick the tutorial for your tool (CLI, Python SDK or REST), then the track Scenarios 1-3 to build or Scenarios 4-6 to clean up. It runs on Windows. On Linux and macOS, follow the quickstarts with the CLI (bash), Python SDK or REST tab. Download the ESAF Tutorial Guide. It's a private preview: ask Joakim Åström on LinkedIn for a preview code.

docs.title: Run it yourself or from your service desk
docs.text: You can run the scenarios yourself, or let teams order projects from ServiceNow, Jira Service Management or your own portal. Your automation then calls the same Factory API. See ITSM integration.

docs.title: Quickstart: Install the ESAF tools
docs.text:
In this quickstart, you install one ESAF tool, start the Factory API and check that they connect. The Factory API is the one service that every tool calls. It ships inside the app, so you don't install it separately.

Tip

Run it guided. The ESAF Tutorial Guide types each command for you and checks every step: it also starts its own Factory API. Open an ESAF tutorial and the track Scenarios 1-3. Download the ESAF Tutorial Guide. It's a private preview: ask Joakim Åström on LinkedIn for a preview code.

Every tool is an L1 client of the same Factory API, so the result is the same whichever you pick. See the onion architecture.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Windows x64: Git for Windows, which includes Git Bash. For the CLI (PowerShell) tab, also PowerShell 7.3 or later.
  • Linux or macOS: Git and Bash. Use the CLI (bash), Python SDK or REST tab. The one-call scenarios need the app package v0.47.100 or later. Check the download table: a Linux or macOS package older than that starts the API, but it doesn't have the one-call scenarios yet.
  • Azure CLI and Python 3.10 or later.
  • A Git repository for your Factory's configuration, in GitHub or Azure DevOps. This is your consumer repository.

docs.title: Start the Factory API
docs.text:
The Factory API ships inside the AIFactory Config Wizard, a desktop app for Windows, Linux and macOS.

  1. Download the AIFactory Config Wizard for your system.
  2. Extract the archive. On Windows, keep the _internal folder beside aifactory-config.exe.
  3. Open the app. On Windows, that's aifactory-config.exe. For the other systems, see macOS and Linux.
  4. In the left menu, select Quick setup, then Start API host. Do this before you open any other window in the app, so that you choose the key.
  5. In the API Host Authentication dialog, enter a private API key. You choose it; remember it for the next steps.
  6. Copy the API address from the API Host Started dialog. The default is http://127.0.0.1:8765. The status bar shows it too.

Keep the app open. The API stops when you close it.

docs.title: Create your Factory folder
docs.text:
Your Factory's configuration lives in an azurefactory folder in your consumer repository.

  1. Open Bash in the root of your consumer repository. On Windows, that's Git Bash.
  2. Add this repository as a submodule and create the folder:
git submodule add -b release/v1.25 https://github.com/jostrm/azure-enterprise-scale-ml
bash ./azure-enterprise-scale-ml/01-start-v125-and-above.sh

Expected output, among other lines:

Initialized empty register: C:\work\team-factory\azurefactory\register.json

The script creates azurefactory\register.json with no factories in it. It changes nothing in Azure. See folder structure.

docs.title: Connect your tool
docs.text:
Choose one tool. You can add the others later; they all use the same API address, key and folder.

AppCLI (PowerShell)CLI (bash)Python SDKREST (curl)

The App tabs use Enterprise Scale AI Factory, the ESAF desktop app for Windows 11. It starts its own Factory API, so you can skip "Start the Factory API" above.

  1. Install the app from its download folder. You need version 1.0.24 or later.
  2. Open Enterprise Scale AI Factory from Start.
  3. On Start Guide, under Consumer repository root, select Browse repository and pick your consumer repository.

Open PowerShell in the root of your consumer repository:

python -m pip install .\azure-enterprise-scale-ml\environment_setup\azurefactory-cli
$env:AIFACTORY_API_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:8765'
$env:AIFACTORY_API_KEY = Read-Host 'API key you entered in the app'
$env:ESAF_FOLDER = (Resolve-Path .\azurefactory).Path
azurefactory health

Open Bash in the root of your consumer repository:

python3 -m pip install ./azure-enterprise-scale-ml/environment_setup/azurefactory-cli
export AIFACTORY_API_URL='http://127.0.0.1:8765'
read -r -s -p 'API key you entered in the app: ' AIFACTORY_API_KEY && export AIFACTORY_API_KEY
export ESAF_FOLDER="$PWD/azurefactory"
azurefactory health

In Git Bash on Windows, the API needs a Windows path: export ESAF_FOLDER="$(cygpath -w "$PWD/azurefactory")".

Install the SDK and set the connection once. This is PowerShell; on Linux or macOS, use the three export lines from the CLI (bash) tab instead:

python -m pip install .\azure-enterprise-scale-ml\environment_setup\azurefactory-cli
$env:AIFACTORY_API_KEY = Read-Host 'API key you entered in the app'
$env:ESAF_FOLDER = (Resolve-Path .\azurefactory).Path

Then save this as check_connection.py and run it:

from azurefactory import esaf

session = esaf.connect()  # reads ESAF_FOLDER, AIFACTORY_API_URL and AIFACTORY_API_KEY
catalog = session.client.catalog_list(session.folder)
print([factory["key"] for factory in catalog["factories"]])

Open Bash (on Windows: Git Bash). Health needs no key:

curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:8765/health

List the scenario routes that the API serves:

curl --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:8765/openapi.json \
  | grep -o '"/api/v1/esaf/[^"]*"' | sort -u

Every other request needs your key in the X-API-Key header.

docs.title: Verify the result
docs.text:
Your tool reaches the API, and your folder holds no factory yet.

Tool Expected output App The status light at the bottom shows API connected. CLI, in either shell azurefactory health prints "status": "ok". Python SDK The script prints []. REST The second command lists seven routes that start with /api/v1/esaf/.

For example, the CLI prints:

{
  "status": "ok",
  "version": "1.0.0"
}

If something goes wrong:

Message Fix AIFACTORY_API_KEY is required, or HTTP 401 Set the key again. It must match the key you entered in the app. The Factory API has no /api/v1/esaf routes Your app package is older than v0.47.100. Download the current package. On Linux and macOS, check the download table for a package with that version. Select an absolute local factory folder without traversal. Set ESAF_FOLDER with Resolve-Path, as shown. ModuleNotFoundError: azurefactory Run the pip install line again with the same python.

docs.title: Quickstart: Create your AI Factory
docs.text:
In this quickstart, you create your AI Factory and its first project with one call. An AI Factory is the shared part that every project uses: the network, private DNS, monitoring and the deployment pipelines.

Tip

Run it guided. The ESAF Tutorial Guide types each command for you and checks every step: open an ESAF tutorial and the track Scenarios 1-3. Download the ESAF Tutorial Guide. It's a private preview: ask Joakim Åström on LinkedIn for a preview code.

The scenario video, 9 minutes. Watch it in the ESAF Tutorial Guide under Resources > Scenario videos.

When you finish, you have this in your Dev subscription:

flowchart LR
  F(AI Factory):::purple --> S(Dev<br/>scale set 001):::purple
  S --> C(Common<br/>resource group:<br/>network, DNS,<br/>monitoring):::blue

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The tools from Quickstart: Install the ESAF tools, with the Factory API running. The one-file examples on this page need the app package v0.47.101 or later.
  • An Azure subscription for Dev, where you can create resource groups and assign roles.
  • A signed-in Azure CLI: run az login --tenant <your tenant ID>.
  • For GitHub Actions: GitHub CLI, signed in, and access to your consumer repository.
  • For Azure DevOps: access to your organization, project and repository.
  • A free private address range for the Factory's virtual network, for example 10.140.0.0/16.

docs.title: Choose your topology
docs.text:
Pick one hub mode and one networking mode. Every tool supports the same combinations.

You want Hub mode Networking mode Keep in mind The fastest first test Standalone, no hub Public You can't run Agent Chat on it. The full path, with Agent Chat Own hub Private The Factory creates a VPN gateway, which takes longer and costs more. To join your landing zone External hub Private or hybrid Your hub must exist first.

Private networking needs a hub. Agent Chat needs private or hybrid networking and a way in, such as a VPN. Read hub and network modes before you choose, because the hub mode is part of how the Factory is built.

docs.title: Describe your Factory
docs.text:
The Factory API needs to know what to build. Choose one of four ways: three use one file, for the CLI, the Python SDK and REST, and one uses the app. None of them creates anything in Azure.

In a file, you describe the whole Factory once. Save it as create-factory.json in the root of your consumer repository. It has up to three parts:

Part What it describes creation_request The Factory, its first scale set and project 001 scale_set_settings Your own VNet or subnets for the first scale set. Leave it out and ESAF builds the network. project_settings The services of project 001, such as API Management, the Factory MCP and Agent Chat

The API saves the two settings parts before anything deploys, so the first run already uses them.

In a file: automated networking

ESAF builds the VNet and its subnets from dev_vnet_cidr. This example is the fastest first test: standalone, public networking and GitHub Actions.

{
  "creation_request": {
    "contract_version": 1,
    "mode": "full-bootstrap",
    "action": "create-factory",
    "folder": "<absolute path of your azurefactory folder>",
    "orchestrator": "gha",
    "factory_key": "acme-ai",
    "region_short_name": "sdc",
    "config": {
      "subscription_id": "<your Dev subscription ID>",
      "tenant_id": "<your tenant ID>",
      "location": "swedencentral",
      "factory_prefix": "acme-",
      "aifactory_version": "1.25",
      "scale_set_number": "001",
      "project_number": "001",
      "repo_root": "<absolute path of your consumer repository>",
      "github_repository": "<owner>/<your consumer repository>",
      "github_visibility": "private",
      "dev_vnet_cidr": "10.140.0.0/16",
      "cost_center": "123456",
      "coordination_mode": "single-writer",
      "identity_mode": "create",
      "runner_mode": "self-hosted",
      "team_member_email": "<your sign-in email>",
      "team_group_name": "acme-ai-team",
      "access_hub_mode": "integrated",
      "setup_hub_access": false,
      "network_mode": "public"
    }
  },
  "project_settings": {
    "ENABLE_KONG": "false",
    "ENABLE_APIM": "true",
    "enableAIFactoryMCP": "true",
    "addAIFactoryMCP2APIM": "true",
    "enableFactoryChatAgent": "true"
  }
}

On Windows, write each backslash in a path twice, for example C:\\work\\team-factory\\azurefactory.

Change these values in creation_request before you use the file:

Setting What it does folder, repo_root Point to your azurefactory folder and to the repository that holds it, as absolute paths. subscription_id, tenant_id Select where the Factory deploys. Nothing is taken from your Azure sign-in. location, region_short_name Set the Azure region and its short name, for example swedencentral and sdc. factory_key Names the Factory in your folder, for example acme-ai. It isn't a secret. factory_prefix Starts every resource name. Keep it to six characters or fewer. dev_vnet_cidr Sets the Factory's private address range. It must not overlap your hub or a peered network. team_member_email, team_group_name Create or reuse the Microsoft Entra group that gets access to project 001. github_repository Names the consumer repository that runs the pipelines. access_hub_mode, setup_hub_access, network_mode Set the topology. See the values for each hub mode.

The project_settings in this example turn on API Management, the Factory MCP and its publication in API Management, and the Factory chat agent. addAIFactoryMCP2APIM needs enableAIFactoryMCP, so the file turns on both. Agent Chat has its own prerequisites: see Quickstart: Create your first agent by enabling ESAF Agent Chat.

Keep create-factory.json out of Git if you treat your subscription IDs as private.

In a file: BYO VNet

You bring the VNet, and ESAF creates the subnets in it. scale_set_settings names your VNet. byoVnetResourcegroupName and byoVnetName are the friendly names of the variables vnetResourceGroup_param and vnetNameFull_param.

{
  "creation_request": {
    "contract_version": 1,
    "mode": "full-bootstrap",
    "action": "create-factory",
    "folder": "<absolute path of your azurefactory folder>",
    "orchestrator": "gha",
    "factory_key": "acme-ai",
    "region_short_name": "sdc",
    "config": {
      "subscription_id": "<your Dev subscription ID>",
      "tenant_id": "<your tenant ID>",
      "location": "swedencentral",
      "factory_prefix": "acme-",
      "aifactory_version": "1.25",
      "scale_set_number": "001",
      "project_number": "001",
      "repo_root": "<absolute path of your consumer repository>",
      "github_repository": "<owner>/<your consumer repository>",
      "github_visibility": "private",
      "dev_vnet_cidr": "10.140.0.0/16",
      "cost_center": "123456",
      "coordination_mode": "single-writer",
      "identity_mode": "create",
      "runner_mode": "self-hosted",
      "team_member_email": "<your sign-in email>",
      "team_group_name": "acme-ai-team",
      "access_hub_mode": "integrated",
      "setup_hub_access": false,
      "network_mode": "public"
    }
  },
  "scale_set_settings": {
    "byoVnetResourcegroupName": "<resource group of your VNet>",
    "byoVnetName": "<name of your VNet>"
  },
  "project_settings": {
    "ENABLE_KONG": "false",
    "ENABLE_APIM": "true",
    "enableAIFactoryMCP": "true",
    "addAIFactoryMCP2APIM": "true",
    "enableFactoryChatAgent": "true"
  }
}

Change the values in creation_request as described under "In a file: automated networking".

In a file: BYO subnets

You bring the VNet and its subnets, and ESAF creates no network. enableByoSubnets is the friendly name of the variable BYO_subnets. The file has no dev_vnet_cidr, because there is no network for ESAF to plan: the API refuses a request that has both.

{

    "contract_version": 1,
    "mode": "full-bootstrap",

    "factory_key": "acme-ai",
    "region_short_name": "sdc",
    "config": {
      "subscription_id": "<your Dev subscription ID>",
      "tenant_id": "<your tenant ID>",
      "location": "swedencentral",
      "factory_prefix": "acme-",
      "aifactory_version": "1.25",
      "scale_set_number": "001",
      "project_number": "001",
      "repo_root": "<absolute path of your consumer repository>",
      "github_repository": "<owner>/<your consumer repository>",
      "github_visibility": "private",
      "cost_center": "123456",

      "identity_mode": "create",

      "team_group_name": "acme-ai-team",
      "access_hub_mode": "integrated",

      "network_mode": "public"
    }
  },
  "scale_set_settings": {
    "byoVnetResourcegroupName": "<resource group of your VNet>",
    "byoVnetName": "<name of your VNet>",
    "enableByoSubnets": true,
    "subnetCommon": "snet-dev-esml-cmn-001",
    "subnetProjGenAI": "snt-dev-prj001-genai"
  },
  "project_settings": {
    "ENABLE_KONG": "false",
    "ENABLE_APIM": "true",
    "enableAIFactoryMCP": "true",
    "addAIFactoryMCP2APIM": "true",
    "enableFactoryChatAgent": "true"
  }
}

Your subnets must exist before the run. Name each one you bring with its subnet… variable: the list is under networking in the variable reference. Change the values in creation_request as described under "In a file: automated networking".

In the app: Full bootstrap

Use the Enterprise Scale AI Factory app from Quickstart: Install the ESAF tools. The saved form is your draft.

  1. On Start Guide, select Use Full bootstrap. It supports GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps, every hub mode and every networking mode.
  2. Under Where will your pipelines run?, choose GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps.
  3. Fill in the form. It asks for the same values as the creation request: subscription, tenant, region, prefix, VNet range, team and repository.
  4. Select Save local configuration.

For the smallest form, select Use Simple Mode instead: GitHub Actions, Dev and private networking.

docs.title: Create the Factory
docs.text:
Warning

Running a scenario is the approval. It deploys billable resources to Azure, and there is no separate confirm step.

AppCLI (PowerShell)CLI (bash)Python SDKREST (curl)
  1. Save your draft as described under "In the app: Full bootstrap".
  2. Open the menu and select Configuration wizard > Quick setup & tear down.
  3. Select 1. Init AI Factory.
  4. Tick I approve this scenario: it runs at once and changes Azure., then select Run selected scenario.
  5. Follow Job status on the same page until it shows that the job succeeded.
azurefactory esaf init-factory --request-json .\create-factory.json --wait

--wait follows the job to its end. Without it, the command prints a job ID that you follow with azurefactory esaf job <job ID> --wait. Did you save a draft in the app instead? Then leave out --request-json.

azurefactory esaf init-factory --request-json ./create-factory.json --wait

--wait follows the job to its end. Without it, the command prints a job ID that you follow with azurefactory esaf job <job ID> --wait. Did you save a draft in the app instead? Then leave out --request-json.

import json

from azurefactory import esaf

request = json.load(open("create-factory.json", encoding="utf-8-sig"))
job = esaf.init_factory(**request)
print("Job", job.id)
state = job.wait()
print(state["status"], "-", state["message"])

Did you save a draft in the app instead? Then call esaf.init_factory() with no arguments.

In Bash, from the root of your consumer repository. On Windows, that's Git Bash. You need jq.

API_URL='http://127.0.0.1:8765'
read -r -s -p 'API key: ' API_KEY
FOLDER="$(cygpath -w "$PWD/azurefactory")"   # on Linux or macOS: FOLDER="$PWD/azurefactory"

jq -n --arg folder "$FOLDER" --slurpfile request create-factory.json \
  '{folder: $folder, approved: true} + $request[0]' |
  curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body -X POST "$API_URL/api/v1/esaf/init-factory" \
    --header "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @-

The API answers 202 Accepted with a job_id. Read the job until it ends:

curl --silent --show-error --get "$API_URL/api/v1/esaf/jobs/<job ID>" \
  --header "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" --data-urlencode "folder=$FOLDER"

The run takes about one hour, and up to 90 minutes in the recorded runs. You can stop waiting at any time; the job keeps running while the app stays open.

To change the project's settings later, send them with scenario 3: see Add a project. To add a scale set on another network, see Add a scale set.

docs.title: Verify the result
docs.text:
The job ends with status succeeded:

{
  "status": "succeeded"
}

The job also carries a message and the run it started.

Then check Azure:

az group list --subscription <your Dev subscription ID> --query "[].name" --output table

You see the common resource group and the project001 resource group. Their names start with your prefix. Your folder now holds the Factory under azurefactory\factories\<factory key>. Commit and push it.

Job status What to do accepted, preparing, confirming, running, retrying Wait. The job is still going. blocked Read blockers in the job, fix what they name, and run the scenario again. Finished steps are skipped. failed Read problem in the job. The API already retried the run twice. interrupted Run the scenario again. The API stopped before the run started.

docs.title: Clean up resources
docs.text:
To remove everything this quickstart created, delete the Factory with one call:

Tool Call CLI azurefactory esaf delete-factory --wait Python SDK esaf.delete_factory() REST POST /api/v1/esaf/delete-factory

See Quickstart: Clean up for what stays and what goes.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text:
Back: Quickstart: Install the ESAF tools

Next: Quickstart: Add a scale set. It's optional: to stay on one scale set, go to Quickstart: Add a project for your team.

Related:

  • The six scenarios: every call and its parameters.
  • Hub and network modes: the topology choices in detail.
  • Guide 19: review each change yourself before the API applies it.

docs.title: Quickstart: Add a scale set
docs.text:
In this quickstart, you add a second scale set to your AI Factory with one call. A scale set is one floor of the Factory: a virtual network and a common resource group that hold up to seven projects by default.

Tip

Run it guided. The ESAF Tutorial Guide types this call for you and checks every step: open an ESAF tutorial and the track Scenarios 1-3. It runs on Windows. Download the ESAF Tutorial Guide. It's a private preview: ask Joakim Åström on LinkedIn for a preview code.

The scenario video, 9 minutes. Watch it in the ESAF Tutorial Guide under Resources > Scenario videos.

AI-generated illustration.

You can skip this quickstart. Scale set 001 from the previous quickstart holds seven projects. Add a scale set when one of these is true:

When Example A floor is full Dev scale set 001 holds seven projects, and an eighth team asks for one. A group of projects needs its own network or subscription A business unit pays for its own projects.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A Factory from Quickstart: Create your AI Factory.
  • The Factory API running, and your tool connected. See Quickstart: Install the ESAF tools.
  • A free three-digit suffix, for example 002.
  • A free private address range for the new virtual network, for example 10.141.0.0/16. It must not overlap your hub, the first scale set or any network peered to them.

docs.title: Add the scale set
docs.text:
Warning

Running a scenario is the approval. It deploys billable resources to Azure, and there is no separate confirm step.

You name the suffix, the environment and the VNet range. The pipeline computes the subnets.

AppCLI (PowerShell)CLI (bash)Python SDKREST (curl)
  1. In the app, open the menu and select Configuration wizard > Quick setup & tear down.
  2. Select 2. Add scale set.
  3. Set Environment to dev, Scale set suffix to 002 and VNet range to 10.141.0.0/16.
  4. Tick I approve this scenario: it runs at once and changes Azure., then select Run selected scenario.
  5. Follow Job status on the same page until it shows that the job succeeded.
azurefactory esaf add-scale-set 002 dev --cidr 10.141.0.0/16 --wait

azurefactory esaf add-scale-set 002 dev --cidr 10.141.0.0/16 --wait

from azurefactory import esaf

job = esaf.add_scale_set("002", "dev", cidr="10.141.0.0/16")
state = job.wait()
print(state["status"], "-", state["message"])

In Bash, with API_URL, API_KEY and FOLDER set as in Quickstart: Create your AI Factory:

jq -n --arg folder "$FOLDER" \
  '{folder: $folder, approved: true, scale_set: "002", environment: "dev", cidr: "10.141.0.0/16"}' |
  curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body -X POST "$API_URL/api/v1/esaf/add-scale-set" \
    --header "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @-

The run takes 15 to 30 minutes. If it stops, run the same call again: it resumes, and it doesn't register the scale set twice.

Parameter What it does scale_set Sets the suffix, three digits as a string: "002". environment Selects "dev", "stage" or "prod". It's required. cidr Sets the VNet range of the new scale set. It's required for a new scale set. max_projects Sets how many projects the scale set holds. The default is 7. settings Sets scale-set settings, for example your own VNet and subnets. The CLI option is --settings-json. subscription_id, tenant_id, orchestrator Place the scale set in another subscription. Without them, it uses the same ones as the environment's first scale set. The CLI has no option for them: use Python or REST.

docs.title: Use your own VNet or subnets
docs.text:
By default, ESAF creates the VNet and its subnets from the range you give. To use your own network, pass scale-set settings with the same call.

You bring Settings The VNet. ESAF creates the subnets in it. byoVnetResourcegroupName and byoVnetName The VNet and its subnets The same two, enableByoSubnets set to true, and the names of your subnets

These are the friendly names of vnetResourceGroup_param, vnetNameFull_param and BYO_subnets. They need the app package v0.47.101 or later; the older names work in every version. Save the settings as scale-set-settings.json: they are the scale_set_settings part of the examples in Quickstart: Create your AI Factory. Then add them to the call:

Tool Call CLI, in either shell azurefactory esaf add-scale-set 002 dev --cidr <range of your VNet> --settings-json ./scale-set-settings.json --wait Python SDK esaf.add_scale_set("002", "dev", cidr="<range of your VNet>", settings=settings) REST Add "settings": {...} to the body of POST /api/v1/esaf/add-scale-set.

The API saves the settings before it deploys the scale set.

docs.title: Verify the result
docs.text:
The job ends with status succeeded, and your folder holds the new scale set:

azurefactory\factories\<your factory>\scalesets\002\scaleset_state.json

In Azure, you see one more common resource group, and the subscription's resource providers are registered:

az group list --subscription <your Dev subscription ID> --query "[?contains(name, 'common')].name" --output table

Dev now has two scale sets. From here on, name the scale set in every project call, for example --scale-set 001. Without it, the API can't tell which floor you mean.

If the call is refused:

Message Fix The call asks for cidr A new scale set needs its VNet range: add --cidr or cidr=. The range overlaps another network Pick a range that your hub, scale set 001 and their peered networks don't use. A job stays blocked Read blockers in the job, fix what they name, and run the call again.

docs.title: Clean up resources
docs.text:
Delete the scale set when it holds no project you need:

Tool Call CLI azurefactory esaf delete-scale-set 002 dev --wait Python SDK esaf.delete_scale_set("002", "dev") REST POST /api/v1/esaf/delete-scale-set

See Quickstart: Clean up.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text:
Back: Quickstart: Create your AI Factory

Next: Quickstart: Add a project for your team

Related:

  • The six scenarios: every call and its parameters.
  • Hub and network modes: how a scale set's network reaches the hub.
  • Folder structure: where a scale set lives in your folder.

docs.title: Quickstart: Add a project for your team
docs.text:
In this quickstart, you add a project for a team with one call, then change one of its settings with the same call. A project is one team's own resource group, with its AI services and its access group.

Tip

Run it guided. The ESAF Tutorial Guide types this call for you and checks every step: open an ESAF tutorial and the track Scenarios 1-3. Download the ESAF Tutorial Guide. It's a private preview: ask Joakim Åström on LinkedIn for a preview code.

The scenario video, 9 minutes. Watch it in the ESAF Tutorial Guide under Resources > Scenario videos.

Every project lives on a scale set, one floor of the Factory. This quickstart puts project 002 on Dev scale set 001, and names that scale set in every call. You must name it once Dev has more than one scale set, as it does after Quickstart: Add a scale set.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A Factory from Quickstart: Create your AI Factory.
  • The Factory API running, and your tool connected. See Quickstart: Install the ESAF tools.
  • A free three-digit project number, for example 002.

docs.title: Add the project
docs.text:
"Upsert" means add or update. A new project is registered and deployed. An existing project gets its settings saved and is deployed again.

AppCLI (PowerShell)CLI (bash)Python SDKREST (curl)
  1. In the app, open the menu and select Configuration wizard > Quick setup & tear down.
  2. Select 3. Add or update project.
  3. Set Environment to dev, Project number to 002 and Project scale set to 001.
  4. Tick I approve this scenario: it runs at once and changes Azure., then select Run selected scenario.
  5. Follow Job status on the same page until it shows that the job succeeded.
azurefactory esaf upsert-project 002 dev --scale-set 001 --wait

azurefactory esaf upsert-project 002 dev --scale-set 001 --wait

from azurefactory import esaf

job = esaf.upsert_project("002", "dev", scale_set="001")
state = job.wait()
print(state["status"], "-", state["message"])

In Bash, with API_URL, API_KEY and FOLDER set as in Quickstart: Create your AI Factory:

jq -n --arg folder "$FOLDER" \
  '{folder: $folder, approved: true, project: "002", environment: "dev", scale_set: "001"}' |
  curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body -X POST "$API_URL/api/v1/esaf/upsert-project" \
    --header "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @-

A new project takes about an hour: the recorded runs took 50 to 65 minutes.

docs.title: Change a setting
docs.text:
Send the same call with the settings you want to change. Settings you leave out keep their value.

AppCLI (PowerShell)CLI (bash)Python SDKREST (curl)
  1. On the same page, select 3. Add or update project and enter the same project.
  2. In Optional settings JSON, enter the settings to change, for example {"tag_costcenter": "lab"}.
  3. Tick I approve this scenario: it runs at once and changes Azure., then select Run selected scenario.
'{"tag_costcenter": "lab"}' | Set-Content .\project-settings.json
azurefactory esaf upsert-project 002 dev --scale-set 001 --settings-json .\project-settings.json --wait

echo '{"tag_costcenter": "lab"}' > project-settings.json
azurefactory esaf upsert-project 002 dev --scale-set 001 --settings-json ./project-settings.json --wait

from azurefactory import esaf

job = esaf.upsert_project("002", "dev", scale_set="001", settings={"tag_costcenter": "lab"})
print(job.wait()["status"])

jq -n --arg folder "$FOLDER" \
  '{folder: $folder, approved: true, project: "002", environment: "dev", scale_set: "001",
    settings: {tag_costcenter: "lab"}}' |
  curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body -X POST "$API_URL/api/v1/esaf/upsert-project" \
    --header "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @-
Parameter What it does project Sets the project number, three digits as a string: "002". environment Selects "dev", "stage" or "prod". It's required. scale_set Selects the scale set. It's required when the environment has more than one. settings Replaces the settings you name. display_name Gives a new project a display name.

docs.title: Verify the result
docs.text:
The job ends with status succeeded, and your folder holds the new project:

azurefactory\factories\<your factory>\scalesets\001\projects\project002\variables.json

In Azure, you see one more resource group, for project 002. After the settings change, its resources carry the new cost center tag.

If the call is refused:

Message Fix More than one dev scale set matches; pass scale_set. Name the scale set: --scale-set 001 or scale_set="001". environment must be dev, stage or prod Use one of the three names, in lower case. A job stays blocked Read blockers in the job, fix what they name, and run the call again.

docs.title: Clean up resources
docs.text:
Delete the project when the team no longer needs it:

Tool Call CLI azurefactory esaf delete-project 002 dev --wait Python SDK esaf.delete_project("002", "dev") REST POST /api/v1/esaf/delete-project

See Quickstart: Clean up.

docs.text:
Back: Quickstart: Add a scale set

Related:

  • The six scenarios: every call and its parameters.
  • Usage docs: hand the project over to the team.
