docs.title: Quickstart: Create your first agent by enabling ESAF Agent Chat
docs.text:
In this quickstart, you switch on ESAF Agent Chat for a project and ask it a first question. ESAF Agent Chat is a Microsoft Foundry agent with a private web chat and live voice. It answers questions about your Factory from your own documentation and code.

Tip

Run it guided. The ESAF Tutorial Guide types the project calls for you and checks every step: open an ESAF tutorial and the track Scenarios 1-3. Download the ESAF Tutorial Guide. It's a private preview: ask Joakim Åström on LinkedIn for a preview code. The guide has no Agent Chat lab yet.

sequenceDiagram
  participant You
  participant API as Factory API
  participant Run as Project pipeline
  participant Chat as Agent Chat app
  You->>API: upsert project with the four settings
  API->>Run: start the project run
  Run->>Chat: create the Foundry agent, then deploy the chat app
  You->>Chat: sign in and ask a question

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A project in Dev from Quickstart: Add a project for your team, or project 001 from Quickstart: Create your AI Factory. Any project number works. The examples use project 001 on scale set 001.
  • On that project: enableAIFoundry, enableAISearch and enableContainerApps set to "true".
  • Private or hybrid networking, so that the project's Container Apps environment is internal. A Factory with public networking can't run Agent Chat. See hub and network modes.
  • A chat model deployment that succeeded. The project setting modelGPTXName names it.
  • A text-embedding deployment that succeeded, for example text-embedding-3-large.
  • A Microsoft Entra admin who can create an app registration.
  • The Entra object IDs of the people who may use the chat. They get read-only access.
  • VPN or another route into the project's private network.

Important

The chat app deploys in Dev only. Runs for Stage and Prod skip it.

docs.title: Create the sign-in registration
docs.text:
An Entra admin does this once per project. Pipelines never write to Microsoft Entra. The commands in this section are PowerShell. In Bash, end a continued line with a backslash instead of a backtick.

  1. Find the address your chat app gets. The app name is aifactory-agent-project<NNN>-dev:
az containerapp env list --resource-group <project resource group> `
  --query "[0].properties.defaultDomain" --output tsv
  1. Copy config.example.json in usecase_code\40-agent-factory\40-aifactory-agent and put your own object ID under auth.grants.
  2. From that folder, plan the registration. Add --apply when the plan looks right:
python -m aifactory_agent.browser_auth --config ./my-agent.json `
  --redirect-uri "https://aifactory-agent-project001-dev.<default domain>/" `
  --user-object-id "<your Entra object ID>"
  1. Copy client_id from the output. You need it in the next step.

The tool gives sign-in access to you only. Ask your Entra admin to assign the other readers to the Enterprise Scale AI Factory Agent enterprise application. For the details, see authentication in the agent guide.

docs.title: Turn on the four settings
docs.text:
Agent Chat is an update of your project, so it's scenario 3 with four settings. The call saves the settings and then deploys them.

Setting What it does enableFactoryChatAgent Creates the Foundry prompt agent enterprise-scale-ai-factory. enableAIFactoryAgentLiveVoice Deploys the chat web app with live voice. Needs enableFactoryChatAgent. aifactoryAgentEntraAppId Sets the client ID of the sign-in registration. aifactoryAgentReaderObjectIds Lists 1 to 20 object IDs, comma-separated, that get read-only access. More settings Setting What it does aifactoryAgentContainerAppsEnvironment Names the internal environment. Empty picks the only one in the project resource group. aifactoryAgentModelDeployment Names the agent's own model deployment. Empty uses modelGPTXName. aifactoryAgentVoiceName Sets the voice. Empty uses en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural. aifactoryAgentVoiceLanguages Lists the input languages. Empty uses en-US; Swedish needs sv-SE,en-US. aifactoryAgentConfigFile Points to your own agent configuration file in your repository. It's merged over the generated one. AppCLI (PowerShell)CLI (bash)Python SDKREST (curl)
  1. In the app, open the menu and select Configuration wizard > Quick setup & tear down.
  2. Select 3. Add or update project, and enter your project: Environment dev, Project number 001 and Project scale set 001.
  3. In Optional settings JSON, enter the four settings, as in the agent-chat.json file on the CLI tabs.
  4. Tick I approve this scenario: it runs at once and changes Azure., then select Run selected scenario.

The same settings are checkboxes and fields under AI Factory Agent chat & live voice, on the Simple Mode page and in the Configuration wizard.

@{
  enableFactoryChatAgent        = 'true'
  enableAIFactoryAgentLiveVoice = 'true'
  aifactoryAgentEntraAppId      = '<client ID>'
  aifactoryAgentReaderObjectIds = '<object ID 1>,<object ID 2>'
} | ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content .\agent-chat.json

azurefactory esaf upsert-project 001 dev --scale-set 001 --settings-json .\agent-chat.json --wait

cat > agent-chat.json <<'JSON'
{
  "enableFactoryChatAgent": "true",
  "enableAIFactoryAgentLiveVoice": "true",
  "aifactoryAgentEntraAppId": "<client ID>",
  "aifactoryAgentReaderObjectIds": "<object ID 1>,<object ID 2>"
}
JSON

azurefactory esaf upsert-project 001 dev --scale-set 001 --settings-json ./agent-chat.json --wait

from azurefactory import esaf

job = esaf.upsert_project("001", "dev", scale_set="001", settings={
    "enableFactoryChatAgent": "true",
    "enableAIFactoryAgentLiveVoice": "true",
    "aifactoryAgentEntraAppId": "<client ID>",
    "aifactoryAgentReaderObjectIds": "<object ID 1>,<object ID 2>",
})
print(job.wait()["status"])

In Bash, with API_URL, API_KEY and FOLDER set as in Quickstart: Create your AI Factory:

jq -n --arg folder "$FOLDER" '{folder: $folder, approved: true, project: "001", environment: "dev",
  scale_set: "001",
  settings: {enableFactoryChatAgent: "true", enableAIFactoryAgentLiveVoice: "true",
    aifactoryAgentEntraAppId: "<client ID>", aifactoryAgentReaderObjectIds: "<object ID 1>,<object ID 2>"}}' |
  curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body -X POST "$API_URL/api/v1/esaf/upsert-project" \
    --header "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @-

Allow about an hour for the first run: the project run, plus about 30 minutes to build the knowledge index. Later runs are faster.

You can also deploy only the agent from a terminal, without a full project run. From your consumer repository root, ./GHA-azurefactory.sh add-aifactory-agent-chat --to-project 001 shows the plan, and --apply deploys. ADO-azurefactory.sh takes the same options.

docs.title: Ask your first question
docs.text:
1. Connect your VPN.
  2. Get the chat address:
az containerapp show --name aifactory-agent-project001-dev --resource-group <project resource group> `
  --query properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn --output tsv
  1. Open https://<that address>/ in Edge, Chrome, Safari or Firefox, and sign in with Microsoft.
  2. Ask: "What is the health of my AI Factory, and which skills can I use?"

You get a written answer with source citations. To talk instead, select Start talking and allow the microphone.

docs.title: Verify the result
docs.text:
The job ends with status succeeded, and the orb in the chat shows what the agent is doing:

Listening Thinking Speaking

If something goes wrong:

Symptom Fix The run fails on the live voice step Check the prerequisites: the agent, both model deployments and an internal Container Apps environment must exist. Voice is on but the chat agent isn't Set enableFactoryChatAgent to "true" too. Voice alone fails with a clear message. A reader can't sign in Assign that person to the enterprise application in Microsoft Entra. Voice is unavailable Select Use typed chat. Typing still works.

For more, see troubleshooting in guide 21.

docs.title: Clean up resources
docs.text:
Set both switches to "false" and run the same call again. Later runs then skip Agent Chat. This doesn't delete anything: the app, the index and the role assignments stay.

To remove them, follow teardown in the agent guide, or delete the whole project with Quickstart: Clean up.

docs.title: Quickstart: Clean up
docs.text:
In this quickstart, you delete a project, a scale set or your whole AI Factory with one call each. A delete removes the Azure resource groups that ESAF created, and nothing else.

Tip

Run it guided. The ESAF Tutorial Guide types each command for you and checks every step: open an ESAF tutorial and the track Scenarios 4-6. Download the ESAF Tutorial Guide. It's a private preview: ask Joakim Åström on LinkedIn for a preview code.

The scenario video, 9 minutes. Watch it in the ESAF Tutorial Guide under Resources > Scenario videos.

Scenario What goes What stays 4. Delete project The project's resource group, with its Key Vault Other projects, the scale set, the project's subnets 5. Delete scale set The scale set's project and common resource groups in that environment Other scale sets, other environments 6. Delete AI Factory Every project and common resource group, and the Factory's local configuration Hub resource groups, subscriptions, Entra groups, Git history

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A Factory from Quickstart: Create your AI Factory.
  • The Factory API running, and your tool connected. See Quickstart: Install the ESAF tools.
  • No other job running on the Factory. A second scenario waits until the first one ends.

docs.title: Delete what you no longer need
docs.text:
Caution

A delete is permanent, and running it is the approval. Check the project number and the environment before you press Enter. A delete never reaches another environment.

Run only the lines you need. To remove everything, the last line is enough. The first two lines delete project 002 and scale set 002 from the earlier quickstarts. The recorded project delete took about 30 minutes.

AppCLI (PowerShell)CLI (bash)Python SDKREST (curl)
  1. In the app, open the menu and select Configuration wizard > Quick setup & tear down.
  2. Select 4. Delete project, 5. Delete scale set or 6. Delete AI Factory, and enter the target.
  3. In Deletion phrase, type the phrase that the page asks for. It names what you delete.
  4. Tick I approve this scenario: it runs at once and changes Azure., then select Run selected scenario.
  5. Follow Job status on the same page until it shows that the job succeeded.
azurefactory esaf delete-project 002 dev --wait
azurefactory esaf delete-scale-set 002 dev --wait
azurefactory esaf delete-factory --wait

azurefactory esaf delete-project 002 dev --wait
azurefactory esaf delete-scale-set 002 dev --wait
azurefactory esaf delete-factory --wait

from azurefactory import esaf

job = esaf.delete_project("002", "dev", wait=True)
print(job.scenario, job.result["status"])
job = esaf.delete_scale_set("002", "dev", wait=True)
print(job.scenario, job.result["status"])
job = esaf.delete_factory(wait=True)
print(job.scenario, job.result["status"])

wait=True waits until the job ends, so each delete starts after the one before it.

In Bash, with API_URL, API_KEY and FOLDER set as in Quickstart: Create your AI Factory:

jq -n --arg folder "$FOLDER" '{folder: $folder, approved: true, project: "002", environment: "dev"}' |
  curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body -X POST "$API_URL/api/v1/esaf/delete-project" \
    --header "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @-

For a scale set, post scale_set and environment to /api/v1/esaf/delete-scale-set. For the whole Factory, post only folder and approved to /api/v1/esaf/delete-factory:

jq -n --arg folder "$FOLDER" '{folder: $folder, approved: true}' |
  curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body -X POST "$API_URL/api/v1/esaf/delete-factory" \
    --header "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @-

Two options change what a project delete removes:

Option What it does include_project_subnets=True, or --include-project-subnets Also deletes the project's subnets. include_keyvault_and_resource_group=False, or --keep-keyvault-and-resource-group Deletes only the project's services and keeps its Key Vault and resource group.

You don't grant a deletion permission first. The API grants it once for the Factory, then runs the delete.

docs.title: Verify the result
docs.text:
Each job ends with status succeeded. After a Factory delete, the resource groups are gone:

az group list --subscription <your Dev subscription ID> --query "[].name" --output table

Expected output: no resource group that starts with your Factory's prefix.

Job status What to do blocked Another job is still running on the Factory, or a review refused the delete. Read blockers in the job. A scale-set call says the target is unknown You skipped Quickstart: Add a scale set. Leave that line out. failed Read problem in the job, then run the same call again. Deletes that are already done are skipped.

docs.title: Clean up resources
docs.text:
A Factory delete keeps what other teams may share. Remove these yourself when you no longer need them:

  • The hub resource groups, if you created a hub only for this Factory.
  • The Microsoft Entra groups and the Agent Chat sign-in registration.
  • Your consumer repository.

Then close the app. That stops the Factory API.

docs.title: Quickstart: Run your first agent in your ESAF project
docs.text:
In this quickstart, you plan, deploy and ask your first agent in your ESAF project. You use a prompt agent: Microsoft Foundry runs its model and its tools, so you have no server to build.

Tip

This page gives you the short path. The template's own guide has every option: Foundry prompt agents.

You deploy aif-reviewer. It reviews a draft that you give it, so it needs no data of its own.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The usage prerequisites: an ESAF project, access to it and Python 3.13.
  • A Microsoft Foundry project with a chat model deployment in your ESAF project. Your platform team enables both.
  • From your platform team: your target key, for example project001-dev, and the path of your project's variables file.

docs.title: Prepare your environment
docs.text:
1. Open PowerShell in your checkout of this repository.
  2. Create the environment and install the tools:
Set-Location .\usecase_code\40-agent-factory
py -3.13 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r .\requirements.txt
  1. Copy config.example.json to a folder of your own, for example aifactory\agent-factory\config.json.
  2. In your copy, set the target key and the variables file path that your platform team gave you.
  3. Point two variables at them:
$Config = 'C:\work\my-project\aifactory\agent-factory\config.json'
$Target = 'project001-dev'

docs.title: Plan the agent offline
docs.text:
A plan reads only your configuration. It calls nothing in Azure.

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m agent_factory plan --config $Config --target $Target --agent aif-reviewer

To see every agent in the catalog first, save this as inspect_agents.py and run it with the same Python:

import json
from agent_factory.catalog import agent_catalog

print(json.dumps([{"name": agent["name"], "kind": agent["kind"]} for agent in agent_catalog()], indent=2))

docs.title: Deploy and ask the agent
docs.text:
1. Sign in: az login --tenant <your tenant ID>. Connect your VPN if your project is private.
  2. Check your access. This step only reads Azure:
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m agent_factory preflight --config $Config --target $Target
  1. Deploy the agent. This step changes your Foundry project:
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m agent_factory deploy --config $Config --target $Target --agent aif-reviewer --apply
  1. Ask it to review a draft. This call uses your model, so it can cost money:
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m agent_factory invoke --config $Config --target $Target --agent aif-reviewer `
  --input "Review this draft: Everyone must reset passwords daily. No evidence was supplied."

docs.title: Verify the result
docs.text:
The plan reports that it changes nothing:

{
  "mutations": false
}

The deploy step reports a version record with created or unchanged. The answer is JSON with agent, response_id and text. In text, the reviewer points out that the draft has no supporting evidence.

Symptom Fix The plan fails Check the target key and the variables file path in your configuration. Preflight can't reach Foundry Connect your VPN, and check that you're in your project's Entra group. The answer asks for a tool approval You invoked another agent. aif-reviewer has no tools by default.

docs.title: Clean up resources
docs.text:
The tools never delete an agent. To remove it, delete aif-reviewer in your Foundry project in the Foundry portal. Then remove your local environment:

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .\.venv

docs.title: Quickstart: Train your first model in your ESAF project
docs.text:
In this quickstart, you validate a scenario and train your first model on your own machine. A scenario is one JSON file that names your data, your features, your model and the quality gates it must pass.

Tip

This page gives you the short path. The template's own guide has every option: ML Model Factory: your configuration.

You train locally first. The same scenario then runs in Azure Machine Learning in your ESAF project.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The usage prerequisites: an ESAF project, access to it and Python 3.10 to 3.13.
  • A local diabetes.csv that matches the scenario's features and label. The data isn't bundled. Check its license before you use it.

docs.title: Prepare your environment
docs.text:
1. Open PowerShell in your checkout of this repository.
  2. Create the environment and install the package:
Set-Location .\usecase_code\50-ml-model-factory
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e ".[train]"

docs.title: Validate the scenario
docs.text:
Check the scenario, then list the routes it can take. Neither step calls Azure:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ml_model_factory validate --scenario user-config\model\scenarios\diabetes.json
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ml_model_factory usecases --pattern batch --task-folder classification --technology notebook

docs.title: Train and evaluate the model
docs.text:
Save this as train_local.py in the same folder, then run it with .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe .\train_local.py:

import json
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4
from ml_model_factory.config import load_json, validate_scenario
from ml_model_factory.data import prepare
from ml_model_factory.training import train
from ml_model_factory.evaluation import evaluate

scenario = validate_scenario(load_json(Path("user-config/model/scenarios/diabetes.json")))
csv_path = Path(input("Path to your local diabetes.csv: ").strip()).resolve(strict=True)
run_dir = Path("ml-environment/outputs/diabetes") / ("local-" + uuid4().hex)
prepared, model, report = run_dir / "prepared", run_dir / "model", run_dir / "report"
manifest = prepare(scenario, csv_path, prepared)
train(scenario, prepared, model)
evaluation = evaluate(scenario, prepared, model, report)
print(json.dumps({"output": str(run_dir), "metrics": evaluation["metrics"]}, indent=2))

The script prepares the data, trains the model and checks it against the scenario's quality gates. It writes only local files. It registers no model and deploys no endpoint.

docs.title: Verify the result
docs.text:
The script prints the output folder and the metrics. In that folder you find:

File What it tells you prepared\manifest.json Shows how the data was split. report\metrics.json Lists the model's metrics. report\quality-gate.json States whether the model passed its gates. report\responsible-ai.json Summarizes the responsible AI checks.

A failed gate raises an error. Investigate it; don't change the gate to make it pass.

This scenario is a teaching example. It isn't clinical decision support.

docs.title: Clean up resources
docs.text:
Nothing was created in Azure. Remove the local output and the environment:

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .\ml-environment\outputs\diabetes, .\.venv

docs.title: View your project dashboards
docs.text:
Your ESAF project comes with dashboards that answer three questions: what does it cost, how much is it used, and is it healthy? This page shows where each dashboard lives and how to open it for your project.

Before you start, check the usage prerequisites. You also need the Reader role on your project's resource group, which your project's Entra group gives you.

docs.title: Where the dashboards live
docs.text:
Dashboard Where it lives Best for Project dashboard Azure portal, in your project's resource group A daily look at cost, usage and shortcuts to your services My Project - Usage and Cost workbook Azure Monitor, linked from the project dashboard Token usage per model, resources per region and health Monitoring in the ESAF app Enterprise Scale AI Factory, the desktop app your platform team runs Reports across projects: value, cost, quality and security

All three read the same Azure sources: Cost Management for cost, and Azure Monitor for usage and health.

docs.title: Open your project dashboard
docs.text:
1. In the Azure portal, open your project's resource group.
  2. Filter the resources on the type Shared dashboard.
  3. Select your project's dashboard, then select Go to dashboard.

To find the resource group from a terminal:

az group list --subscription <your subscription ID> --query "[?contains(name, 'project001')].name" --output table

Your platform team deploys the dashboard with your project. If you can't find it, ask them to deploy it.

docs.title: Read the project dashboard
docs.text:
Area What you see Resource group, on the left Lists every resource in your project. Cost analysis, on the right Shows this month's accumulated cost for your project. Shortcuts Open Foundry, Storage, Key Vault, AI Search and Application Insights. Azure Machine Learning, Databricks and Data Factory appear when your project has them. Daily cost charts Show the daily total, and the daily total per service, with Azure's forecast. Foundry tiles Show requests, calls and content safety counts for the past 30 days. Report cards Open the Usage and Cost workbook.

The two cost charts show the same cost in two ways. Don't add them together.

docs.title: Read cost, usage and health
docs.text:
Question Where to look Keep in mind What does my project cost? Cost analysis and the daily cost charts These show actual billed cost. A forecast is a prediction, not a charge. How much is it used? The Foundry tiles and View > Model tokens in the workbook Token counts are usage, not cost. Don't turn them into money yourself. Is it healthy? The workbook's health section and Application Insights A number on the region map counts resources, not incidents.

Change the time range at the top of the dashboard. It starts at the past 30 days.

docs.title: Ask in the ESAF app
docs.text:
Your platform team can also open your project in the ESAF app, under Monitoring > My Project. It shows a Usage & outcomes tab beside a separate Cost tab, for one project and one environment at a time. Ask them for a report when you need numbers across several projects.

Back: Quickstart: Train your first model in your ESAF project

docs.title: The six ESAF scenarios
docs.text:
Every tool runs the same six scenarios, and each scenario is one call. The app, the azurefactory CLI, the Python SDK and REST are clients of the same Factory API, so the outcome is the same.

Scenario Python SDK Outcome 1. Init AI Factory esaf.init_factory() Starting from an empty subscription, creates the common part of the AI Factory, such as connectivity and private DNS zones, and the first project. 2. Add scale set esaf.add_scale_set("002", "dev", cidr="10.141.0.0/16") Prepares a new, empty Azure subscription by enabling resource providers, and creates the scale set's common resource group. 3. Add or update project esaf.upsert_project("002", "dev") Creates the project's resource group and assigns team access. Adds or removes resources, changes settings such as SKUs, or creates the project if it doesn't exist. 4. Delete project esaf.delete_project("002", "dev") Deletes the project's resource group. 5. Delete scale set esaf.delete_scale_set("002", "dev") Deletes the project and common resource groups, leaving an empty Azure subscription. 6. Delete AI Factory esaf.delete_factory() Deletes all project and common resource groups in every environment and removes the Factory's local configuration. Hub resource groups, Entra groups and Git repositories stay.

Running a scenario is the approval: it changes Azure. Each scenario has a quickstart that runs it step by step: 1, 2, 3 and 4 to 6.

docs.title: The same call in every tool
docs.text:
Scenario CLI REST 1 azurefactory esaf init-factory POST /api/v1/esaf/init-factory 2 azurefactory esaf add-scale-set 002 dev --cidr 10.141.0.0/16 POST /api/v1/esaf/add-scale-set 3 azurefactory esaf upsert-project 002 dev POST /api/v1/esaf/upsert-project 4 azurefactory esaf delete-project 002 dev POST /api/v1/esaf/delete-project 5 azurefactory esaf delete-scale-set 002 dev POST /api/v1/esaf/delete-scale-set 6 azurefactory esaf delete-factory POST /api/v1/esaf/delete-factory

The CLI commands are the same in PowerShell and in Bash. Every REST body carries "folder" and "approved": true. The API answers 202 Accepted with a job_id.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Used by What it does scale_set Scenarios 2 and 5; in 3 and 4 when the environment has more than one Names the scale set, three digits as a string: "002". project Scenarios 3 and 4 Names the project, three digits as a string: "002". environment Scenarios 2 to 5, required Selects "dev", "stage" or "prod". A delete never reaches another environment. cidr Scenario 2 Sets the new scale set's VNet range. The pipeline computes the subnets. max_projects Scenario 2 Sets how many projects the scale set holds. The default is 7. subscription_id, tenant_id, orchestrator Scenario 2, Python and REST Default to the environment's existing scale set. orchestrator is "gha" or "ado". The CLI has no option for them. settings Scenarios 2 and 3 In scenario 3, replaces the project settings you name; settings you leave out keep their value. In scenario 2, sets scale-set settings such as your own VNet and subnets. display_name Scenario 3 Gives a new project a display name. include_project_subnets Scenario 4 Also deletes the project's subnets. The default is False. include_keyvault_and_resource_group Scenario 4 False deletes only the project's services. The default is True. scale_set_settings, project_settings Scenario 1, with creation_request Save settings for the first scale set (your own VNet or subnets) and for project 001 (its services) before anything deploys. The CLI takes one file with all three parts: --request-json. Needs the app package v0.47.101 or later. creation_request Scenario 1 Saves a new Factory and starts it in one call. Leave it out to run the draft you saved in the app. The CLI option is --creation-request-json. See the example. retries All Sets how often the API runs the scenario again after a failed run: 0 to 5, default 2. version_ref All Deploys an explicit ESAF version instead of the Factory's own. wait, poll All, Python only wait=True follows the job to its end and reads it every poll seconds.

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text:
Each call returns a job at once. Follow it with job.wait(), azurefactory esaf job <job ID> --wait or GET /api/v1/esaf/jobs/{job_id}?folder=....

Status Meaning accepted, preparing, confirming, running, retrying The job is still going. succeeded The scenario finished. blocked A review refused it, or another job is running. Read blockers. failed The run failed after its retries. Read problem. interrupted The API stopped before the run started. Run the scenario again.

The CLI exits with 0 when the job succeeded or is still running, 3 when it was blocked and 5 when it failed.

docs.title: Errors
Hub and network modes
docs.text:
You make two network choices when you create an AI Factory. The hub mode decides how the Factory connects to the rest of your network. The networking mode decides how people reach the services inside it. Every tool and all six scenarios support the same combinations.

AI-generated illustration.

docs.title: Hub modes
docs.text:
A hub is the shared network that gives people a private way in: a VPN gateway, a DNS resolver and the private DNS zones.

Hub mode What you get Choose it when External hub The Factory connects to a hub that you already own, in its own subscription or resource group. You have a landing zone, or several Factories share one hub. Standalone, no hub The Factory keeps its network and private DNS zones in its own common resource group. You evaluate ESAF, run a workshop or want an isolated Factory. Own hub The Factory creates its own hub in its Dev network, with a VPN gateway and Bastion. You need private access and have no central hub. External hub Standalone, no hub Own hub

Select a diagram to open its animation.

docs.title: Networking modes
docs.text: Networking mode How people reach the services Private Only over the private network. Public access is off, so you need a VPN, Bastion or a machine inside the network. Hybrid Over the private network, and over the internet for the AI services that allow it. Public Over the internet. The project also gets a public perimeter.

docs.title: Which combinations work
docs.text:
Private networking needs a hub, because someone has to get in. A standalone Factory without a hub uses hybrid or public networking.

Hub mode Private Hybrid Public External hub Yes Yes Yes Standalone, no hub No: add a hub Yes Yes Own hub Yes Yes Yes

docs.title: Settings behind the choices
docs.text:
The app sets these for you. You only need the names when you automate the setup.

Setting External hub Standalone, no hub Own hub access_hub_mode external integrated integrated setup_hub_access Your choice false true network_mode private, hybrid or public hybrid or public private, hybrid or public

An external hub also needs four values that locate it: access_hub_subscription_id, access_hub_resource_group, access_hub_vnet_name and access_hub_vnet_cidr. An own hub also needs vpn_client_cidr, the address pool of its VPN clients. It must not overlap the Factory's VNet range.

These settings go in the config part of the creation request. See Quickstart: Create your AI Factory.

docs.title: Trade-offs
docs.text:
• External hub gives you one VPN and one set of DNS zones for all Factories. It needs a team that owns the hub.
  • Standalone, no hub is the fastest to create and the easiest to delete. It can't be private-only, and with public networking it can't run Agent Chat.
  • Own hub is self-contained and private. Each Factory then pays for its own VPN gateway.

A Factory delete keeps hub resource groups in every mode. See Quickstart: Clean up.

Next: Quickstart: Create your AI Factory

docs.title: Folder structure
docs.text: ESAF keeps your configuration in one azurefactory folder in your consumer repository. One folder can hold several AI Factories. The Factory API writes these files; you change them through a tool, not by hand.

docs.title: The azurefactory folder
docs.text:
azurefactory\
  register.json                       The register: every Factory in this folder
  factories\
    acme-ai\                          One AI Factory
      factory.json
      pipelines\
        ado.json                      Or gha.json: how the Factory reaches its pipelines
      scalesets\
        001\                          One scale set
          scaleset_state.json
          projects\
            project001\               One project
              project_state.json
              variables.json          The project's settings for Dev, Stage and Prod
Item What it holds register.json Commits the identity and configuration of every Factory together. factories\<key>\ Holds one Factory. The key is the name you gave it, for example acme-ai. scalesets\<suffix>\ Holds one scale set. The suffix is three digits, for example 001. projects\projectNNN\ Holds one project, for example project001. Every project lives under its scale set. variables.json Holds the project's settings, with a dev and a stage_prod section.

Dev, Stage and Prod are sections in variables.json, not extra folders. Keep credentials in a key vault, never in these files.

docs.title: Your consumer repository after setup
docs.text:
01-start-v125-and-above.sh adds the tools and an empty register to your consumer repository:

consumer-repository\
  azure-enterprise-scale-ml\          This repository, as a submodule
  azurefactory\
    register.json                     Empty until you create a Factory
    .azurefactory\                    Local API state: never commit it
  azurefactory.sh                     Runs the azurefactory CLI
  GHA-azurefactory.sh                 Terminal entry point for GitHub Actions
  ADO-azurefactory.sh                 Terminal entry point for Azure DevOps
  .azurefactory-tools\                A local copy of the CLI and SDK
  .gitignore                          Gains one line: .azurefactory/
Item What you do with it azurefactory\ Commit it. It's your Factory's configuration. azurefactory\.azurefactory\ Leave it out of Git. It holds the API's lock and operations database. azurefactory.sh and the two entry points Run them from the repository root.

Run the script again to refresh the tools. It keeps your register and your settings, and it backs up changed tool files under .aifactory-backups.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: This page lists the settings you meet in the quickstarts: how a tool connects to the Factory API, and the naming limits that apply to every Factory.

docs.title: Connection settings
docs.text:
Set the connection once. Every call then names only what it changes.

Setting Required What it does ESAF_FOLDER Yes Points to the absolute path of your azurefactory folder, on the machine that runs the API. AIFACTORY_API_KEY Yes Carries the API key you entered in the app. Never put it in a script, a URL or a log. AIFACTORY_API_URL No Sets the API address. The default is http://127.0.0.1:8765. ESAF_TIMEOUT No Sets how many seconds one request may take. The default is 1800. 
$env:AIFACTORY_API_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:8765'
$env:AIFACTORY_API_KEY = Read-Host 'API key you entered in the app'
$env:ESAF_FOLDER = (Resolve-Path .\azurefactory).Path

In Python, you can connect in code instead:

from azurefactory import esaf

esaf.connect(folder=r"C:\work\team-factory\azurefactory", url="http://127.0.0.1:8765", factory="acme-ai")
connect() parameter What it does folder Points to the azurefactory folder. The default is ESAF_FOLDER. url Sets the API address. The default is AIFACTORY_API_URL. api_key Carries the API key. The default is AIFACTORY_API_KEY. factory Selects a Factory by key or ID. You need it only when the folder holds more than one.

Over REST, send the key in the X-API-Key header. The API accepts plain HTTP on your own machine only.

docs.title: Naming limits
docs.text:
Azure limits a deployment name to 64 characters, and ESAF builds names from your prefixes.

Rule Why Keep the Factory prefix and the project prefix to six characters or fewer. Longer prefixes can push a deployment name over the limit. Use three digits for a project number and a scale-set suffix, as a string: "002". The tools reject other forms. Use dev, stage or prod for the environment, in lower case. The same number can exist in several environments.

The app checks prefix lengths and warns you before a name is cut.

docs.title: Project metadata and secret names
docs.text:
Setting What it does org-department-id, org-department-name Label a project with its department. They provision nothing. inputCommonSPSecretKey, project_service_principal_Secret_seeding_kv_name Name a Key Vault secret. They hold the secret's name, never its value.

Supply a secret name only when your sign-in method needs one. Saving the name doesn't create the secret.

docs.title: Project settings
docs.text:
Each project's settings live in its variables.json. Change them with scenario 3:

from azurefactory import esaf

esaf.upsert_project("002", "dev", settings={"tag_costcenter": "lab"})

See Quickstart: Add a project for your team and, for the Agent Chat switches, Quickstart: Create your first agent by enabling ESAF Agent Chat.
